SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8039 A
Date 11 7 38

THE CURFEW

THE speculation has been latterly revived as to whether the curfew will be lifted in the near future. By those who are in favor of lifting it, it is contended that inasmuch as the curfew is not being enforced it may as well be abolished. This contention seems to be begging the issue.
The curfew, it may be pointed out, is essentially a temporary measure to maintain peace and order, and its enforcement may be tempered with reason when circumstances permit it. On the other hand those who choose to wander about in the wee hours of the night will be doing so at their own risk, and the municipal police may at any time elect to question them and, if necessary, place them in detention for the night.
The real question to be decided is whether the local conditions have become sufficiently normal to warrant unrestricted personal movements at night. We do not think so. The recent terrorist activities coupled with the reported guerilla warfare in threshold of Shanghai cannot but convince any reasonable person that things are not what they should be. The police has been over-worked of late. The lifting of the curfew will impose on its members an added burden, and that would be most unfair in view of the prevailing circumstances.
If the curfew has inconvenienced those who thrive on night life, that inconvenience has to be endured for the greater good of the greater number.

FILE
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 11 7 38）

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特务科登记室
编号 S. B. D. 8039 A
日期 1938年7月11日

宵禁

最近，关于宵禁是否会在不久的将来解除的猜测再次兴起。支持解除宵禁的人认为，既然宵禁并未得到严格执行，不如干脆废除。这种论点似乎是在回避问题的实质。
需要指出的是，宵禁本质上是一项维持和平与秩序的临时措施，在情况允许时，其执行可以通情达理地加以缓和。另一方面，那些选择在深夜时分四处游荡的人将自行承担风险，巡捕可随时决定对他们进行盘问，并在必要时将他们拘留过夜。
真正需要决定的问题是，当地局势是否已 sufficiently 正常化，足以证明夜间个人自由行动是合理的。我们认为并非如此。最近的恐怖活动，加上据报道在上海周边地区发生的游击战，不能不使任何理智的人相信，事态并不像应有的那样正常。警方最近工作过度。解除宵禁将给警员增加额外负担，鉴于目前的局势，这将是最不公平的。
如果宵禁给那些依靠夜生活谋生的人带来了不便，那么为了大多数人的更大利益，这种不便必须忍受。

归档
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特务科 1938年7月11日）

Opening Of
Hongkew Is
Under Study

Removal Of Barriers
Likely To Benefit
Nippon Traders

JAPANESE SAID
CONSIDERING ISSUE

Parts Of Yangtzepoo
May Remain Closed
During War

Reports that the Japanese authorities in Shanghai are planning to reopen certain sections of the northern and eastern areas of the International Settlement at an early date gained renewed circulation in the city yesterday following the information that high officials of the Nipponese army, navy and Consulate-General have resumed study of the question.

While confirmation was lacking yesterday from official quarters, the impression prevailed in well informed circles that these reports may not be entirely without factual foundation.

S.M.C. Not Notified

The Shanghai Municipal Council, it is understood, has thus far received no information on the subject. No direct negotiations are being carried out at the present time with the Japanese authorities regarding the reopening of the areas or on the subject of S.M.C. control in the districts, it is reported.

However, testifying that normalcy is slowly returning in the northern and eastern areas the Shanghai Municipal Police as well as the members of the other branches of the S.M.C. services are now said to be encountering less interference from the Japanese as compared with several months ago.

Japanese Suffer

The feeling exists today among competent observers that it would be definitely to the benefit to the Japanese community in Hongkew and the Yangtzepoo areas if restrictions on entrance to and residence in those districts could be relaxed.

Many Japanese residents who recently returned to Shanghai after staying in Japan during the first few months of the war have found it increasingly more difficult to make a living from their businesses as a result of the strict regulations limiting entry to the areas, it is said.

Nipponese Lose Trade

One observer expressed his opinion thus: "The Japanese residents in Hongkew cannot expect to make a living by cutting each other's hair or by selling goods only to their own compatriots. The Japanese are stopping up their own trade by excluding non-Nipponese people from the districts."

However, taking into consideration that the Japanese army and navy authorities are using certain sections of Yangtzepoo and Hongkew as a base of operations and a depot, these same sources are aware of the fact that several specific localities in those two districts probably will be never reopened as long as the war lasts.

Reason Not Valid

This consideration nevertheless, is not held as a valid reason for the Nipponese authorities to continue the isolation of the two areas.

Meantime, before entrance and residence restrictions in Hongkew and Yangtzepoo are lifted many questions touching upon the administrative and police problems in the areas remain to be threshed out between the Japanese and the Council. These negotiations, which will seek an understanding on many existing issues, have so far not been launched.

（批：D.S. / Kennedy / Qsx）
pages.zh:
1041

虹口重新开放
正在研究中

移除路障
可能有利于
日本商人

称日本人
正在考虑此问题

杨树浦部分地区
在战争期间
可能保持封闭

继获悉日本陆、海军及总领事馆的高级官员已恢复对该问题进行研究后，有关上海日本当局计划尽早重新开放国际租界北部和东部某些区域的报道，昨日在全市范围内再次流传。

虽然昨日官方方面缺乏证实，但在消息灵通人士中普遍存在一种印象，即这些报道可能并非完全没有事实依据。

未通知工部局

据了解，上海工部局（S.M.C.）迄今为止未收到有关此事的任何信息。据报道，目前并未就重新开放这些区域或工部局在这些地区的控制权问题与日本当局进行直接谈判。

然而，据称，随着北部和东部地区逐渐恢复正常，与几个月前相比，上海公共租界工部局警务处以及工部局其他部门的人员现在受到的日本方面的干扰较少。

日本人受损

当今有能力的观察家认为，如果能够放松进入和居住在这些区域的限制，肯定有利于虹口和杨树浦地区的日本侨民社区。

据说，许多在战争头几个月留在日本、最近才返回上海的日本居民发现，由于严格限制进入这些区域的规定，他们越来越难以通过经商维持生计。

日本人失去贸易

一位观察家这样表达他的观点：“虹口的日本居民不能指望靠互相理发或只向同胞出售商品来维持生计。日本人通过将非日本人排除在这些区域之外，阻碍了自己的贸易。”

然而，考虑到日本陆海军当局正使用杨树浦和虹口的某些部分作为行动基地和仓库，同样的消息来源也意识到，只要战争持续，这两个区内的几个特定地点可能永远不会重新开放。

理由不成立

尽管如此，这一考量并不被视为日本当局继续隔离这两个区域的有效理由。

与此同时，在解除虹口和杨树浦的入境和居住限制之前，还有许多涉及该地区行政和警察方面的问题需要在日本人和工部局之间彻底解决。旨在就许多现有问题达成谅解的这些谈判，迄今尚未启动。

（批：D.S. / Kennedy / Qsx）

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by C. Crawford. A. S

27/6/38

With reference to the attached cutting from the
"Shanghai Times" dated June 24, 1938, I have to state that
a meeting of local Japanese residents, who suffered from
the recent Sino-Japanese hostilities, was held at the
Japanese Club, Boone Road, between 6.30 p.m. and 9.30 p.m.,
June 23, with the object of securing an increase in the
rehabilitation fund which was formerly allotted by the
Japanese Government. The meeting was attended by some
200 persons and was presided over by Mr. Y. Hayashi,
Honorary President of the Federation of the Japanese Street
Unions.

In opening the meeting, one minutes silent prayer

Subject Japanese Plans re Development of Kiangwan and Woosung Areas.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

See also
D 8155 (22-12-38)

Enquiries indicate that the Japanese Military
and Civic Authorities have decided to adopt the plans, with
but very minor alterations, of the former Municipality of
Greater Shanghai regarding the development of the Civic Centre
at Kiangwan and the Woosung areas.

In furthering the plans, it is contemplated
to replace eventually the recently constructed light military
railway with a proper trunk line. The new railway will run
from Nanziang via Tazang and Kiangwan to Jukong Wharf, where
a modern railway terminus will be built. It is understood
that, owing to its proximity to the Settlement, the Shanghai
North Railway will be demolished altogether after the con-
struction of the new railway has been completed.

It is further learned that conservancy work
in the Whampoo River west of the Jukong Wharf will not be
undertaken or at least discouraged with the evident purpose
to making it increasingly difficult for large ocean liners
to proceed to Settlement wharves. On the other hand, con-
servancy work in the section between Woosung and Jukong Wharf
will be undertaken in one or two months time.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE * 24 JUNE 1938 * SPECIAL BRANCH）

查询表明，日本军方和民政当局已决定采用前大上海市政府关于江湾市民中心及吴淞地区开发的规划方案，仅做极微小的修改。

为推进该计划，拟最终用一条正规的干线铁路取代近期修建的轻型军用铁路。新铁路将从南翔经大场和江湾至虬江码头，并将在此处建造一座现代化的铁路终点站。据悉，由于靠近租界，在新铁路建成后，上海北站铁路将被完全拆除。

此外获悉，虬江码头以西黄浦江段的疏浚工程将不会进行，或者至少会受到阻挠，其明显目的是使大型远洋班轮越来越难以驶往租界码头。另一方面，吴淞与虬江码头之间河段的疏浚工程将在一两个月内开展。

S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8039 A
Date 25 6 38

Hungjao Areas
Curfew Revised

Week-End Closure Now
9 P.M.; Residents
Need Passes

Revised curfew regulations in the area west of the Shanghai International Settlement, now under the control of the Japanese military authorities, were announced by a Japanese Embassy spokesman today.
The barriers at the railway crossings will remain open to the general public up to 7 o'clock at night on week-days, until 9 o'clock On Saturdays and Sundays.
Members of the Hungjao Area Association possessing special passes issued by the Japanese garrison headquarters will be allowed passage until 10 o'clock. These passes will be obtainable through Mr. K. M. Cumming, secretary of the Hungjao Area Association, the spokesman said.
After 7 o'clock at night, the only barrier open will be at Great Western Road, he added.
"Those persons who pass by motorcar after 7 p.m. are requested to have a light inside their car. When they approach the sentry line, they are requested to stop and show their special permits to the sentry, who, if need be, may search the interior of the car," the spokesman declared.
The purpose of such a search was to prevent the transportation of firearms and other dangerous goods, the spokesman said, recalling the incident involving a "snipe shooting" party consisting of prominent local residents.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 25 JUNE 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

日本大使馆发言人今日宣布，位于上海公共租界以西、现由日本军事当局控制的地区的修订版宵禁规定。
工作日晚7点前，周六和周日晚9点前，铁路道口的路障将对公众保持开放。
持有日本驻军司令部签发的特别通行证的虹桥地区协会成员，允许通行至晚10点。该发言人称，这些通行证可通过虹桥地区协会秘书K. M. Cumming先生获取。
他补充说，晚7点后，唯一开放的路障位于大西路（Great Western Road）。
“晚上7点后驾车通过的人员，请在车内开灯。当接近哨兵线时，请停车并向哨兵出示特别许可证，如有必要，哨兵可能会搜查车内，”该发言人宣称。
该发言人称，此类搜查的目的是为了防止运输枪支和其他危险物品，并提及了一起涉及当地知名人士组成的“猎鹬射击”聚会的事件。

Subject French Concession Licensed Establishments - Curfew Enforcement.

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. J.

With reference to the contents of the attached newspaper
cuttings and the endorsements appearing thereon, Mr. JOHEZ,
Directeur-Adjoint of the French Police has been interviewed
and he states as follows:

In view of the fact that owners of cabarets, bars, cafes,
etc. are now paying full licence fees for their premises, the
French Police are permitting these establishments to cater to
customers until 5 a.m. daily, providing that persons visiting
the premises concerned are inside prior to 12.30 a.m. and
do not leave during the hours of curfew.

This measure has been put into effect in an effort to
allow owners of these establishments to offset their many
losses during past months. Actually however, except for
week-ends, these premises are not expected to augment their
business, as a check by the French Police reveals that
they are practically not patronized at all during ordinary
week-days, after 12.15 a.m.

ASSISTANCE OF MILITARY.

In cases where assistance is rendered by the
Military to the Police Force, whether by individual members
on their own initiative or by groups under orders from their
respective Commanders, outside normal patrol duties and so
forth, and when this assistance is valuable and indicates
friendly cooperation, it is very necessary that a letter
of thanks should be forwarded to the Commanding Officer of
the unit concerned.

In the case of British Military, such a letter of
thanks will be informal in manner to the G.O.C. Shanghai
Area and a copy to the Commanding Officer of the unit in
question.

In the case of the United States Marine Corps,
Italian Forces and others, the letter will be addressed to
the Colonel in Command of the Unit concerned, and also
informal in terms.

Please keep this in mind, as I think it is a great
asset towards good cooperation if we immediately recognise
assistance rendered and initiative shown both by individuals
and junior Commanders.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 14 JUNE 1938）

CONSULATE GENERAL FOR FRANCE IN SHANGHAI
CONSULAR ORDINANCE

We MARCEL BAUDEZ, CONSUL GENERAL FOR FRANCE in
Shanghai, Chevalier de la Legion d'Honneur,

In accordance with article XIII of the Municipal
Regulations of the French Concession, as promulgated by
Consular Ordinance on April 14th 1868;

In accordance with the Police Regulations promul-
gated and modified by Consular Ordinances No63, of April 18th
1929; No11, of June 30th 1930; No159, of October 11th 1930;
No27, of February 23rd 1931; No53, of February 15th 1936;

Have ordered and do order the following:

Art. 1 - POSSESSION OF WAR MATERIAL PROHIBITED. -
The possession of arms and ammunition is forbidden in the
French Concession, unless a special permit is issued by the
French Police. The cost of this permit is 5 dollars per year.

Art. 2 - NOTIFYING THE POLICE.- Any person now in
possession of, or likely to be in possession of arms and
ammunition (automatic pistols, revolvers, rifles, grenades,
explosives, etc....) will be held responsible for notifying
the French Police to this effect prior to January 1st 1938.

Any person who has knowledge of the existence of
arms or ammunition in the French Concession will be held
responsible for advising the French Police within 24 hours
of the acquisition of this knowledge.

Art. 3 - PENALTIES. - Any person who, from January
1st 1938, is in possession of arms or ammunition without
having made a declaration to this effect, or not having
obtained the permit as mentioned in Art.1 above, will be
liable to be fined from 25 to 1,000 dollars, without
prejudicing any case before the competent court.

Any person proved to have had knowledge of the
existence of arms or ammunition, and not having advised the
Police to this effect in accordance with Art. 11 above, will

CONSULAT GÉNÉRAL DE FRANCE A CHANGHAI
ORDONNANCE CONSULAIRE
Nous Marcel BAUDEZ, Consul Général de France à Changhai, Chevalier
de la Légion d'Honneur,
Vu l'Article XIII du Règlement d'Organisation Municipale de la Con-
cession française de Changhai, mis en vigueur par ordonnance consulaire du
14 avril 1868 ;
Vu le Règlement de police et voirie mis en vigueur et modifié par les
ordonnances consulaires N° 63 du 18 avril 1929 ; N° III, du 30 juin 1930 ;
N° 159, du II octobre 1930 ; N° 27, du 23 février 1931 ; N° 53, du 15
février 1936 ;
Avons arrêté et arrêtons ce qui suit :
ART. I — Interdiction de la détention d'armes de guerre. — La détention
d'armes et de munitions de guerre est interdite sur le territoire de la Concession
française, sans un permis spécial délivré par la Police Française. Le coût de .
ce permis est de 5 dollars par an.
ART. L. — Déclaration. — Toute personne détenant actuellement ou qui
serait amenée à détenir des armes ou des munitions de guerre (pistolets auto-
matiques, révolvers, fusils, grenades, explosifs, etc...) sera tenue d'en faire
la déclaration à la Police française avant le 1er Janvier 1938.
Toute personne qui aura connaissance de l'existence d'un dépôt d'armes
ou de munitions sur la Concession française sera tenue d'en donner avis, dans
les 24 heures, à la Police française.
ART. 3 — Sanctions. — Toute personne qui, à dater du 1er janvier 1938,
détientrait des armes ou des munitions de guerre sans en avoir fait la déclara-
tion et sans avoir obtenu le permis prévu à l'article I ci-dessus sera passible
d'une amende de 25 à 1.000 dollars sans préjudice des poursuites devant les
tribunaux compétents.
Toute personne convaincue d'avoir eu connaissance de l'existence d'un
dépôt d'armes ou de munitions sans en avoir donné avis à la Police, comme il
est prévu à l'article 2 ci-dessus, sera passible d'une amende de 25 à 500 dollars
sans préjudice des poursuites devant les tribunaux compétents.
Les armes détenues irrégulièrement seront confisquées.
ART. 4 — Exécution. — Le Directeur des Services de Police et de Sûreté
est chargé de l'exécution de la présente ordonnance.
Fait à Changhai, en l'Hôtel Consulaire, le dix sept décembre Mil neuf
cent trente sept.
POUR COPIE CERTIFIÉE CONFORME
Changhai, le Décembre 1937.
Le Vice-Consul,
Le Consul Général de France,
Signé : M. BAUDEZ.

我们 Marcel BAUDEZ，法国驻上海总领事，荣誉军团骑士勋章获得者，
鉴于1868年4月14日由领事命令生效的上海法租界市政组织章程第十三条；
鉴于由以下领事命令生效及修订的警务及道路章程：1929年4月18日第63号；1930年6月30日第III号；1930年10月11日第159号；1931年2月23日第27号；1936年2月15日第53号；
裁定如下：
第一条 — 禁止持有军用武器。— 在法租界境内，若无由法国巡捕房颁发的特别许可证，禁止持有武器及军用弹药。该许可证费用为每年5美元。
第二条 — 申报。— 任何目前持有或将会持有武器或军用弹药（自动手枪、左轮手枪、步枪、手榴弹、炸药等）的人，有义务在1938年1月1日前向法国巡捕房申报。
任何知悉法租界内存在武器或弹药存放处的人，有义务在24小时内通知法国巡捕房。
第三条 — 制裁。— 自1938年1月1日起，任何持有武器或军用弹药而未进行申报且未获得上述第一条规定之许可证的人，将被处以25至1,000美元的罚款，且不影响向主管法院提起诉讼。
任何被证实知悉武器或弹药存放处的存在，却未按上述第二条规定通知警方的人，将被处以25至500美元的罚款，且不影响向主管法院提起诉讼。
违规持有的武器将被没收。
第四条 — 执行。— 警务及保安处总监负责执行本命令。
一九三七年十二月十七日于上海领事馆。

Subject (in full) War contributions by local Japanese merchants.

Information has been obtained that the management

on May 26 drew from these three banks a sum of Yen 4,500,000

Date May 28 1938
30 5 38

Subject Reported preparations made to evacuate Hankow.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

According to information received by
ex-government officials here from private sources, the
Hankow Government although holding an optimistic view of
the war situation, is somewhat disturbed at the fall of
Hsuchow, the strategic city on the Lunghai and Tientsin-
Pukow Railways and is preparing to remove all important
documents and to evacuate their offices to Szechuen in
case the Chinese forces are unable to check the Japanese
advance towards Kaifeng from the east and Chengchow from
the north in Honan. However, reinforcements are being
rushed from Szechuen and Hunan to meet the invaders and
the war will be prolonged as far as possible to wear out
Japan.

What worries the Hankow Government most
at present are the exchange fluctuations and the difficulties
of raising loans internally and externally.

Subject Rumoured appointment of General Chin Yun Feng to the
Chairmanship of the Peking Provisional Government.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Rumours have been prevalent in Shanghai that
General Chin Yun Peng (靳雲鵬) who was Minister of War and
later Premier of a former Northern regime, and who has been
living in retirement since 1924, will be appointed Chairman
of the Provisional Government at Peking in succession to
Mr. Wang Keh Ming.

It is stated that Tokyo is dissatisfied with
Wang's administration in the North and that Wang and his
Japanese advisors recently paid a visit to Japan in an
endeavour to save himself from being removed from his
present post.

In the eyes of Japanese politicians General
Chin Yun Peng will make a more satisfactory President of
China when the Peking and Nanking Governments are amalgamated.
Among the Northern politicians and militarists in retirement,
General Chin is next in seniority to General Tsao Kun (once
President of China) whose death took place in Tientsin on
May 17.

制作人及转呈人 警司 Tan Shao Liang

上海流传着一种说法，曾任前北洋政府陆军总长及后来国务总理、自1924年以来一直隐居的靳云鹏将军，将接替王克敏先生出任北京临时政府主席。

据悉，东京方面对王在北方的统治感到不满，王及其日本顾问最近访问日本，试图保住其现有职位不被撤换。

在日本政客眼中，当北京和南京政府合并时，靳云鹏将军将成为更令人满意的中国总统。在隐居的北方政客和军阀中，靳将军的资历仅次于曹锟将军（曾任中国大总统），后者于5月17日在天津去世。

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I

On May 12, the Municipal Police obtained a pamphlet
which sets forth the happenings in the next six months and
which, when translated, is as follows:-

The Words of a French Prophet

June 9 China wins.
June 24 Japan wins a small victory.
June 26 China wins a great victory.
July 26 War breaks out between Japan
and the U.S.S.R.
August 5 Soviet planes bomb Japan.
October 15 Soviet naval, land and air forces
win a great victory.
October 30 Revolution breaks out in Japan.
November 30 Great disturbances in Japan.
End of this
year(1938) China wins the final victory.
ditto Some slight disturbance occurs
in China.

This pamphlet alleges in quoting the French
prophet that he foretold the annexation by Germany of Austria
before it took place and that it would take place on March 11,
and that before April 9 the Chinese forces at Taierchwang
would win a great victory on that day, which actually happened. *

Information has been obtained that certain
individuals have had copies of the pamphlet re-printed for
the purpose of posting same or distributing them to the
public.

A copy of the pamphlet is attached.

由副督察潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）撰写，由督察克劳福德（C. Crawford）转呈。

5月12日，工部局警务处获得一本小册子，其中阐述了未来六个月将发生的事件，翻译如下：

《一位法国预言家的话》

6月9日 中国获胜。
6月24日 日本取得小胜。
6月26日 中国取得大胜。
7月26日 日本与苏联之间爆发战争。
8月5日 苏联飞机轰炸日本。
10月15日 苏联海陆空军取得大胜。
10月30日 日本爆发革命。
11月30日 日本发生大动乱。
今年（1938年）年底 中国取得最终胜利。
同上 中国发生轻微骚乱。

这本小册子在引用这位法国预言家的话时声称，他在德国吞并奥地利之前就预言了此事，并称该事件将于3月11日发生；还称在4月9日之前，中国军队将在台儿庄于当日取得大胜，而这一情况确实发生了。*

已获情报，某些个人已重印该小册子，目的是将其张贴或向公众分发。

SECRET
REPORT

Subject Possible Outbreak of Disturbances in the French Concession.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

As a result of enquiries made on the attached
report of a possible Japanese uprising, it has been learned,
that such an uprising is not expected at present. In view,
however, of the rather strained relations existing between the
French Police and the Japanese Military Authorities owing to
restricting the free passage of Japanese troops, the likelihood
of staging some sort of civilian disturbance in the French
Concession by Chinese elements under Japanese instigation or
some similar action is quite within the range of probability,
should there be no compromise on the issues involved.

The French Authorities are reported to be divided
in their opinion as to what should be done to face the
Japanese demands. Some officers in the French Police
maintain the opinion that under the present circumstances,
the only and best way would be to yield to Japanese as far as
possible so as to save the Concession from possible Japanese
reprisals. Others, and they form the majority, refuse to
yield and are uncompromising in their stand.

E. Papp
Inspector

THE CHINA PRESS.
17 APR 1938
897

Open Door Slammed In
Tsingtao, Say Foreign
Shipping Firms Here

Through Passengers Unable To Land; Cargo
Manifests Must Be Submitted To Japanese
Naval Authorities Before Vessels Sail

Tsingtao, one of China's open doors, was slammed shut last week by Japanese naval and military authorities. This information seeped through to Shanghai yesterday with vessels returning from the north carrying reports that they had been unable to land through-passengers at Tsingtao and, in fact, had experienced great difficulty in obtaining permission for their officials to land in order to visit branch offices.

"We are experiencing the utmost difficulty in carrying out our service," one of the heads of a well-known foreign China coast steamship company said yesterday. "Before we can convey cargo to Tsingtao, we have to submit a copy of our manifests to the Japanese naval authorities—not that we blame them, since we understand that they are busy landing forces and supplies there for the purpose of delivering a new offensive from that area.

"In addition to the onerous rules imposed on consignments of cargo to the port of Tsingtao by the Japanese authorities, we are still denied the use of wharves, which puts the cost of our transport up by a considerable percentage.

"Publicly And Privately"

"So far we have managed to avoid trouble with the Japanese authorities, but only by adhering strictly to the rules they have announced publicly and privately. These rules would not be greatly oppressive were it not for the restrictions imposed on navigation, freedom of passengers and lack of wharfage facilities.

"Lack of wharfage facilities has been a severe handicap to our trade in Tsingtao, since all cargo consigned to that port must be landed on the beach by lighters, and there inspected by Japanese officials. This handicap is the greater because our agents have observed that Japanese merchant vessels, whether under Government charter or not, are drawing alongside to unload. We understand that the majority of these vessels are not under Japanese Government charter, and therefore are operating, so far as we are concerned, in unfair competition.

Officials Insulted

"There have been occasions when our officials have been refused permission to land in order to visit our Tsingtao offices, and no reason has been given for the refusal. The Japanese authorities well know that we have observed the rules of neutrality since the blockade was established, and we feel that the restrictions placed on our trade in Tsingtao is a deliberate slamming of what we have been assured would be preserved as an open door.

"Last week we were obliged to refuse permission to passengers to go ashore owing to restriction placed on civilian movements. A woman passenger traveling through to Shanghai was unable to land to inspect property which she bought last spring and intended to occupy this summer. Other passengers have been prevented from landing to visit their shops and agencies. Either the Japanese authorities intend to use Tsingtao as a military base of operations, or the Japanese financial powers intend to close the port to foreign trade by a process of 'peaceful prevention.'"

Confirmation on the virtual closure of Tsingtao to "free" foreign trade was obtained from the representative of another shipping company. "We have placed the facts before the British Consular authorities," he said, "and that is as far as we can go at present. I believe the British and Japanese authorities are negotiating towards an amicable agreement on the subject."

S!

1938年4月17日
897

在沪外籍航运公司称：
青岛“门户开放”政策被强行关闭

过境乘客无法登陆；船舶离港前须向日本海军当局提交货物舱单

上周，日本海军和军事当局将中国门户之一的青岛强行关闭。这一消息于昨日传至上海，从北方返回的船只带来报告称，它们无法让过境乘客在青岛登陆，事实上，其职员为访问分支机构而申请登陆许可时也遭遇了极大困难。

昨日，一家知名外籍在华沿海轮船公司的负责人之一表示：“我们在开展业务时正面临极大的困难。在向青岛运送货物之前，我们必须向日本海军当局提交一份舱单副本——这并不是我们要责怪他们，因为我们理解他们正忙于在该地区登陆部队和物资，以便从该区域发动新的攻势。

除了日本当局对运往青岛港的货物施加的繁重规定外，我们仍被拒绝使用码头，这使我们的运输成本大幅上升。

‘公开与私下’

“到目前为止，我们设法避免了与日本当局的麻烦，但这仅仅是通过严格遵守他们公开和私下宣布的规定才得以实现。如果不是因为对航行、乘客自由以及码头设施的限制，这些规定本不会过于苛刻。

“缺乏码头设施严重阻碍了我们在青岛的贸易，因为所有运往该港口的货物都必须由驳船卸在海滩上，并接受日本官员的检查。这种障碍尤为严重，因为我们的代理人观察到，日本商船，无论是否受日本政府包租，都在靠岸卸货。我们了解到，这些船只中的大多数并未受日本政府包租，因此就我们而言，它们是在进行不公平竞争。

官员受辱

“曾有多次，我们的官员为访问我们在青岛的办事处而申请登陆时被拒绝，且未给出任何理由。日本当局很清楚，自封锁建立以来，我们一直遵守中立规则，我们认为，对我们在青岛贸易施加的限制，是故意关闭那扇曾被保证将保持开放的门户。

“上周，由于对平民行动施加了限制，我们不得不拒绝乘客上岸。一名途经上海的女乘客无法登陆去查看她去年春天购买并打算今年夏天入住的房产。其他乘客也被阻止登陆去拜访他们的商店和代理机构。日本当局要么打算将青岛用作军事行动基地，要么日本金融势力打算通过‘和平预防’的过程关闭港口，阻止对外贸易。”

另一家航运公司的代表证实了青岛对“自由”对外贸易实际已关闭的情况。“我们已将事实提交给英国领事当局，”他说，“目前我们只能做到这一步。我相信英国和日本当局正在就此问题进行谈判，以达成友好协议。”

S!
A.S.J. Roger 4月17日

Subject Reported massacre of nine missionaries - by Japanese Military.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

It has been learned that nine foreign missionaries have been murdered by Japanese soldiers in Chengting, Hopeh, during November, 1937 following the occupation of the city by the Japanese Forces. The murdered priests included Bishop Schraven, six other priests and two laymen, most of whom were of French and Belgian and of Polish (one) nationality.

According to the report, the Japanese Command took under protection the Mission and pasted scrolls to this effect outside the building. Despite this fact, however, unruly Japanese soldiers tore down the permits and shot all inmates, who were just having their meals, without mercy to death.

It has been learned that this dastardly deed is not denied by the Japanese Military Command, who are now conducting negotiations with the foreign consulates for the settlement of the matter. They are said to have offered $300,000 to the French Government in the settlement of this affair.

事由 据报九名传教士遭日军屠杀。

制作及转呈人 Papp 巡官。

据悉，1937年11月，在日军占领河北省正定城后，九名外籍传教士被日本士兵杀害。遇害的神职人员包括 Schraven 主教、另外六名神父和两名平信徒，其中大多数为法国、比利时国籍，另有一人为波兰国籍。

据报道，日军司令部对该传教团采取了保护措施，并在建筑物外张贴了以此为目的的告示。然而，尽管如此，不法日本士兵撕毁了许可证，无情地枪杀了所有正在用餐的住户。

据悉，日本军事司令部并未否认这一卑鄙行径，目前正与各外国领事馆进行谈判以解决此事。据说他们已向法国政府提供30万美元以解决此事件。

Information from a reliable source indicates that since the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai members of the Special Service Section of the Japanese Army have been endeavouring to locate the agents or representatives of General Li Chung Jen or Pei Tsung Hsi in Shanghai with the object of bringing about a separate peace with the Kwangsi leaders. SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. REGISTRY 8039 A
C.S.6, Special Branch. Mar. 4 38
REPORT
Date March 26, 1938.

Subject Present Japanese expectations to end the war.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp

According to information received, the Japanese
Government and Army are most anxious to bring the war to an
early termination and for this reason the closest attention
is being given to the developments in the Chinese political
world.

According to one thought of opinion, it is hoped
that present relations existing between the Chinese Communist
Party and General Chiang Kai Shek will gradually deteriorate
to such a degree that one day they must reach the breaking
point. Some observers claim to see already manifestations
of such a tendency and are of the opinion that this develop-
ment would force General Chiang Kai Shek to break away from
his Communist affiliations and even stand up against them.
That such an eventuality is within the range of possibility
is indicated by the report that General Chiang Kai Shek
keeps in reserve five of his best trained divisions, who
have not yet seen active service. It is agreed that the
materialization of such an eventuality at present is beyond
the dreams even of the greatest optimists, as it would force
General Chiang Kai Shek to accept all Japanese demands un-
conditionally whereas it is realized that China has not yet
been beaten. On the other hand, in case General Chiang
Kai Shek should also be willing, the Japanese Government
and Army would be ready to come to terms with General Chiang
Kai Shek and to assist him in the establishment of a New
Chinese Government at Nanking. By this strategy, it is
hoped to placate the Chinese people as it would bring back
their idol, General Chiang Kai Shek, as the head of a new
government.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 26 MAR. 1938）

根据收到的消息，日本政府和军队迫切希望尽早结束战争，为此，他们正密切关注中国政界的动态。

有一种观点认为，人们希望中国共产党与蒋介石将军之间现有的关系会逐渐恶化，直至有一天达到破裂点。一些观察家声称已经看到了这种倾向的迹象，并认为这一发展将迫使蒋介石将军脱离与共产党的联系，甚至与之对抗。有报告称，蒋介石将军保留了五个训练有素、尚未投入实战的精锐师，这表明此类可能性存在。大家一致认为，目前实现这种可能性即使是最乐观的人也难以想象，因为这将迫使蒋介石将军无条件接受日本的所有要求，而众所周知中国尚未被击败。另一方面，如果蒋介石将军也愿意，日本政府和军队准备与蒋将军达成协议，并协助他在南京建立一个新的中国政府。通过这一策略，希望能安抚中国人民，因为这将使他们心目中的偶像蒋介石将军作为新政府的元首回归。

The information contained in the attached report
is misleading in some parts and far from the truth and may have
been based on gossip amongst people who do not appear to be in
touch with the political situation. The most misleading point
is the allegation that General Chiang Kai Shek is willing to
recognize Manchukuo and to join the Japan-Manchukuo anti-
Communistic Group. If peace negotiations are conducted on such
a basis, Chiang will not only lose the support and cooperation
of the communists and of the Kwangsi Party but will quickly
lose his position and power.

Lo Chia Heng, lawyer, has never been and will never
be entrusted by the Hankow Government to make peace.

Tang Shao Yi is a veteran Southern political leader
but he is not a member of the Kuomintang and therefore is not

2 3 38

Condition of the Western District

During the weekend February 26 and 27, U.S.I.
Laurier, D.S. Larby and D.S. McKeown traversed the
western district as far as the village of Siau Kyung
Kaung towards Tsoo Ka Za both by road and across country
on foot. The whole area is littered with live hand
grenades, cartridges and shells, especially in the
fields forming a dangerous hazard not to pedestrians but
to cross country riders. At one point a missile,
presumably a hand grenade, was heard to explode at a point
one hundred yards distant. Unexploded shells of as high
a calibre as 9" were observed. On Hungjao Road
approximately 300 yards East of the Blind School is a
wrecked limber containing two live shells. This limber
is actually on the roadway and may prove disastrous to
the occupants of a swerving or skidding motorcar. In
the ditch between the limber and the Blind School may be
observed a number of hand grenades. In many cases the
hand grenades are well preserved in pouches. Numerous
foreign schoolboys were seen on the roads hunting for
souvenirs. The party encountered no difficulties
from the Japanese soldiers, who appear to be confined
to the roads for the most part, only two or three being
seen in the actual countryside.

Parts of dead bodies were seen particularly in the
creeks and in the water near Chinese defence works. The
wonk dogs (in large numbers) encountered differed from
those seen in normal times being sleek and well fed and
less timid. Although the animals were not vicious,
their attitude may change following the clearance of
the corpses when they again become hungry.

西区状况

在2月26日和27日的周末期间，美国籍警员 Laurier、侦探警佐 Larby 和侦探警佐 McKeown 通过公路和徒步穿越乡野，巡视了西区直至靠近曹家宅的小泾港村。整个地区散落着未爆炸的手榴弹、子弹和炮弹，尤其是在田野里，这对越野骑行者而非行人构成了危险隐患。在某处，听到一枚疑似手榴弹的抛射物在一百码外爆炸。观察到口径高达9英寸的未爆炮弹。在虹桥路盲童学校以东约300码处，有一辆损毁的弹药车，里面装有两枚实弹炮弹。这辆弹药车实际上就在路面上，可能会对急转弯或打滑的汽车乘员造成灾难性后果。在弹药车和盲童学校之间的沟渠中，可以看到许多手榴弹。在许多情况下，手榴弹完好地保存在袋子里。看到许多外国男学生在路上寻找纪念品。巡逻队没有遇到日本士兵的阻碍，他们似乎大多局限于道路上，在实际的乡野间只看到两三个人。

特别是在溪流中和中国防御工事附近的水中，看到了尸体残骸。遇到的野狗（数量众多）与平时见到的不同，它们毛色光亮、喂养良好且不那么胆小。虽然这些动物并不凶恶，但在尸体被清理后，当它们再次挨饿时，态度可能会改变。

30/12/37

Subject Exodus of Chinese Residents from Zi-ka-wei and vicinity.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

（批：d.g. / 24/12）
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / 24 DEC. 1937 / (DIVISION)）

After the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Nantao
and district, the protection of property at Zi-ka-wei and
its vicinity, O.O.L. was taken over by the French military
forces. At noon, December 20, rumours were rife to the
effect that the Japanese would take over the control of
the area to the west of Zi-ka-wei. The apprehension of
the populace was increased when the Chinese policemen
numbering forty, who formerly belonged to the Shanghai
City Government Bureau of Police, but later were employed
by the French authorities to maintain peace and order at
Zi-ka-wei, were paid salaries for the half month of
December, and discharged. An exodus of the residents
into the French Concession followed. The French authorities
closed the barricades erected at the entrances of Avenue
Petain and Route Picard Destelan, bordering on Chinese
controlled territory. On December 21, the barricades were
opened to allow the entry of residents into the Concession.

（批：CP / 24/12）
（批：DC(Div)）

It is reported that the Japanese have notified the
French Consul-General of their intention to take over Hu-ka-
zah (胡家宅) and Tang-tse-king (塘子涇) Villages in
the Hungjao area and that the French authorities agreed to the
Japanese request and withdrew French soldiers as from December
21. To-shan-wan (土山湾), another village in the neighbourhood of
Zi-ka-wei, is still, however, being patrolled by members of
the French Police.

（印：M3 / 23 DEC 1937 / SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

在中国军队从南市及其周边地区撤退后，徐家汇及其附近区域（越界筑路区）的财产保护工作由法国军队接管。12月20日中午，谣言四起，称日本人将接管徐家汇以西地区的控制权。当四十名原属上海市政府警察局、后被法国当局雇用以维持徐家汇治安的中国警察领取了12月上半月的薪水并被解雇时，民众的恐慌情绪加剧。随后，居民纷纷逃入法租界。法国当局关闭了位于爱多亚路（Avenue Petain）和毕勋路（Route Picard Destelan）入口处、与中国控制区接壤的路障。12月21日，路障开放，允许居民进入租界。

（批注：CP / 12月24日）

December 25, 1937.

The following revised regulations have been announced by the 8039A
Headquarters of the Settlement Area Garrison Forces and will
take effect as from December 25, 1937.

GENERAL MATTERS

(1) Modification of Regulations regarding Control of Lights.

Lights in Open Air.

Following the procedure now in force regarding the control
of street lamps, all lights located outside premises shall
have shades affixed so that the ray be directed towards the
ground.

Inside Premises.

All lights installed within premises shall have suitable
shades affixed so that the direct ray from the lights may
not be visible from outside. In the event of air-raids
strict control of lights shall be exercised by all concerned
and it is recommended that every one will be prepared for
any such eventuality.

(2) Servants.

Provided that a valid pass and armed band are carried by
in accordance with the regulations at present in force,
henceforth Chinese servants in the employ of Japanese or
Foreigners will be permitted to pass through the barrier at
the Garden Bridge unaccompanied by their employers.

(3) Foreigners.

Foreigners are now permitted to live, remove articles from
or pass through Hongkew Area and Yangtszepoo District (North-
east of Tinghai Road excluded) and as from 25-12-37, similar
privileges shall be extended to Extension Roads in northern
area which will be thrown open forthwith.
The procedure at present in force shall apply to those pro-
ceeding to the newly opened area.

(4) Free access to Hongkew, Yangtszepoo and Extension Roads in
northern district through the Garden Bridge shall be permitted
without restrictions regarding permits. These visits, however,
shall be confined only to during day light.
Chauffeurs employed by such foreigners shall be granted
similar privileges when driving their masters into the area.
Those wishing to visit the area during the night or remove
property shall have to apply for permits in accordance with
the procedure at present in force.

一般事项

(1) 关于灯光管制的规章修改。

室外灯光。

遵循目前关于路灯管制的程序，所有位于建筑物外部的灯光必须加装灯罩，使光线射向地面。

(2) 仆役。

只要按照现行规定持有有效通行证并佩戴臂章，此后受雇于日本人或外国人的中国仆役将被允许在无雇主陪同的情况下通过外白渡桥的检查站。

The following revised regulations were announced by the Headquarters
of the Settlement Area Garrisoned by Japanese Forces.

(1) Permission for admission, habitation or business for
foreigners.

With the exception of certain areas reserved for military
purposes, foreigners will be permitted the freedom of
admission, habitation or business in the area lying north
of the Soochow Creek, irrespective of the Settlement or
Chinese territory, as from 27-12-37.
Sentries will be posted outside the area confined to
military use.
Curfew will be enforced between 11.30 p.m. and 5 a.m.
but free movement will be permitted those who are on
urgent official duty.

(2) Removal of Property.

Removal of property, without permits, will be permitted
to foreigners provided that such removal is confined to
warehouses, factories, etc., owned by foreigners. Escort
will be provided for the party at the Garden Bridge.
No foreigner will be allowed to remove property or goods
from Chinese owned warehouses, factories, etc.

(3) Control of lights.

(a) Lights installed outside or those in premises from
the first floor upwards shall have suitable shades affix-
ed so that the direct ray thrown by the light may not be
visible from the sky.
(b) Other lights in the premises may be lit as usual,
but arrangements must be made so that in the event of
an air-raid the light can be at once obscured.
(c) Hereafter no restrictions will be put on motor
vehicle head-lights, however, in the event of an air-
raid the light must be extinguished and speed reduced.

(4) The foregoing regulations will take effect as from
December 27, 1937.

以下修订后的规章已由日军驻防租界区司令部公布。

(1) 外国人入境、居住或经商许可。

除保留用于军事目的的特定区域外，自1937年12月27日起，无论属于租界还是中国领土，苏州河以北区域将允许外国人自由入境、居住或经商。
在限定为军事使用的区域外部将部署哨兵。
宵禁将在晚上11:30至凌晨5:00之间执行，但执行紧急公务者允许自由行动。

(2) 财产搬运。

如果搬运仅限于外国人拥有的仓库、工厂等处的财产，则允许外国人在无许可证的情况下搬运财产。外白渡桥将为该团体提供护送。
任何外国人均不得从中国拥有的仓库、工厂等处搬运财产或货物。

(3) 灯光管制。

(a) 安装在室外或建筑物一楼及以上的灯光，必须加装合适的灯罩，以便从空中看不到灯光的直接射线。
(b) 建筑物内的其他灯光可以照常点亮，但必须做出安排，以便在发生空袭时能立即遮蔽灯光。
(c) 此后，机动车前大灯将不受限制，但是，如遇空袭，必须熄灭灯光并降低车速。

Revised Regulations Governing Employment
of Chinese Servants by Foreigners.

(1) Those wishing to engage servants should proceed to the
Municipal Police Station of the district concerned and the
officer on charge-room duty will investigate the antecedents
character, etc., of the proposed employee.

accompany his employee to the Japanese Consulate-General.

Subject Tung Wen College - Japanese institution.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Fih Forwarded by C. Gansford. W.I

The Tung Wen College, a Japanese institution situated
at 100 and 101 Hungjao Road, O.O.L. was partially destroyed
during hostilities and since the withdrawal of the Chinese
forces the duty of protecting the college has been undertaken
by the French authorities. In the afternoon of December 16,
a party of Japanese military in three motor trucks called at
the institution and requested the French authorities to hand
the college over to them. The Japanese alleged that cases
of theft had occurred and desired that the school be guarded
by them. The French authorities consented to this request,
and the Japanese Military have stationed six soldiers in the
College as from December 17.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

Proclamation

The appended proclamation has been approved by the Shanghai Municipal Council. Copies have been printed in English and Chinese and will be posted throughout the Settlement today, December 16:—
In pursuance of Bye-Laws 35 and 37 annexed to the Land Regulations and Proclamation dated August 17, 1937, the Council for the Foreign Settlement of Shanghai hereby makes further proclamation for the maintenance of peace, order and good government of the Settlement.
1. All persons, except those exempted by Bye-Law 37, who are now in possession of arms or war munitions such as:—automatic pistols, revolvers, rifles, grenades, explosives etc., are required to declare same to the Shanghai Municipal Police on or before January 1, 1938. All persons who have knowledge of the existence of any such arms or munitions within the Settlement are required to furnish the information to the Municipal Police.
2. PENALTIES :
All persons who as from January 1, 1938, fail to declare arms or munitions as stipulated above are, under Bye-Laws 35 and 37, liable to a fine not exceeding $300.00 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding three months or to any other such penalty as shall be prescribed by any other law to which such persons may be amenable.
3. Persons already in possession of Police firearm permits are reminded that such permits unless renewed on or before that date will become invalid after December 31, 1937.
Unwanted firearms, explosives, etc., may be surrendered to any police station for destruction free of charge.

No November 11, 1937, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce,
470 Hankow Road, despatched two circular notices to various
trade associations in Shanghai. One notice refers to a
confidential order received from the local Tangpu and the
Bureau of Social Affairs, instructing public bodies to
continue their activities in assisting the war of resistance,

other contains an order from the Bureau of Public Utilities,
instructing the owners of vehicles commandeered by the
Chinese military, to warn their respective chauffeurs not
to disclose anything they learned in the war areas. The
order intimates that failure to comply will lead to their
arrest and punishment by the authorities.

Subject....Communication between Shanghai and Yangtse River Ports -
alternate commercial routes.

Made by D.S.....Henchman.......................Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

In view of the fact that the flow of commerce between
Shanghai and the Yangtse ports has been seriously hampered
by the construction of a boom across the Yangtse River at
Kiangyin, it may be of interest to give details of alternate
routes whereby merchandise could be carried to ports above
Kiangyin and from the river ports to Shanghai.

The following information, which may be taken as being
reliable, was obtained from a member of the outport staff of
one of the local shipping companies. As representative of
his firm he was sent to investigate by personal test the
practicability of utilizing creeks and other inland waterways
to circumvent the boom at Kiangyin.

Three routes, with an extension of one which may make a
fourth, are suggested:-

(1) Shanghai to Minghong via Whangpoo River, thence by the
creeks to Taihu Lake, after crossing which the Grand Canal
would be utilized as far as Chinkiang which is on the
Yangtse River and above the boom. (Transshipment from
river-boat to junk at Minghong and Chinkiang)

(2) Shanghai via Whangpoo River to Woosung; Woosung to
Luchingkong on the north bank of the Yangtse and below the
boom. From Luchingkong by creek via Tungchow-Tangkiachia-
Jukao-Haian-Kiangyen-Taihsien, to Kowan on the north bank
of the Yangtse. Extension: Above route as far as Taihsien
and from thence by creek to Siennumiao. (Transshipment
at Luchingkong and at Kowan or Siennuniao.)

(3) Shanghai to Woosung via Whangpoo. From Woosung down the
Yangtse estuary to the mouth of the river and from thence
- north along the coast to Tunghai. From Tunghai inland

主题....上海与长江各港口之间的通讯 -
替代商业路线。

由特别巡捕（D.S.）.....Henchman.......................呈报 C. Crawford. 督察长（D.I.）。

鉴于江阴处长江上设置的封锁线已严重阻碍了上海与长江各港口之间的商业流通，兹提供替代路线的详情，以便将货物运往江阴以上的港口，以及从沿江港口运往上海，此举或许具有参考价值。

以下信息取自本地一家轮船公司外埠办事处的一名职员，可视为可靠。该员作为其公司的代表，奉命通过实地测试，调查利用河汊及其他内河水道以绕过江阴封锁线的可行性。

建议三条路线，其中一条的延伸部分可构成第四条：-

(1) 上海经黄浦江至闵行，随后经由河汊至太湖，穿越太湖后利用大运河直至镇江，镇江位于长江上且在封锁线之上。（在闵行和镇江从轮船驳运至民船）

(2) 上海经黄浦江至吴淞；从吴淞至长江北岸、封锁线之下的鹿颈港。从鹿颈港经河汊，途经通州-唐家闸-掘港-海安-姜堰-泰县，至长江北岸的口岸。延伸段：上述路线至泰县，此后经河汊至仙娘庙。（在鹿颈港以及在口岸或仙娘庙进行驳运。）

(3) 上海经黄浦江至吴淞。从吴淞沿长江口下行至入海口，然后- 向北沿海岸至东海。从东海向内陆

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

It is reported that since the outbreak of Sino-
Japanese hostilities in Shanghai, Mr. Chow Ziang Sun, proprietor
of the Johnson's Garage, Peking Road, has, through some arrange-
ments offered for use by the Police Bureau and Garrison
Commander's Office about 60 cars for transportation purposes.
This was probably due to certain privileges having previously
been given to this garage by Chinese Authorities at the
Railway Station and the Civic Centre.
On October 5, the Police Bureau applied for and
obtained 19 S.M.C. private car licences for Johnson's cars
which are being used by them and on October 8 three additional
licences. The numbers are : 1057, 1085, 1170, 1421, 1573,
1606, 1621, 1670, 1675, 1721, 5303, 5339, 5434, 5579, 5704,
5987, 8005, 8025, 8180, 3647, 3703 and 9153.
With the return of Johnson's own licences to the
Council for reserve, the Revenue Office has thus received a cut
in the licence fees collected, the rate for private car licence
being about one-third of the charges for hire cars.
Of the above numbers, No. 9153 is licensed in the
name of the Miscellaneous Affairs Section of the 1st Dept.,
the 21 others in the name of the Transport Office of the Bureau.

MESSAGES ON SINO-JAPANESE SITUATION
FROM 8 AM TO 12 NOON 24/9/37.

8.25 am. From P.A.(Divs). It is believed that cows belonging to a herd left unattended at Woosung are being brought into the Settlement by refugees and others. Any seen having numbered metal clips in the ears marked 'S.D.F.' are to be detained and Headquarters informed.
(Circulated).

9.00 am. From Lookout Watch. During the past hour occasional shelling in Paoshan Road area.

10.00 am. From Lookout Watch. There are several fires in the vicinity of the Far Eastern Race Course. During the past hour heavy shelling in the vicinity of the Commercial Press, Paoshan Road. During the past hour there has been considerable movement in an easterly direction in Pootung. The parties are moving in groups and it cannot be ascertained whether they are troops or not.
There are two Japanese transports now proceeding upstream.

10.35 am. From W.H. At about 10.00 a.m. today a large calibre shell landed in the Kwei Zung Li Alleyway Haining Road and exploded. No casualties.
(Circulated).

11.00 am. From Lookout Watch. There are three separate fires in the vicinity of Woosung and Jukong Roads. Occasional bursts of machine gun fire from Pootung Point.
Another Japanese transport has arrived and the "Ikuta Maru" has departed.
The following is the location of Japanese transports now lying in the river:-
One at the China Merchants Lower Wharf,
One at the N.Y.K. Wayside Wharf,
Four at the O.S.K. Wayside Wharf and
Three at the Jukong Wharf.

12.00 md. From Lookout Watch. Another Japanese freighter is coming upstream.

从上午8时至中午12时 1937年9月24日。

上午8.25。来自 P.A.(Divs)。据信，留在吴淞无人看管的一群牛中的奶牛正被难民及其他人员带入租界。凡被发现耳部带有标有“S.D.F.”字样的编号金属夹者，应予扣留并通知总部。
（传阅）。

上午9.00。来自瞭望哨。过去一小时内，宝山路地区偶有炮击。

上午10.00。来自瞭望哨。远东跑马厅附近有多处火灾。过去一小时内，宝山路商务印书馆附近遭受猛烈炮击。过去一小时内，浦东方面有大量人员向东移动。这些人成群结队移动，无法确定他们是否为军队。
现有两艘日本运输船正溯江而上。

上午10.35。来自 W.H.。今天上午约10.00时，一枚大口径炮弹落在海宁路桂宗里弄堂内并爆炸。无伤亡。
（传阅）。

上午11.00。来自瞭望哨。吴淞路和掘港路附近有三处独立的火灾。浦东角方向偶有机枪扫射声。
另一艘日本运输船已抵达，“生田丸”（Ikuta Maru）已离开。
以下是目前停泊在江面上的日本运输船的位置：-
一艘在招商局下栈码头，
一艘在日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）路边码头，
四艘在大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）路边码头，以及
三艘在掘港码头。

中午12.00。来自瞭望哨。另一艘日本货轮正溯江而上。

防空法
AIR DEFENCE LAW
(Promulgated by the National Government
on August 19, 1937)
8039A
29 9 37

Article 1. This Law is specially enacted with a
view to defending the safety of the nation and to
protecting the lives and property of the people against
air raids by hostile crafts and to mitigating dangers
thereby created.

Article 2. Matters relating to national air defence
shall be undertaken by the highest military authorities.
Where any matter is connected with the various Yuans,
Ministries, Commissions, Boards or the local authorities,
the respective offices shall assist in its execution.

Article 3. (I) During air defence, all citizens
of the Chinese Republic shall be under the obligation
to render service and to supply materials.
(II) During the time of war or emergency,
all citizens, private planes and navigable vessels shall
be under the obligation to watch the movements of hostile
crafts or other crafts in sympathy with the hostile
nation and report same to the nearest military, police
or air-defence organs.

Article 4. Foreigners or persons without nationality
who have residence, domicile, or property in Chinese
territory, as well as juristic persons, organizations
and corporate body who have offices or property in
Chinese territory shall be under the obligation to
help air defence, provided that such obligation shall
not be in conflict with the Treaties and International
Law.
pages.zh:
防空法
AIR DEFENCE LAW
（由国民政府
于1937年8月19日公布）
8039A
29 9 37

第一条 本法专为防御国家安全，保护人民生命财产免受敌机空袭，并减轻由此造成的危险而制定。

第二条 国家防空事项由最高军事机关办理。凡涉及各院、部、会、署或地方当局的事项，各该机关应协助执行。

第三条 （一）在防空期间，中华民国全体公民均有服役及供应物资的义务。
（二）在战时或紧急状态下，全体公民、私人飞机及可航行船只均有义务监视敌机或与敌国同情之其他飞机的动向，并向最近的军事、警察或防空机关报告。

第四条 在中国领土内有住所、居所或财产的外国人或无国籍人，以及在中国领土内设有办事处或拥有财产的法人、组织和社团，均有协助防空的义务，但此项义务不得与条约及国际法相冲突。

pages.en:
-2-
Article 5. During air defence, persons under any
one of the following circumstances may be exempted
from service:-
(1) Being a cripple;
(2) Suffering from mental diseases;
(3) Unfit for service due to age or physical
condition;
(4) When discharging a public function or
serving in active military service the
duty of which cannot be interrupted.
Article 6. For the following acts, permission
shall be obtained from the National Government, or
the highest military authorities or any organ designated
by them:-
(1) Trading in materials or instruments for
air defence;
(2) Issuing or distributing printed matters
relating to air defence;
(3) Showing air defence pictures;
(4) Holding air defence exhibitions.
Article 7. During the time of war or emergency,
for the transmission of information or the sounding
of alarms, the authorities may enjoy priority in the
use of government, public or private communication
apparatus or may improve or modify same.
Article 8. Whenever it is deemed necessary for the
purpose of air defence, the various local air defence
organs shall petition the local military authorities
for permission to exercise the following powers or work
in conjunction with them, provided that permission shall
be obtained from the National Government or the highest
military authorities for the exercise of the powers
specified in sub-sections (6) and (7):-
pages.zh:
-2-
第五条 在防空期间，有下列情形之一者，可免除服役：-
(1) 残疾者；
(2) 患有精神疾病者；
(3) 因年龄或身体状况不适合服役者；
(4) 在执行公务或服现役且职责不可中断时。
第六条 下列行为须取得国民政府、最高军事机关或其指定机关的许可：-
(1) 买卖防空器材或仪器；
(2) 发行或分发有关防空的印刷品；
(3) 放映防空影片；
(4) 举办防空展览。
第七条 在战时或紧急状态下，为传递信息或发出警报，当局可优先使用政府、公共或私人的通信设备，或对其进行改进或修改。
第八条 凡认为出于防空目的有必要时，各地防空机关应请求当地军事机关许可，行使下列权力或与其协同工作，但行使第(6)和(7)款规定的权力须取得国民政府或最高军事机关的许可：-

pages.en:
-5-

(1) To order people to participate in the work
or preparations for air defence;
||(2) To utilise hospitals and clinics established
by the people or foreign nationals in the
locality for air defence purposes;
(3) To requisition or expropriate according to law
land or structures belonging to the people;
(4) To renovate or enlarge the whole or a part
of the street or residential buildings;
(5) To order the people for or restrict from
removing;
(6) To prohibit or restrict the flying of civil
aviation planes;
(7) To levy surcharges for air defence purposes;
| (8) To exact information or conduct searches
when it is necessary to investigate regarding
air defence.

Article 9. Whoever violates the provisions of
Articles 3, 4 and 6 of this Law shall be punished with
detention for not more than thirty days or a fine of
not more than one hundred yuans. Whoever instigates
another person to violate the provisions of these
Articles shall be punished twice as severe.

Article 10. Whoever discloses air defence secrets,
or destroys defence preparations, thereby hampering
defence work or creating danger, shall be dealt with
according to the provisions in the Military Criminal
Code or the Law for the Protection of Military Secrets.

Article 11. The expenses required for preparing or
operating air defence shall be paid by the Central or
local authorities respectively according to the nature
and actual circumstances.

Article 12. Losses incurred by the people when their
land or structures are requisitioned for air defence purposes
shall be compensated by the local government in accordance
with the law.
pages.zh:
-5-

(1) 命令民众参与防空工作或准备；
||(2) 利用当地民众或外国人设立的医院和诊所用于防空目的；
(3) 依法征用或征收民众所有的土地或建筑物；
(4) 改建或扩建街道或住宅建筑物的全部或部分；
(5) 命令民众迁移或限制其迁移；
(6) 禁止或限制民用飞机飞行；
(7) 征收防空附加费；
| (8) 在调查防空相关事宜必要时，索取信息或进行搜索。

第九条 凡违反本法第三条、第四条和第六条规定者，处三十日以下拘留或一百元以下罚款。凡教唆他人违反这些条款规定者，加倍处罚。

第十条 凡泄露防空秘密，或破坏防御设施，从而妨碍防御工作或造成危险者，依照《军刑法》或《保守军事秘密法》的规定处理。

第十一条 准备或实施防空所需的费用，根据性质和实际情况，分别由中央或地方当局支付。

第十二条 民众因土地或建筑物被征用于防空目的而遭受的损失，由地方政府依法予以补偿。

pages.en:
-4-
Article 13. Whoever suffers injury, sickness or
death during service in the air defence, shall be
compensated with medical, burial or compassionate
fees by the Central or Local Government in accord-
ance with the law.
Article 14. The Detailed Rules for the Enforcement
of this Law shall be enacted by the highest military
authorities attached to the National Government.
Article 15. This Law shall come into force on
the date of its promulgation.
pages.zh:
-4-
第十三条。凡在防空服役期间遭受伤害、疾病或死亡者，由中央或地方政府依法给予医疗、丧葬或抚恤费用补偿。
第十四条。本法施行细则，由隶属于国民政府之最高军事机关制定之。
第十五条。本法自公布之日起施行。

September 15, 1937.    3.    Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-

REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE PUNISHMENT OF CHINESE TRAITORS

The Military Affairs Commission has drawn up a set of regulations governing the punishment of Chinese traitors and has notified the various provincial and municipal authorities of the same.
The regulations are as follows :-
Article 1. - All cases pertaining to Chinese traitors shall be dealt with in accordance with these regulations.
Article 2. - (I) Whoever commits any one of the following acts by conspiring with or aiding an enemy country or its officials and civilians is a Chinese traitor and shall be punished with death :-
(1) Attempts to conspire with an enemy country in fighting against his own country.
(2) Plots to start a riot.
(3) Works for an enemy army.
(4) Recruits soldiers or other man power for military purpose on behalf of an enemy country.
(5) Provides, purchases or transports military supplies for an enemy army.
(6) Spies on or steals military intelligence or secrets.
(7) Communicates with an enemy army.
(8) Incites military men, public officers or civilians of his own country to violate discipline, abandon their duties or conspire with the enemy.
(9) Allows himself to be incited by offenders under the previous items.
(10) Transports or sells to an enemy country raw materials that can be manufactured into firearms.
(11) Disturbs the finance of the country.
(12) Destroys means of communication.
(13) Attempts to commit acts harmful to his own country besides those specified in the foregoing.
(II) Whoever attempts, makes preparation or plots to commit any of the offences specified in Section 1 of this Article shall be punished with imprisonment for not less than seven years.
Article 3. - Violators of these regulations shall be tried by military organs by court-martial.
Article 4. - Where a sentence is given for an offence under these regulations, the case shall be forwarded to the highest military organ for confirmation, before such sentence can be executed. Whereas if the case requires immediate disposal, request for confirmation of sentence may be made by telegram or report may be forwarded for record in due course after the sentence has been executed. In time of war, the Commander for the Enforcement of Martial Law, the Commander of the Forces in the war zone or the Commander-in-Chief of the National Armies are authorized to forward reports on such cases for record purposes.
Article 5. - These regulations will come into force on the date of their promulgation.

1937年9月15日。    3.    晨间译件

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

惩治汉奸条例

军事委员会已制定一套惩治汉奸条例，并通令各省市当局知悉。
条例如下：-
第一条。- 所有涉及汉奸之案件，均依本条例处理。
第二条。- (一) 凡勾结或辅助敌国及其官员、平民，实施下列行为之一者，即为汉奸，处死刑：-
(1) 企图勾结敌国以对抗本国。
(2) 策划发动暴乱。
(3) 为敌军效力。
(4) 代表敌国招募士兵或其他人力用于军事目的。
(5) 为敌军提供、购买或运输军需物资。
(6) 刺探或窃取军事情报或机密。
(7) 与敌军通讯。
(8) 煽动本国军人、公务员或平民违反纪律、擅离职守或与敌人勾结。
(9) 受前款所列罪犯之煽动。
(10) 向敌国运输或出售可制造枪械之原材料。
(11) 扰乱国家金融。
(12) 破坏通讯设施。
(13) 企图实施除上述规定以外之危害本国行为。
(二) 凡企图、预备或策划实施本条第一款所列任何罪行者，处七年以上有期徒刑。
第三条。- 违反本条例者，由军事机关进行军法审判。
第四条。- 凡因触犯本条例而被判刑之案件，须呈报最高军事机关核准后，方可执行刑罚。惟若案件需紧急处置，可通过电报请求核准刑罚，或在执行刑罚后适时呈报备案。战时，戒严司令、战区部队指挥官或国军总司令有权将此类案件呈报备案。
第五条。- 本条例自公布之日起施行。

REPORT
Date September 24, 1937
Subject Warning Letter received by Chinese Employees of the Yokohama
Specie Bank, The Bund.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C Crawford D.S.

With reference to the remarks of Acting Commissioner on
the attached report, enquiries have been made but have failed
to establish any connection between Mr. Liang Tung-fan(梁桐芳),
one armed "Hero" of the Blood and Soul Corps in 1934, with the
so-called "Merchants Joint Group to Eliminate Traitors(商民联合
诛奸团)which purported to be responsible for the sending of
a threatening letter to the Chinese staff of the Yokohama Specie
Bank on September 13, 1937.

Liang Tung-fan is at present engaged in the management
of the *Chinese Youths Anti-Enemy and National Salvation Association
(中華青年抗敵救亡團 ) with offices at Kwan Ti Miao Tample,
West Gate, Nanteo. Details of this Association were reported
upon by this Section on August 6, 1937.

Discreet enquiries show that members of this Association
totalling some 250 confine their activities to conducting anti-
air raid and anti-gas propaganda among villagers in and around
Shanghai and assisting Chinese troops in the front line in all
possible ways. It is learned that of these 250 members only
10 are remaining in Shanghai for the purpose of dealing with
affairs relating to recruiting new members; 40 having gone to
Sungkiang and Kashing for propaganda work and 200 having been
sent to various sectors of the front.

(印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 25 SEP. 1937 (C.I.BRANCH))

撰写人 C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang 转交人 C Crawford D.S.

鉴于代理总监对附件报告的批示，经查询，未能证实梁桐芳先生（1934年“血魂团”的一名武装“英雄”）与所谓“商民联合诛奸团”之间有任何关联，该团体声称对1937年9月13日向横滨正金银行华籍职员发送恐吓信一事负责。

梁桐芳目前任职于“中华青年抗敌救亡团”，该团办事处位于南市西门关帝庙。本部已于1937年8月6日就该协会详情提交报告。

秘密调查显示，该协会成员总计约250人，其活动局限于在上海及周边村民中开展防空袭和防毒气宣传，并以各种可能方式协助前线中国军队。据悉，在这250名成员中，仅有10人留在上海处理招募新会员相关事务；40人已前往松江和嘉兴从事宣传工作；200人已被派往各个前线区域。

At 7p.m. 14-9-37, P.C. 240 Albon, attached to
Central Station, brought two letters written in
Chinese to the station. One of the letters was
addressed to the Chinese manager of the Mitsui Bank
Ltd., 93 Nanking Road, while the other was addressed to
all the Chinese employees of the same concern.

P.C. Albon reported that the two letters had been
given to him by the sub-manager of the bank in view
of their threatening nature.

Owing to the late hour when the letters were
received it was impossible to locate the manager of
the firm until today.

At 9a.m. 15-9-37, Dets. Abayesani and C.M.C.
204 visited the bank and interviewed the sub-manager
Mr. Kawai, who stated that the letters were received
at the bank on the 11th and 12th inst.

Herewith is a translation of the two letters:-

No.1.

"To all the Chinese employees
of the Mitsui Bank, Ltd.,
Since the hostilities started in Shanghai,
the Japanese have conducted a great massacre
by bombing several thousands of Chinese
civilians and refugees, but you, all Chinese,
are still working in the enemy's firm. We
notify you to leave your positions within three
days after the receipt of this letter, otherwise
certain suitable action will be taken as you
are being investigated by us. You may consult
with the Chinese manager regarding your
financial support. After your general resigna-
tion you may find other work in inland. We don't
think that your Chinese manager will refuse your
request, because he is also a Chinese.
Sgd:- The Traitor Suppression Party"

1937年9月14日下午7点，隶属中央捕房的警员240号 Albon 将两封中文信件带到捕房。其中一封信寄给南京路93号三井银行有限公司的华籍经理，另一封则寄给该公司的全体华籍雇员。

Albon 警员报告称，鉴于这两封信具有威胁性质，银行副经理将其交给了他。

由于收到信件的时间较晚，直到今天才找到该公司经理。

1937年9月15日上午9点，侦探 Abayesani 和华籍巡长 204号 访问了银行，并会见了副经理 Kawai 先生，他表示信件是在本月11日和12日收到的。

兹附上两封信的译文：-

第1号。

“致
三井银行有限公司全体华籍雇员，
自从上海战事爆发以来，日本人通过轰炸数千名中国平民和难民进行了大屠杀，但你们所有中国人仍在敌对公司工作。我们通知你们，在收到此信后三天内离开职位，否则我们将采取适当行动，因为我们正在调查你们。你们可就经济支持问题与华籍经理协商。在集体辞职后，你们可以在内地寻找其他工作。我们认为你们的华籍经理不会拒绝你们的请求，因为他也是中国人。
签署：- 诛奸党”

2nd.

"To
All Chinese employees,

As to the national situation is now at a crisis, all the Chinese people should conscientiously contribute their individual assistance to their own country. It is every one's duty to offer his assistance to the country. Each of us is responsible for the national prosperity or adversity. We hate to learn that the uneducated loafers are engaged by the enemy to be the traitors of the country, but we excuse them for not having education. Now let us look back upon the educated people, a number of them are unable to carry out partial work for their own country, but they at least should not be utilized by the enemy to perform tasks against the conscience. Is this a shameful thing ? You are continuing your work in the firm for the sake of subsistence, therefore, you can be excused. Under such a critical situation, all that you may do is to carry out your usual work, but not any task to assist the enemy. It is stated that you have already done something wrong. Upon hearing this news we were very angry. Therefore we write this letter of warning and hope all of you will repent regarding your previous misconduct, and turn to be a good citizen.

From:- The Merchants' Traitor Suppression Party.
10-9-37".

Further enquiries made ascertained that there are sixteen Chinese employed at the bank, and since the commencement of hostilities only half of this number have shown up for work.

Mr. Fukai added, that as there was now no Chinese business being carried out it was not necessary for any of the Chinese staff to attend. The staff were aware of this, but simply attended so that they would be able to draw their wages.

第2号。

“致
全体华籍雇员，

鉴于国家局势现已处于危机之中，所有中国人都应 conscientiously（原文如此，意为真诚地/自觉地）为各自的国家贡献个人力量。为国效力是每个人的责任。我们每个人都对国家的兴衰负有责任。我们痛心地得知，一些未受教育游手好闲之人被敌人雇佣成为国家叛徒，但我们原谅他们缺乏教育。现在让我们回顾一下受过教育的人，他们中许多人无法为国家做部分工作，但他们至少不应被敌人利用去执行违背良心的任务。这是一件可耻的事吗？你们为了生计继续在公司工作，因此可以得到原谅。在此危急关头，你们所能做的只是完成日常工作，而不是执行任何协助敌人的任务。据说你们已经做错了事。听到这个消息我们非常愤怒。因此，我们写这封警告信，希望你们都能悔改以前的不当行为，做一个好公民。

来自：- 商民诛奸团。
1937年9月10日”。

进一步查询查明，该银行雇佣了十六名华人，自战事开始以来，只有半数人员上班。

Fukai 先生补充说，由于现在没有中国业务在进行，任何华籍职员都无需出勤。职员们知道这一点，但只是为了能够领取薪水而照常出勤。

Twenty four Japanese are employed at the bank, and
they carry out what business there is to be done. After
office hours they reside at the Metropole Hotel.

The following police protection has daily been

1 Foreign policeman 8 a.m. to 12noon and 2p.m. to 5p.m.
2 S.R.C.s the whole twenty four hours.
2 C.I.C.s 7 a.m. to 11p.m.

The manager of the bank stated that he is quite
satisfied with the police protection afforded.

The actual persons who wrote the letters are unknown.

within his power for the sake of the nation. It
goes without saying that we are responsible for the
existence or downfall of our country. The fact that
the ignorant people who are utilized as tools by the
enemy is very much regretted, but in mitigation we
must not forget that they are uneducated people who
are lacking in national spirit. Now those educated
people, who are unable to work for the nation, they
should at least refrain from serving as tools of the
enemy as it may will be construed as an unpatriotic.
You people are still working for your company (?)
for the purpose of maintaining your living. We fully
realize your circumstances in this respect. However,
during this period when the fate of the nation is in
the balance, every Chinese citizen should stop forthwith
any activities in favour of the enemy, maybe with the
exception of routine work which you are compelled to do.
It has come to our notice that you have been recently
engaged in reckless acts. We, the members of the
Merchants Joint Group to Eliminate Traitors, are
highly indignant at such activity. We therefore give
you this warning in the hope that you will repent and
become good citizens, after receipt of this letter.

Merchants Joint Group to
Eliminate Traitors
(商民联合除奸团)
September 10.

据称出自“商民联合除奸团”、日期为9月10日的信件译文。
............

致华籍职员，

国难日益深重。为尽公民之责，每一位明智的中国人皆应为国家竭尽全力。我国之存亡，吾辈责无旁贷，此乃不言而喻之事。愚民被敌人利用作为工具，虽令人深感遗憾，但予以宽宥时，切莫忘记他们是缺乏民族精神的未受教育者。如今那些受过教育却未能为国效力之人，至少应避免成为敌人的工具，否则将被视为不爱国。尔等仍为公司工作以维持生计。对此境况，我们充分理解。然而，在国家命运悬于一线之际，每一位中国公民应立即停止任何有利于敌人的活动，或许除了你们被迫进行的日常工作之外。我们要知悉，尔等近期从事了鲁莽之举。我们，“商民联合除奸团”成员，对此类活动感到极度愤慨。因此，我们发出此警告，希望你们在收到此信后能悔过自新，成为良民。

商民联合除奸团
(商民联合除奸团)

D.C. in Charge.

Two Chinese employees of the Soviet Consulate
arrested by the Japanese Naval Authorities.

At about 9.30 a.m. August 18, 1937, Mr. E.A. Long,
Secretary to the Consular Body, telephoned the following:-

About 12 m.n. on August 16, two Chinese employees
of the Soviet Consulate were arrested by the Japanese
Naval Authorities for keeping a light showing at night
within the Consulate. After enquiry, at the instance
of the Soviet Authorities, the Japanese Consulate
Authorities informed Mr. Long that both the men had been
handed over to the Shanghai Municipal Police.

Enquiries were made and it was found that the two
had not been handed over to us and they were subsequently
found to be in the custody of the Japanese Naval Police.
Negotiations between the D.O. and D.D.O. "C" and the
Japanese Authorities eventually resulted in both men
being handed over to the Police on 19.8.37 to be released
on the obtaining of a receipt signed by a responsible
official of the Soviet Consulate.

Mr. U.A. Konstantinov, Vice-Consul, signed and
sealed the necessary receipt (copy attached) and both
the servants were released from Police Headquarters at
11.20 a.m. 19-8-37.

Particulars of two servants: (1) Yang Kyau Loong
(楊怪流), father, and (2) Yang Ah Tsoo (楊阿福),
son (Coolies).

D. O. (Crime).

苏联领事馆两名华籍雇员被日本海军当局逮捕。

1937年8月18日上午约9时30分，领事团秘书 E.A. Long 先生致电告知如下：

8月16日午夜约12时，苏联领事馆两名华籍雇员因在领事馆内夜间亮灯，被日本海军当局逮捕。经查询，应苏联当局要求，日本领事馆当局通知 Long 先生，两人已移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。

经调查，发现两人并未移交给本局，随后查明他们处于日本海军警察的拘留之下。行动部主任（D.O.）和行动部副主任（D.D.O.）“C”与日本当局进行交涉，最终导致两人于1937年8月19日移交给警方，并在取得苏联领事馆负责官员签署的收据后予以释放。

副领事 U.A. Konstantinov 先生签署并盖章确认了必要的收据（附副本），两名仆役于1937年8月19日上午11时20分从警察总局获释。

两名仆役详情：(1) 杨怪流（Yang Kyau Loong），父亲，以及 (2) 杨阿福（Yang Ah Tsoo），儿子（苦力）。

Subject Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications -
Erection of a new plant on Bubbling Well Road.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

On September 1, 1937 work commenced at Houses 149 and
151, Lane 591, Bubbling Well Road for the erection of a new
plant for a reserve office of the Shanghai Telegraph Office
of the Ministry of Communications. These two houses
are being converted into a telegraph receiving office and
when completed will be able to handle traffic to the volume
of approximately 1,000 messages per day.
According to Mr. Orlando PAO, general manager of the
head office located at 70 Foochow Road, the new office is
being erected to replace the one which was formerly in use
in Nantao, and will probably be put into service in one week
to ten day's time. Mr. Pao emphasised that the new
office would be employed solely for domestic telegraph
traffic and that no transmitting or receiving of radio
messages would take place. He also indicated that as far
as he was aware, no correspondence had passed between the
Ministry of Communications and the Shanghai Municipal Council
regarding the erection of the new plant.

Ja. Pitts

September 5, 1937. Morning Translation

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-

REVISED LAW GOVERNING THE PUNISHMENT OF PERSONS WHO COMMIT
ACTS WITH INTENT TO INJURE THE REPUBLIC OF CHINA

In a mandate issued on September 4, the
National Government ordered the nullification of the Law
governing the Punishment of Persons Who Commit Acts with
Intent to Injure the Republic of China and promulgated the
revised text of the law.
The Revised Law governing the Punishment of
Persons Who Commit Acts with Intent to Injure the Republic
of China is as follows :-
Article 1. - (I) Whoever commits, with
intent to injure the Republic of China, any one of the
following acts shall be punished with death:
(1) Secretly communicates with an enemy
country and plots to disturb the public peace.
(2) Conspires with rebels and plots to
disturb the public peace.
(3) Purchases or transports military supplies
on behalf of an enemy country or rebels.
(4) Divulges or transmits political or military
secrets to an enemy country or rebels.
(5) Destroys means of communication or
military bases.
(6) Incites military men to violate discipline,
abandon their duties or to conspire with an enemy country or
rebels.
(7) Incites others to conspire with an enemy
country or rebels, or to disturb the public peace.
(8) Fabricates rumours to incite the public,
cause sedition among the military men or to disturb the
public peace.
(9) Spreads rebellious propaganda by means
of written or spoken words, drawings, pictures or speeches
beneficial to an enemy country or rebels.
(II) Whoever, being incited,
commits any of the offences specified in the last section
and surrenders himself shall have his punishment reduced
or remitted.
Article 2. - (I) Whoever knowingly harbours
a person conspiring with an enemy country or a rebel and
fails to report same shall be punished with imprisonment
for not less than five years.
(II) Whoever commits the offence
specified in the last section and surrenders himself shall
have his punishment reduced or remitted.
Article 3. - Whoever with intent to injure
the Republic of China organizes associations or holds
meetings shall be punished with imprisonment for not less
than five years, and not more than fifteen years.
Article 4. - Whoever, although without
intent to injure the Republic of China, spreads propaganda
by means of written words, drawings or speeches beneficial
to the enemy country during a period of hostilities with an
alien country shall be punished with imprisonment for not
more than three years.

1937年9月5日。晨间译文

《申报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

修订惩治危害民国行为条例

国民政府在9月4日发布命令，废止《惩治危害民国行为条例》，并颁布该条例的修订文本。
修订后的《惩治危害民国行为条例》如下：-
第一条. - (一) 凡意图危害中华民国，有下列行为之一者，处死刑：
(1) 通谋敌国，图谋扰乱治安。
(2) 勾结叛徒，图谋扰乱治安。
(3) 为敌国或叛徒购买或运输军用物资。
(4) 向敌国或叛徒泄露或传递政治或军事秘密。
(5) 破坏交通或军事设施。
(6) 煽动军人违反纪律、放弃职责或与敌国或叛徒勾结。
(7) 煽动他人通谋敌国或叛徒，或扰乱治安。
(8) 制造谣言以煽动民众、引起军人骚动或扰乱治安。
(9) 通过文字、言语、图画、图片或演讲散布有利于敌国或叛徒的反宣传。
(二) 受煽动而犯前项各款之罪并自首者，减轻或免除其刑罚。
第二条. - (一) 明知是通谋敌国之人或叛徒而予以藏匿且不报告者，处五年以上有期徒刑。
(二) 犯前项之罪并自首者，减轻或免除其刑罚。
第三条. - 凡意图危害中华民国而组织团体或举行集会者，处五年以上十五年以下有期徒刑。
第四条. - 虽无危害中华民国之意图，但在与外国交战期间，散布有利于敌国之文字、图画或言论宣传者，处三年以下有期徒刑。

pages.en:
September 5, 1937.    2    Morning Translation

Article 5. - Whoever spreads false news liable
to disturb the public peace or alarm the people during a
period of hostilities with an alien country shall be
punished with imprisonment or detention for not more than
one year.
Article 6. - Whoever without permission from
the Government corresponds with the people of an enemy
country during a period of hostilities with such country
shall be punished with imprisonment or detention for not
more than one year.
Article 7. - Violators of this law shall be
tried by the highest local military organ in districts
concerned.
Article 8. - Where sentences are given by
military organs for offences under this law, the case
shall be forwarded to the Higher Military Organ having
jurisdiction for confirmation, before such sentences can
be executed.
Article 9. - A military or police organ which
arrests offenders suspected of having committed an offence
mentioned in this law shall immediately inform the
organization concerned.
Article 10. - In the absence of any specific
provision in this law, the provisions in the Criminal Code
shall be applicable.
Article 11. - This law shall come into force
on the date of its promulgation.

第五条. - 在与外国交战期间，散布足以扰乱治安或惊扰民众之虚假新闻者，处一年以下有期徒刑或拘役。
第六条. - 未经政府许可，在与该国交战期间与敌国人民通信者，处一年以下有期徒刑或拘役。
第七条. - 违反本法者，由有关地区最高军事机关审判。
第八条. - 军事机关对本法规定之罪行作出判决后，须报送有管辖权的高级军事机关核准，方可执行。
第九条. - 逮捕涉嫌犯本法所述罪行之罪犯的军事或警察机关，应立即通知有关机构。
第十条. - 本法未作具体规定的，适用刑法典之规定。
第十一条. - 本法自公布之日起施行。

September 1, 1937. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

PROVISIONAL REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE PUNISHMENT OF PERSONS WHO SUPPLY FOOD STUFFS TO THE ENEMY

In a mandate issued on August 31, the National Government promulgated the following Provisional Regulations governing the Punishment of Persons who Supply Food Stuffs to the Enemy:-

Article 1. - Whoever supplies food stuffs to the enemy shall be dealt with according to these regulations.

Article 2. - The phrase "food stuffs" referred to in these regulations denotes grains, rice, wheat, flour, cereals and other products that can be used for food.

Article 3. - Whoever supplies food stuffs to the enemy troops shall be punishable with death.

Article 4. - Whoever during the period of emergency secretly exports food stuffs, whose exportation is prohibited, of more than a hundred thousand catties shall be considered as supplying food stuffs to the enemy.

Whoever commits the preceding offence but only to the quantity of a hundred thousand catties shall be punished with life imprisonment.

Article 5. - Whoever harbours offenders as specified in the preceding two Articles shall be dealt with with the same severity as the chief culprit.

Article 6. - The food provisions shall be confiscated and fines equivalent to the value of the food provisions shall be imposed on the offenders specified in Articles 3 and 4. In the event of failure to pay the imposed fines, administrative organs in the district concerned may be entrusted to sell the property of the offender by auction, but a report to such effect should be submitted to the highest military authorities for record.

Article 7. - Fines will be imposed on persons who attempt to commit the offences specified in Articles 3 and 4.

Article 8. - Whoever attempts or plots to commit an offence specified in Article 3 shall be punished with imprisonment for not less than 7 years.

Whoever attempts or plots to commit an offence specified in Article 4 shall be punished with imprisonment for not less than one year and not more than seven years.

Article 9. - Perpetrators of offences specified in these regulations shall be tried by official organs enjoying military authority whose judgment will become effective after having been approved by the Central military authorities. In areas where fighting is in progress, or during the disruption of traffic or during emergency, such cases will be tried by the highest military organ in the vicinity, but reports should be submitted after the occurrence.

Article 10. - These regulations will come into effect on the date of their promulgation.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

惩处向敌人供应食品者暂行条例

国民政府于8月31日发布命令，颁布下列《惩处向敌人供应食品者暂行条例》：

第一条。——凡向敌人供应食品者，均依本条例处理。

第二条。——本条例所称“食品”，系指谷类、大米、小麦、面粉、杂粮及其他可用作食物的产品。

第三条。——凡向敌军供应食品者，处以死刑。

第四条。——凡在紧急时期秘密出口禁止出口之食品超过十万斤者，视为向敌人供应食品。

犯前款罪行但数量仅达十万斤者，处以无期徒刑。

第五条。——窝藏前两条规定之罪犯者，与主犯同罪论处。

第六条。——对于第三、四条规定之罪犯，其食品予以没收，并处以相当于食品价值的罚款。如未能缴纳所处罚金，可委托该地区行政机关拍卖罪犯财产，但须将此情况报告最高军事当局备案。

第七条。——企图犯第三、四条规定之罪行的人，将处以罚金。

第八条。——企图或预谋犯第三条规定之罪行的人，处以七年以上有期徒刑。

企图或预谋犯第四条规定之罪行的人，处以一年以上七年以下有期徒刑。

第九条。——本条例规定之罪犯，由拥有军事权力的官方机关审判，其判决经中央军事当局批准后生效。在战斗进行中、交通中断或紧急状态下，此类案件由附近最高军事机关审判，但事后应提交报告。

第十条。——本条例自公布之日起生效。

August 30, 1937.
3
Afternoon Translation

Ta Kung Pao (Extra) :-

JAPAN VIOLATES INTERNATIONAL LAW

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai
yesterday sent the following telegram to the National
Military Affairs' Commission at Nanking :-
"Since her provocation of local hostilities,
brutal Japan has utterly ignored international law by
repeatedly and recklessly bombing innocent civilians,
wounded soldiers and members of the Red Cross Society.
According to international law in times of war, if one
party commits outrageous acts, the other is free to take
reprisals, such as the execution of enemy prisoners and
the confiscation of all enemy properties. The Commission
is requested to make this known to the public, both
Chinese and foreign, so that the enemy may take note
and refrain from continuing their outrageous activities."

Ta Kung Pao (Extra) :-

JAPANESE WARSHIPS CONCENTRATE OUTSIDE WOOSUNG

Despite the great losses which have been
inflicted on their troops in their attempts to land at
Woosung and the vicinity, Japanese militarists are still
planning to make a final struggle. By noon to-day,
thirty-eight Japanese warships, including the flagship
Idzumo which steamed out of the Whangpoo at 2 a.m., were
gathered outside Woosung for the purpose of assisting the
landing of Japanese troops. They are not likely to
meet with success, however, as the Chinese defence lines
are very strong.
The International Recreation Club at Kiangwan
was bombarded by Japanese warships at 9 a.m. to-day, but
little damage was done to the Chinese positions.

All the eleven Japanese warships in harbour
last night are now lying outside Woosung. It is believed
that the Japanese have some plan in view.

Ta Kung Pao (Extra) :-

SINO-SOVIET NON-AGGRESSION TREATY

A telegram received from Europe by well-
informed local circles reveals that when making public
the Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Treaty, the Foreign Office
of the U.S.S.R. did not comment on the subject.
Reporters of European newspapers stationed at
Moscow called on certain Soviet officials soliciting
their opinions in regard to the conclusion of the Sino-
Soviet Non-Aggression Treaty, but these officials maintained
a discreet silence.
Observers hold the belief that the Red Army
will resort to action should Outer Mongolia be subjected
to attack. The Far Eastern Red Army of the Soviet
Government is estimated as being between 400,000 and
500,000 strong.

3
下午译件

《大公报》（号外）：

日本违反国际法

上海总商会昨日向南京国民政府军事委员会发出如下电报：
“自从日本挑衅引发局部战事以来，残暴的日本完全无视国际法，反复肆意轰炸无辜平民、伤兵及红十字会成员。根据战时国际法，若一方犯下暴行，另一方有权采取报复措施，如处决战俘及没收敌方所有财产。恳请委员会向中外公众公布此事，以使敌人知悉并停止其暴行。”

《大公报》（号外）：

日军舰艇集结于吴淞口外

尽管日军在试图登陆吴淞口及周边地区时遭受重大损失，日本军国主义者仍计划做最后挣扎。截至今日中午，包括凌晨2时驶出黄浦江的旗舰“出云”号在内的三十八艘日本军舰，已聚集在吴淞口外，旨在协助日军登陆。然而，鉴于中国防线非常坚固，他们不太可能成功。
位于江湾的国际娱乐总会于今日上午9时遭到日本军舰炮击，但中方阵地受损甚微。

昨晚停泊在港内的全部十一艘日本军舰，现均停泊在吴淞口外。据信日本人有某种计划。

《大公报》（号外）：

中苏互不侵犯条约

本地消息灵通人士收到来自欧洲的电报称，苏联外交部在公布《中苏互不侵犯条约》时，未对此事发表评论。
驻莫斯科的欧洲报纸记者拜访了一些苏联官员，征求他们对签订《中苏互不侵犯条约》的看法，但这些官员保持谨慎的沉默。
观察家认为，如果外蒙古遭受攻击，红军将采取行动。苏联政府的远东红军估计兵力在40万至50万之间。
