Subject Activities of N. BOGDANOFF and N. KIASHKIN in regard to the
present local hostilities.

Made by D. S. Mischenko Forwarded by N. Medvedeff, D.S.I.

Information has been received to the effect that a Russian
named Nicolai BOGDANOFF, 32 of age, arrived in Shanghai from
Tsingtao by train on August 23, 1937 and took up residence with
his mother at No. 764 Rue Lafayette, French Concession.

According to enquiries made from various sources, it
has been ascertained that BOGDANOFF was employed by Edgewater
Mansions, Tsingtao at a salary of $100.00, which position he
left for the purpose of coming to Shanghai and joining his former
partner named Nicolai KIASHKIN, Aviator/mechanic by profession,
with whom he intends to renew his activities as manufacturers
of aviation bombs and torpedoes.

It has been learned from the French Police that on
August 22, 1935 two models of aviation bombs were found in
possession of BOGDANOFF and KIASHKIN at Mr. Hofer's residence
House No. 2 Lane 66, Rue Lorton French Concession, and were
taken away by the French Police for examination. On being found
harmless, they were returned to KIASHKIN who took them to Nanking
for the purpose of demonstration. According to BOGDANOFF, the
demonstration was successful and the bombs are still in Nanking.
Further activities of the two concerned in 1935, indicated that
their project failed.

Nicolai KIASHKIN at present is an inmate of the Russian
Orthodox Confraternity Hospital, 230 Route Sai-zoong, French
Concession, having been admitted on August 14, 1937 suffering
from shrapnel wound sustained in the French Concession during
an air raid.

At present BOGDANOFF is making further arrangements with
the Chinese authorities in order to be permitted to give further
demonstration.

August 28, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

China Times (Noon Issue) :-

ENEMY STOUTLY RESISTED AT LIUHO

According to information secured by this paper at 10 this morning, there are at present over 20 Japanese warships outside Woosung from Changwehpang to the Lion Forest Forts, from where up to the sea coast along Liuho, they are joined in one straight line by an additional number of more than 40 gunboats. All of these vessels have their guns aimed at the Chinese lines. However, in view of the fact that we have already constructed very strong defences along the various strategic points which are very likely to be bombarded by the Japanese warships, there is very small likelihood of the enemy - succeeding in any of their attempts.

According to reliable information, it is definitely ascertained that more than 10 Japanese warships arrived outside Liuho and Yanglingkou after 10 p.m. yesterday, and immediately afterwards they bombarded our defence lines, while at the same time some 30 to 40 small boats and lighters were moored alongside the gunboats as a preparation to force a landing at these points. Besides greeting them with heavy gunfire, the Chinese defenders were ordered to put up a dogged attack with trench mortars and machine guns upon any invaders who were seen attempting to land.

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

18 TRAITORS EXECUTED IN NANKING

18 Chinese traitors, including Huang Tsing (黄濬), a secretary of the Executive Yuan, and his son, were executed in Nanking on August 26 for supplying information to the enemy about confidential documents, prying out military secrets and locations and conditions of fortifications, and carrying out other espionage work for the enemy.

China Evening News of August 27 :-

CHINESE TRAITORS ACTIVE LOCALLY

Chinese traitors are very active at many places in this locality. Whenever the Chinese air force conduct night air raids, they fire into the air red and green signals to indicate the number and location of the Chinese planes, thereby facilitating the anti-aircraft guns of the enemy in finding their mark. The Chinese military authorities are at present conducting a strict investigation and it is hoped that the public will render every assistance in tracking down Chinese traitors.

1937年8月28日。下午译件。

《时报》（午刊）：

敌军在浏河顽强抵抗

据本报今晨10时获得的消息，目前吴淞口外从张华浜到狮子林炮台，有20多艘日本军舰，从那里沿浏河直至海岸线，另有40多艘炮舰排成一条直线。所有这些船只的火炮都瞄准了中国防线。然而，鉴于我们已在很可能遭到日本军舰炮击的各个战略要点构筑了非常坚固的防御工事，敌人企图成功的可能性极小。

据可靠消息证实，昨晚10点后，确有10多艘日本军舰抵达浏河和杨林口外，随即炮击我方防线，同时约有30至40艘小船和驳船停靠在炮舰旁，准备在这些地点强行登陆。中国守军除了以猛烈火力迎击外，还奉命使用迫击炮和机枪，对任何试图登陆的入侵者发起顽强攻击。

《国民新闻》及其他本地报纸：

18名汉奸在南京被处决

包括行政院秘书黄濬（黄濬）及其儿子在内的18名中国汉奸，因向敌人提供机密文件情报、刺探军事秘密及要塞位置和状况，并为敌人从事其他间谍工作，于8月26日在南京被处决。

8月27日《中华晚报》：

本地汉奸活动猖獗

本地多处汉奸活动非常活跃。每当中国空军进行夜间空袭时，他们便向空中发射红绿信号弹，标示中国飞机的数量和位置，从而便于敌方高射炮瞄准。中国军方目前正在严格调查，希望公众全力协助追查汉奸。

File No. .........

REPORT
Date. August 20, 1937.

Subject Inquiries regarding a rumour to the effect that the
Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works were manufacturing
poison gas.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C. Crawford. A.S.

With further reference to this Section's report
of August 20, it has been learnt from an unquestionable
source that the Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works, 420
Brenan Road, is closely associated with the Far East
Oxygen & Acetylene Company, Ltd., 200 Route de Zikawei,
a reputable firm registered at the French Consulate-General
and managed by M. Pierre Santerre, a French citizen.
The first mentioned concern is under a business contract
to supply the French concern with oxygen which is used
in large quantities by the latter concern in carrying out
its oxy-acetylenic welding contracts on the river front
and elsewhere. For this purpose gas cylinders are purchased
and supplied by the Far East Oxygen & Acetylene Co. Ltd.
to the Chinese concern as refills.
The Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works is under
the joint managership of Mr. Woo Yung-chu and M. Pierre
Santerre, and recently the latter discharged twenty native
workers and replaced them with a similar number of Annamite
workers who are considered more suitable by reason of
their ability to speak a little French.
It has been confirmed from another and entirely
reliable source that the Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical
Works has no cooling or compression plant installations,
without which it would be quite impossible to manufacture
poison gas for war purposes.
A Shanghai Power Company official who has checked
the power meter installed at the Brenan Piece Sub-Station
confirms that no power has been used by the Tien Yuen Co.
since August 13.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE AUG. 1937）

日期：1937年8月20日。

主题：关于天原电化厂制造毒气谣言的调查。
由特别股督察劳里尔（Laurier）呈报，经助理总监克劳福德（C. Crawford）转呈。

继本股8月20日的报告之后，从一确凿无疑的消息来源获悉，位于白利南路（Brenan Road）420号的天原电化厂与位于徐家汇路（Route de Zikawei）200号的远东氧气乙炔有限公司（Far East Oxygen & Acetylene Company, Ltd.）关系密切。后者是一家在法国总领事馆注册的信誉良好的公司，由法国公民皮埃尔·桑泰尔（M. Pierre Santerre）先生管理。前述天原电化厂根据商业合同向该法商供应氧气，后者在其承接的沿江及其他地区的氧乙炔焊接合同中大量使用该氧气。为此，气瓶由远东氧气乙炔有限公司购买并作为充装容器提供给这家华商企业。

天原电化厂由吴赓初（Woo Yung-chu）先生和皮埃尔·桑泰尔（M. Pierre Santerre）先生共同管理。最近，后者解雇了二十名中国工人，并以同等数量的安南（Annamite，即越南）工人取而代之，理由是这些工人能讲一点法语，被认为更为合适。

经另一完全可靠的消息来源证实，天原电化厂没有冷却或压缩设备装置，若无这些装置，根本不可能制造用于战争目的的毒气。

一位上海电力公司官员核查了安装在白利南分区变电站的电表后确认，自8月13日以来，天原公司未使用任何电力。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处副总监 1937年8月）
（批：归档 / OBR / 8月20日。）

Shanghai; August 20, 1937.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）

Major K. M. Bourne,
Deputy Commissioner of Police in Charge.

Telephone message to Secretary of Council from
Tien Yuen Factory, 320 Brenan Road.

"A message was received by the Factory this
morning purporting to come from the Council but
name of speaker unknown, asking the Factory whether
there was any truth in the rumour that they had in
their Factory or proposed to make there poisonous
gas. The Factory say that they have no poisonous
gas there and owing to absence of power have shut
down operations. They regard the rumour as a dan-
gerous one in this state of emergency and invite
an immediate investigation by the Council."

I have passed on this message to British Military
Headquarters Brigade Major. The Brigade Major (without
consulting the Brigadier) has expressed the opinion that the
investigation should, if possible, be made by the Municipal
Police and not by British Military. I understand there are
Chinese troops around the Factory and I think that Captain
Rennie fears, what he describes, as an international incident.

DC (Cw)
Any facts in fact
as above? Necessary action / despatch
PL.
Secretary.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ....
S.1, Special Branch. ~~XXXXXX~~
REPORT
Date August 20, 1937.
Subject Possibility of the manufacture of poison gas by the Tien Yuen
Electro & Chemical Works, 420 Brenan Road.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by D.B. Roo C.S.

With reference to the attached telegram received from
"British Force" on August 19 regarding the purchase of gas
cylinders by the Chinese Army ostensibly for the loading
of poison gas which, it is suspected, is being manufactured
by the Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works, 420 (not 320)
Brenan Road: enquiries were made on August 20, 1937, at
176 Rue du Marche, French Concession, the address of the
Tien Lee Synthetic Nitrogen Products, the Tien Chu Manufacturing
Company and the Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works.
Mr. Woo Yong Chu (吴赓初), Managing Director of the
last named concern, who was interviewed, stated that the firm
manufactured hydrochloric acid, caustic soda and various
bleaching powders solely for commercial purposes: hydrochloric
acid for photographic materials and certain condiments;
caustic soda for soap and the manufacture of cotton yarn
and bleaching powders for use in disinfectants. The
cylinders now on the premises are supplied by the Far Eastern
Oxygen Company, Route Ghisi (French Concern) and are filled
with oxygen gas which is manufactured in the Chemical Works
and distributed to various consumers in Shanghai and elsewhere.
In order to manufacture poison gas he stated, it would be
necessary to have a cooling process and compression plant,
neither of which were installed on the premises.
It has been ascertained that the only poison gases which
this firm could possibly manufacture in the circumstances
for use under the conditions at present obtaining in the
Shanghai area are phosgene and chlorine gases, both of which,
however, require treatment in compression and cooling plants
which are necessary in order to reduce the gases to liquid form.

报告
日期 1937年8月20日。
主题：天原电化厂，白利南路420号，可能制造毒气。
由特别股督察劳里尔（Laurier）呈报，经 D.B. Roo C.S. 转呈。

关于8月19日收到的来自“英军部队”的附件电报，内容涉及中国军队购买气瓶，疑似用于装载据信由天原电化厂（地址为白利南路420号，非320号）制造的毒气一事：1937年8月20日，在法租界马浪路（Rue du Marche）176号进行了调查，该地址是天利合成氮肥产品公司（Tien Lee Synthetic Nitrogen Products）、天竺制造公司（Tien Chu Manufacturing Company）和天原电化厂的所在地。

最后提及的那家公司——天原电化厂的董事总经理吴永楚（Woo Yong Chu，音译，即吴赓初）先生在接受问询时表示，该公司仅出于商业目的生产盐酸、烧碱和各种漂白粉：盐酸用于摄影材料和某些调味品；烧碱用于肥皂和棉纱制造；漂白粉用于消毒剂。目前在场的气瓶由位于祁齐路（Route Ghisi，法商）的远东氧气公司提供，里面充装的是在该化工厂制造并分销给上海及其他地区各类消费者的氧气。他表示，要制造毒气，必须要有冷却工序和压缩设备，而现场并未安装这两类设备。

经查证，在目前上海地区的局势条件下，该公司可能制造的唯一毒气是光气和氯气，然而这两种气体都需要经过压缩和冷却设备处理，以便将气体液化。

File No. 8039 A
S. 5, Special Branch. 8 37
REPORT
Date August 27, 1937.

Subject Attached letter from Mollers' Limited.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan.

LETTER
Reference the attached dated 19-8-37, which was
delivered to the undersigned by chit coolie, at 2 p.m. 27-8-37,
the matter referred to concerns an unconfirmed rumour which
reached Police Headquarters (Special Branch) on 18-8-37, to
the effect that the Japanese Naval Landing Party Forces had
hired several tugs and launches belonging to Mollers' Limited,
for the purpose of assisting in the landing of units from
Japanese naval ships in the Liuho and Woosung areas on 17-8-37.
Upon receipt of the rumour, D.S.I. Logan communicated by
telephone with Mr. Eric Moller at the latter's home in order
to obtain confirmation or denial of the rumour. Mr. Moller
emphatically denied the rumour and appeared to be much perturbed,
fearing that should the rumour be given publicity it would
prejudice his business interests with the Chinese. He was
assured that no publicity would be given to the rumour by the
Police.

(批：Clone)
(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / CRIME BRANCH / 28 AUG. 1937)

Upon receipt of the letter, aforesaid, D.S.I. Logan
communicated with Mr. Eric Kermode, Secretary, at 4 p.m.
27-8-37, in the absence of Mr. Eric Moller, and explained that
as the rumour which resulted in the telephonic enquiry mentioned
above, had reached Police Headquarters in the ordinary way, and
had not received publication elsewhere, the making of an
appointment with either Mr. Moller or Mr. Kermode would not
serve a useful purpose, especially as it was impossible for
the Police to divulge the source of information, true or untrue,
obtained in the ordinary way. Mr. Kermode expressed himself
as being satisfied with the explanation given and stated that
he would convey same to Mr. Moller.

(批：fil. / 28/8 / 2898)

D.S. Irvine
D. C. (Special Branch). D.S.I. 28/8.
W Logan
D. S. I.

报告
日期 1937年8月27日。

事由 附马勒有限公司来信。

制作及转呈人：副督察长 Logan。

信件
关于所附日期为19-8-37的信件，该信于27-8-37下午2时由送信苦力送达具名人手中，所述事项涉及一则未经证实的谣言，该谣言于1937年8月18日传至警察总局（特务科），称日本海军陆战队部队于1937年8月17日租用了马勒有限公司所属的数艘拖轮和汽艇，以协助日军舰只部队在浏河和吴淞地区登陆。
收到该谣言后，副督察长 Logan 通过电话与 Eric Moller 先生在其家中联系，以寻求对该谣言的确认或否认。Moller 先生坚决否认了该谣言，并显得十分不安，担心若该谣言公开，将损害其与华人的商业利益。警方向其保证，不会公开该谣言。

(批：Clone)
(印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 刑事科 / 1937年8月28日)

收到上述信件后，副督察长 Logan 于1937年8月27日下午4时，在 Eric Moller 先生不在的情况下，与秘书 Eric Kermode 先生取得联系，并解释说，由于导致上述电话查询的谣言是通过常规途径传至警察总局的，且未在其他地方刊登，因此与 Moller 先生或 Kermode 先生预约会面并无实际用处，尤其是警方不可能泄露通过常规途径获得的信息来源，无论真假。Kermode 先生表示对所作解释感到满意，并称会将此转达给 Moller 先生。

(批：归档 / 28/8 / 2898)

D.S. Irvine
D. C. (特务科)。 副督察长 28/8.
W Logan
副督察长。

SHANGHAI, August 19th, 1937.

Inspector Logan,
Political Intelligence Department,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Headquarters,
185, Foochow Road,
S H A N G H A I.

Dear Inspector Logan,

I am addressing this letter to you as a stranger, though possibly my name is well-known to you.

With reference to your telephone communication to my residence yesterday evening at about 6 p.m. - I beg to confirm that I have advised you that none of our tug boats had been down to Woosung on the 17th instant - as enquired by you - and, in regard to your information that we had been assisting Japanese cruisers - I denied this at the time most emphatically to Yourself.

You will recollect that I asked you for the source of your information - as the remarks and information placed at your disposal are detrimental both to my own good name and to my various Shipping Interests in Shanghai, and I think that you will realize that I am reasonably entitled to protection in this direction.

I would, therefore, greatly appreciate if you would kindly make an appointment whereby my Secretary, Mr. Eric Kermode, and Myself may call upon you to clear up this particular point.

With thanks in anticipation,

I remain,
Dear Inspector Logan,
Yours very faithfully,

Eric Moller.

and their orderly on Nanking Road.

Made XX and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

S.I. Gazeley attached to Louza Station while on
motor cycle patrol at 8.40 a.m. the 26.8.37, saw a public hire
motor car licence No. 17938 proceeding from West to East on
Nanking Road near Chekiang Road. This motor car was partly
camouflaged with twigs of trees and leaves, so he called on
it to stop, instead of which the motor car shot forward and
collided with a public ricsha at the side of the roadway and
damaged the wheel of the ricsha. When S.I. Gazeley approached
the motor car he then perceived that the occupants were
Chinese military officers and they had in their possession
leather satchels, so took them with the motor car to Louza
Station.

On being interrogated at the station they were found
to be (1) Ho Pah Chung, Major General attached to the staff
of the Nanking-Shanghai Garrison Commander's Headquarters,
(2) Tsu Zai Ling, Inspector of the S.C.G.P.B., but attached to
the Nanking-Shanghai Garrison Commander's Headquarters as a
liaison officer with the rank of major (This person was
driving the motor car), and an orderly.

Those people carried no arms, and the satchels contained
a few personal letters and a miscellaneous collection of toilet
articles, soap, tooth brush, tooth paste, face cloth and a few
bills. They were later escorted to Headquarters where they
were interrogated and statements taken from them, but both
could not give any information as to the disposition of the
Chinese troops around Shanghai or their strength, which they
both maintained was kept very confidential by the Garrison
Commander. The liaison officer is known to Supt. Tan as an
inspector of the S.C.G.P.B. Both men state that they entered

日期：1937年8月26日。

主题：关于在南京路逮捕两名中国军官及其勤务兵的报告。

由 XX 制作，并由督察长克劳福德（Crawford）转呈。

1937年8月26日上午8时40分，隶属于老闸捕房（Louza Station）的副巡佐盖兹利（Gazeley）在进行摩托车巡逻时，看见一辆牌照号为17938的公共出租汽车在南京路靠近浙江路处由西向东行驶。该汽车部分用树枝和树叶进行了伪装，因此他示意其停车，但该车反而加速向前冲去，撞上路旁的一辆公共人力车，致使人力车轮受损。当副巡佐盖兹利走近该汽车时，他发现车内乘客为中国军官，且他们持有皮公文包，于是将他们连同汽车一并带往老闸捕房。

在捕房接受讯问后，查明他们的身份为：(1) 何伯钧（Ho Pah Chung），南京-上海卫戍司令总部参谋部少将；(2) 朱才杨（Tsu Zai Ling），上海市政府警察局督察，但以少校军衔作为联络官附属于南京-上海卫戍司令总部（此人驾驶汽车），以及一名勤务兵。

这些人未携带武器，公文包内装有少量私人信件及杂项洗漱用品，包括肥皂、牙刷、牙膏、面巾和几张账单。随后他们被护送至总部接受讯问并录取供词，但两人均无法提供关于上海周边中国军队部署或兵力的任何信息，他们坚称这些信息由卫戍司令严格保密。谭警司（Supt. Tan）认识这位联络官，知道他是上海市政府警察局的一名督察。两人均称他们是经由

I am an Inspector of the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau, holding warrant card No.312 (character
"Nai" ), issued on July 1, 1937 by the Bureau.
At 7 p.m. on August 24 I was instructed to proceed
to the front to obtain first hand information. In order
to accelerate the work I obtained the uniform of a Major
instead of my police uniform. I have in my possession
a "guest badge" issued by the Nanking-Shanghai Garrison
Commander's Headquarters.
At 8 p.m. on August 25 together with Mr. Ho Pah
Chung (何伯鈞), a staff officer attached to the Nanking-
Shanghai Garrison Commander's Headquarters, I returned
to Shanghai in motorcar No.17938. The motor car was driven
by me and was commandeered by the Military. We proceed-
ed along Chung San Road, Feng Ling Jao, Route Ghisi and
Avenue Edward VII arriving at the Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching
Road, at 9.40 p.m. the same day. We engaged room No.301
in the Hotel and passed the night there.
At 8.10 a.m. August 26 I accompanied Mr. Ho to the
Tai Wu Hospital, Lane 49, No.4 Yu Ya Ching Road, with the
motorcar, Mr. Ho suffering from a backache. Half an hour
later we left the hospital and proceeded to Nanking Road
with a view to doing some shopping there.
At the corner of Nanking and Chekiang Roads, our
motorcar, in an attempt to evade a collision with a motor-
cycle of the S.M.P. crashed into the wheel of a ricsha, and
the Foreign Sub-Inspector took us to the Louza Station.

August 25, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-

WAR TIME MILITARY LAW PROMULGATED BY GOVERNMENT

On August 24 the National Government
promulgated for immediate enforcement a set of war-time
military law immediately following its approval by the
Executive Yuan at its weekly meeting in the morning.
Drawn up by the Ministry of War, the new code
consists of 10 articles providing death punishment for:-
(1) Those who disobey orders and desert
strategic points without any reason thereby causing heavy
military losses on the Chinese army.
(2) Those who disobey orders and retreat from
their assigned posts.
(3) Those who linger behind despite orders to
advance or those who fail to defend designated points
thereby upsetting military plans and resulting in heavy
losses on the Chinese forces.
(4) Those who surrender to the enemy.
(5) Those who communicate with the enemy.
(6) Those who deliberately wreck or destroy
Chinese arms and ammunitions, rations, gunboats, airplanes,
munition dumps, workshops, aerodromes, dockyards, defence
works, and communication systems on behalf of the enemy.
(7) Those who foment mutinies or instigate
others to rebel.
(8) Those who disobey orders in face of the
advance of the enemy.
(9) Those who spread rumours with the intention
of breaking down the morale of the army or creating
disturbances in the rear.
(10) Those who permit their soldiers to loot or
rape.

·Promulgated at the same time was the following
set of Regulations for the enforcement of the War-Time
Military Law:-
Article 1: The War-Time Military Law shall be
applicable to both civilians and servicemen.
Article 2: Offenders against the War-Time
Military Law shall be tried by a military court in accord-
ance with the Law Governing the Trial of Members of the
Army, Navy and Air Force.
Article 3: Offenders against the War-Time
Military Law may be punished in accordance with the
Criminal Code for the Army, Navy and Air Force where the
offence in question is stipulated in the Code.
Article 4: All persons who commit offences not
mentioned in the War-Time Military Law shall be dealt with
in accordance with the Criminal Code for the Army, Navy and
Air Force.
Article 5: These Regulations and the War-Time
Military Law shall come into force as from August 24, 1937.

（批：sil ok 24/8）

1937年8月25日。下午译文。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

政府颁布战时军律

国民政府于8月24日晨间行政院例会批准后，立即颁布了一套战时军律，即刻生效。
该新法典由国防部起草，共10条，规定对以下行为处以死刑：-
(1) 无故违抗命令并放弃战略要地，从而导致中国军队遭受重大军事损失者。
(2) 违抗命令并从指定岗位撤退者。
(3) 尽管有前进命令仍滞留后方，或未能防守指定地点，从而扰乱军事计划并导致中国军队遭受重大损失者。
(4) 向敌人投降者。
(5) 与敌人通敌者。
(6) 代表敌人故意破坏或摧毁中国武器弹药、给养、炮艇、飞机、军火库、车间、机场、船坞、防御工事及通讯系统者。
(7) 煽动兵变或唆使他人反叛者。
(8) 在敌军进逼面前违抗命令者。
(9) 散布谣言意图瓦解军心或在后方制造骚乱者。
(10) 纵容士兵抢劫或强奸者。

·同时颁布了以下《战时军律施行条例》：-
第一条：战时军律适用于平民和军人。
第二条：违反战时军律者，应依照《陆海空军审判法》由军事法庭审判。
第三条：若所涉罪行在《陆海空军刑法》中有规定，违反战时军律者可依该法典处罚。
第四条：凡犯有战时军律未提及之罪行的人员，应依照《陆海空军刑法》处理。
第五条：本条例及战时军律自1937年8月24日起施行。

（批注：sil ok 24/8）

Chinese Chamber of Commerce - meeting

Nine committee members of the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce held a meeting in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road, between 11 p.m. and
12.30 p.m. August 23 and passed the following resolutions:-

1)That the proposal of the Silk and Satin Merchants
Association regarding the issue of special promissory
notes to be used by traders for purchase be referred to
the Ministry of Finance and Chinese Bankers and Native
Bankers' Associations for consideration.

2)That measures be devised to evacuate the employees of
member shops and factories who have been left in the
Eastern district.

On August 23, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce issued
a notice to the Hot Water Shop Owners' Association, Nantao
asking it to instruct its members to guard against the
traitors who are poisoning water being retailed by them.

Chinese Medical Practitioners' Association - activities

Members of the Chinese Medical Practitioners'
Association, Room 317, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward
VII, are visiting the various refugee shelters daily. The
inmates of 92 of these shelters benefit by these visits.

Union of Chinese Manufacturers requests removal of factories

On August 23, the Union of Chinese Manufacturers, No.4
Yung Chih Li, Yu Ya Ching Road, sent a telegram to the
Ministry of Finance requesting that factory owners be
instructed to remove their factories from Shanghai and
other coastal cities to the interior in order that production
be continued. The telegram also requests the Ministry to
instruct local bankers to extend all possible credit
facilities to the manufacturers.

主题：人力车车主协会——捐款及捐献人力车以支援中国军队。

Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

the offices and quarters of the N.W.K. situated at 931
Gordon Road are occupied by about 60 to 70 Japanese males,
civilians, who have been recognised as employees of the
N.W.K. mills in the Western district. Prior to the outbreak
of hostilities those N.W.K. employees were members of a
plain clothes corps. There are also ten Japanese females
living at the same address who are believed to be the wives
of members of the Japanese Branch of the Shanghai Municipal
Police and are the only females in the place.

The motor cars used by the inmates of the above place
licence Nos. 9029, 3080, 16439 and 409, run between the
Doong Shing Cotton Mill Quarters on Macao Road and 931
Gordon Road and go out and in all day. There are a number
of Japanese subjects, believed to be in the region of 100,
living in the quarters of the Doong Shing Mill Quarters,
but no females have been seen.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 26 AUG 1937）

From observation kept from the look out post of the
at 936 Gordon Rd.
U.S. Marines it was seen that the inmates of 931 Gordon
Road sit about in groups on the lawn and appear to do no
work. During the night lights were burning in a few of
the rooms of the houses, but nothing of a suspicious nature
was observed.

The license numbers mentioned above are all registered
in the name of Naigai Wata Kaisha.

Subject The Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works.

Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C Crawford D.I.

Further to this Section's report of August 20, I have
to report that due to a misunderstanding it was erroneously
stated that the Tien Yuen Electro & Chemical Works, 420
Brenan Road, is closely associated in business with the Far
East Oxygen & Acetylene Company, Ltd., 200 Route de Ziccawei.
This is incorrect, the business association referred to being
between the latter concern and the Tien Lee Synthetic Nitrogen
Products Company, Ltd., 207 Chen Ka Doo, which is under the
managership of Mr. Woo Yong Chu (also manager of the Tien
Yuen Electro & Chemical Works) and is situated on the north
side of the Soochow Creek opposite the Tien Yuen plant.
However, the error does not affect the main object of the
enquiries, for through Mr. Santerre's business connections
with the Tien Lee Nitrate Company he comes in close contact
with Mr. Woo Yong Chu whom he knows very well and whose
business integrity and high social standing, he states, is
beyond doubt. Mr. Santerre is quite prepared to guarantee
that poison gas is not produced in the Tien Yuen Electro
& Chemical Works, 420 Brenan Road.
On August 20, a certificate clearing the Tien Yuen Electro
& Chemical Works of all suspicion was signed by D.C. (Crime)
and forwarded to the local Japanese authorities through the
Secretariat since which date no attempt has been made by the
Japanese forces to interfere with the plant.

由副督察劳里尔（Laurier）撰写，由督察克劳福德（Crawford）转呈。

继本科8月20日的报告之后，兹报告称，由于误解，此前错误地陈述了位于布伦南路420号的天元电化厂与位于徐家汇路200号的远东氧气乙炔有限公司在业务上有密切关联。此说法不正确，所述的商业关联实际上是后者与位于陈家渡207号的天利合成氮肥产品有限公司之间的关联，该公司由吴永柱先生（亦为天元电化厂经理）管理，位于苏州河北岸，正对天元厂。然而，这一错误并不影响调查的主要目的，因为桑泰尔（Santerre）先生通过与天利硝酸公司的业务联系，与吴永柱先生保持着密切接触，他非常了解吴先生，并表示吴先生的商业诚信和崇高的社会地位毋庸置疑。桑泰尔先生完全愿意担保，位于布伦南路420号的天元电化厂不生产毒气。

REPORT
Date August 18, 1937.
Subject Local Chinese and Native Banks resume business.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I

Local Chinese and Native banks which suspended business
on August 13, reopened on August 17.
The Ministry of Finance has issued the following
instructions:-
1. A depositor is permitted to draw only 5% per week of
his total deposit. $150 is the maximum amount to be
drawn in one week.
2. Accounts opened after August 16, 1937, can be withdrawn.
3. Fixed deposits which were due on and after August 16
will be drawn in accordance with Item I mentioned above.
4. Persons in possession of fixed deposits can apply for
loans amounting to less than half of their deposits.
Fixed deposit books must be deposited with the banks
as a mortgage.
5. Other measures may be adopted when factories, business
firms and official organs draw money for the payment
of wages and to meet expenses in connection with
military affairs.
6. Banknotes are to be used for remittance purposes and
inter-bank transactions.
7. The above measures will be enforced until further
notice.
The Central Bank of China, The Bank of Communications
and The Bank of China, situated on or near The Bund have
established temporary offices at the Canidrom, Avenue du
Roi Albert, No.891 Avenue Joffre, and No.624 Avenue Joffre
respectively.

Sih Tse Liang
C. D. I.

Special Branch.

Removal of Soviet Consular Officials.

Information has been received from reliable sources that
at 2 a.m. on August 14, 1937 eight Soviet diplomatic officials,
members of the staff of local U.S.S.R. Consulate General, 24
Whangpoo Road, left the premises of the Consulate for 534 Avenue
Petain, Picardi Apts. and will occupy the flat of the Soviet
Vice-Consul M.A. Konstantinoff.

It is believed that U.S.S.R. Consulate General received
a warning from the Chinese Authorities of the proposed air
raid on the Japanese navy ships, anchored in the vicinity of
Consulate, and that the removal was the result of this warning.

SIX TRAITORS EXECUTED BY GARRISON COMMISSIONER'S
HEADQUARTERS

During the trial at the Military Court of the
Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters,
Chi Pah-hwa (計伯華) and five other Chinese traitors, who
were recently arrested by the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau, admitted that they had been engaged by the
Japanese authorities at a pay ranging from $16 to $20 to
spy on the military preparations of the Chinese authorities
and to create disturbances at the rear. They were
executed yesterday morning by the Garrison Commissioner's
Headquarters.

Subject Japanese Military Activities.
Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Prince

Sir,
On July 16, 1937, Mr. Zung Tsung Chih (鄭貞吉),
Member of the General Staff of Nanking Government stationed
in Shanghai, came to C.B.H.Q. C.I. and made the following
report :-
On the night of July 13, 1937, the Japanese S.S.
"Aso Maru" arrived at Wayside Wharf from Japan with eight
15 c.m. Field Guns, which were immediately transported to the
Japanese Military Headquarters, Kiangwan Road. Five hundred
pigeons and one hundred dogs used for military purposes are
also secretly kept at their Headquarters on Kiangwan Road.
It is believed that preparations are aimed at the
City Government should a war break out.
At 4 a.m. everyday the Japanese marines assemble at
a primary school on Range Road, where they are busily engaged
in surveying and estimating the distance the Chinese can fire
a field gun from Chinese Territory to destroy their military
base in an attack on the Japanese Headquarters.
Enquiries show that the local Chinese Authorities
seem to be somewhat perturbed over the situation in the North
and fear any incident that may result in hostilities locally.
There are no Chinese soldiers in Kiangwan district,
neither have they any artillery or field pieces in the district.

（左侧批注：）
* Chinese buildings have no insulation to shut this field
* This is no reason they have a flag on top of dirt on top of their barracks
DC.

先生，
1937年7月16日，驻上海的南京政府参谋本部成员郑贞吉（Zung Tsung Chih）先生来到刑事科总部首席督察处，作了如下报告：
1937年7月13日晚，日本轮船“阿苏丸”号（Aso Maru）从日本抵达外码头（Wayside Wharf），载有八门15厘米野战炮，这些火炮随即被运往江湾路的日本军事总部。五百只用于军事目的的鸽子和一百只狗也秘密饲养在他们位于江湾路的总部。
据信，这些准备工作是针对市政府的，以防战争爆发。
每天凌晨4时，日本海军陆战队在兰路（Range Road）的一所小学集合，忙于勘测和估算中国军队从中国领土发射野战炮摧毁其位于日本总部的军事基地的距离。
调查显示，当地中国当局似乎对北方局势感到有些不安，担心任何可能导致本地敌对行动的事件。
江湾地区没有中国士兵，该地区也没有任何火炮或野战炮。

（左侧批注：）
* 中国建筑没有隔热材料来阻挡这种野战
* 这不是他们在营房顶上的泥土上插旗的理由

Subject Reply from General Yang Hu through Col. L.P. Sung re request of Crime Branch Headquarters to receive looters or loafers arrested by S.M.P. for war service at the front.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Colonel L.P. Sung telephoned on September 26, 1937,
to state that with reference to the request made to General Yang Hu
or his representative by Crime Branch Headquarters ( ? C.1)
for the Military Authorities to take into custody looters or
loafers arrested in the Settlement
General Yang Hu instructs Col. Sung to reply that the
request cannot be entertained. The repatriation of these
unemployed people should be, he points out, undertaken by the
various circles Relief Association (organised by Messrs Pan Kung
Chan, Tu Yueh Sung and members of Tangpu) with an office in
the Pootung Guild.

Referring to the enquiry as to the possibility
of the Chinese Government releasing prisoners serving short
terms of imprisonment from gaol, General Yang Hu wishes to be
understood that this matter will have to be referred to the
Executive Yuan.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Crime & Special Branches)

G.A. to D.C. (Crime)

关于中国政府是否可能释放服刑期较短的在押囚犯的询问，杨虎将军希望明确说明，此事必须提交行政院处理。

Enquiries ascertained that Lieu Tah Foo frightened
absconded during the arrest of the 7 accused. Efforts
will be made to locate him. His wife Lieu I Sz
questioned, stated he supplied matting to Japanese,
to the Dong Shing Cotton Mill about 4 or 5 months ago
but had not dealt with them recently. She heard the
7 accused demand $800.00 from her husband. The 5th
accused was in possession of exhibit "A" and the 3rd
accused attempted to destroy exhibit "B" on the way
to the station.

Vice Captain Yang Voong Zien of Shanghai Woosung
Garrison Authorities called to the station failed to
identify the accused and state he had not given them
instructions to arrest any person at 87 Tsang Ka Zah
Road. It is obvious that the accused, representing
themselves to be Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Authorities
officers, attempted to extort $800.00 from Lieu Tah Foo
using the exhibits or documents to make him believe
they had written authority and a warrant. Vice Captain
Yang Voong Zien requested that the 7 accused be handed
over to Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Authorities.

Hsia Ta Sung,
Honan,
11 a.m.          5/9/37,          D.S.I. Van Teh Foo,
                                 translated Interpreter Shen.

My name is Hsia Ta Sung, age 31, native of Honan,
M/unemployed, residing at 447 Heng Foong Road, Chapei. I
was an aide-de-camp attached to the 3rd Regiment 5th Battalion
of the Gendarmerie in Szechuen. Having retired during last
November I returned to Shanghai and took abode at the afore-
mentioned address. Since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities on 13/8/37 I left my home and went to live in
a room (No. 26) in the Chun Nan Lodging House on Avenue Road.
At about 10 a.m. on the 4/9/37 my friend Feng Tsen, who was
formerly working in the Intelligence Department of the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau (S.C.G.P.B.), and was dismissed
for being an opium addict, visited me at the above mentioned
lodging house stating that he had received information from
his informer that there was a traitor named Chiu Nyung Chuen
(邱民根) living at No. 87 Tsang Ka Zah Road. He further
stated that he would report it to Yang Ming Chi, a Detective
Sub-Inspector attached to the Shanghai Woosung Garrison
Headquarters. At 8 p.m. even date, after having communi-
cated with Yang Ming Chi, Feng Tsen, together with his two
friends one named Loh and the other named Hiao, took me to
Wen Zian Bath-house where on arrival we met Yang Ming Chi.
Feng Tsen asked Yang Ming Chi to prepare an official document
for the purpose of requesting assistance from the S.M.P. in
effecting the arrest of the wanted man. Yang said that it
would be better to induce him into the Chinese territory and
then put him under arrest. We then departed. At 8 a.m.
5/9/37, I accompanied by Wen Cha Ming, Yang Kwai Fu, Feng Tsen

河南，
上午11时          1937年9月5日，          副督察范德福（Van Teh Foo，音译），
                                 翻译员沈（Shen）。

我叫谢大生，31岁，河南人，男/无业，居住在闸北恒丰路447号。我曾任四川宪兵第五团第三营的副官。去年十一月退役后回到上海，居住在上述地址。自1937年8月13日中日敌对行动爆发以来，我离开家，住在爱文义路春南旅馆（Chun Nan Lodging House，音译）的一个房间（26号）。1937年9月4日上午10时左右，我的朋友冯森（Feng Tsen，音译）来访，他此前在上海市政府警察局情报部门工作，后因吸食鸦片被开除。他在上述旅馆告诉我，他从线人处得知，有一名名为邱民根（Chiu Nyung Chuen，此处中文名与上文邱仰川不同，照实译出）的汉奸住在张家宅路87号。他还表示，他将向上海吴淞警备司令部总部附属的侦探副督察杨明基（Yang Ming Chi，音译）报告此事。当晚8时，在与杨明基联系后，冯森带着他的两个朋友，一个姓陆，另一个姓萧，带我去了文贤浴室（Wen Zian Bath-house，音译），我们在那里见到了杨明基。冯森请杨明基准备一份官方文件，以便请求工部局警务处协助逮捕这名通缉犯。杨说，最好将其诱入华界，然后实施逮捕。随后我们离开。1937年9月5日上午8时，我与文查明（Wen Cha Ming，音译）、杨桂福（Yang Kwai Fu，音译）、冯森

pages.en:
(sheet No. 2)

Loh, Siao and the informer whose name is unknown to me,
proceeded to No. 87 Tsang Ka Zah Road. We waited outside the
premises and half an hour later we saw Chiu Nyung Chuen come
out to buy some food. We approached him and on being asked to
go along with us Chiu Nyung Chuen replied that he would enter
the house to put some clothing on his person and then accompany
us to wherever we wanted to go. Loh and the informer followed
Chiu into the house while we, four in number, remained outside.
Half an hour later when we entered the house with the intention
to bring them out we simultaneously encountered detectives
who placed us in their custody and brought all concerned to
Sinza Station. The above is my true statement.
sd. Hsia Ts Sung.
pages.zh:
（第2页）

陆、萧以及一名姓名不详的线人，前往张家宅路87号。我们在屋外等候，半小时后，我们看到邱民根出来买食物。我们走近他，当要求他随我们走时，邱民根回答说他要进屋穿些衣服，然后陪我们去任何我们要去的地方。陆和线人跟随邱进入屋内，而我们四人留在外面。半小时后，当我们进入屋内打算将他们带出时，同时遇到了便衣侦探，他们将我们拘押，并将所有相关人员带到新闸路巡捕房。以上是我的真实供词。

由副督察劳里尔（Laurier）制作，由督察克劳福德（C. Crawford）转发。

1937年9月5日上午10时05分，以下人员在爱文义路张家宅87号被博迪（Boddy）督察及配属新闸路巡捕房的人员逮捕，罪名为企图勒索和非法冒充：
(1) 邱仰川（Chiu Nyung Chuen），已婚，无业，54岁，徐州人，居住在新闸路霍贵里（Ho Kwei Lee，音译）210号。非“青年学生救国团”成员。
(2) 胡鸿宾（Woo Hung Ping），已婚，无业，34岁，扬州人，居住在爱德华七世路近重庆路处，系上海市政府警察局新闸分局侦探刘恒（Liu Heng）的线人。非“青年学生救国团”成员。
(3) 温永冰（Wen Yung Ping，与前文温应平名字略有差异，照实译出），单身，无业，25岁，四川人，居住在南市西门关帝庙。系“青年学生救国团”成员。
(4) 萧中立（Siao Chun Lih），失业教师，29岁，金波（Kompo，音译）人，居住在阿尔伯特国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）。非“青年学生救国团”成员。
(5) 陈斌（Zung Ping），已婚，无业，28岁，四川人，居住在南市西门关帝庙。非“青年学生救国团”成员。
(6) 陆海（Loh Hai Chong，此处中文名简写，照实译出），已婚，无业，30岁，扬州人，无固定住所。

（印：1937年9月6日 政治部）
（批：S.1. 进一步备注 1939年3月2日。）

Complainant is a female named Loo Yih Sze (羅葉氏),
who resides at 87 Tsang Kah Zah, Avenue Road with her husband,
one Loo Teh Foo (羅德夫), who, until three months ago was
employed in contracting for the sale to the Doong Shing Cotton
Mill, a Japanese concern at 2068 Yangtszepoo Road, of bamboo
mats which he obtained through a middleman named Chiu Nyung
Chuen (1st accused).
At about 9 a.m. September 5, the seven accused went
to the house of the complainant. The 1st accused told her
that on the commencement of hostilities he was on his way to
her home with a truckload of bamboo mats for her husband when,
whilst still in Chinese territory, he had been arrested by the
Woosung
City Government Police who had handed him over to the/Shanghai
Garrison Commander's Office on a charge of being a traitor
and dealing with the enemy (Japanese), and that in order to
escape the penalty of death he had been obliged to pay $1,100.00
in bribes. A general discussion then took place during which

all but the 1st accused told complainant that her husband
was to be arrested and charged for being a traitor and that
they, being members of the Woosung Shanghai Garrison
Commander's Headquarters were authorized to arrest him.
A sum of $200.00 was also demanded of her. At this stage
the 5th accused produced a letter (translation attached),
purporting to have been chopped by the Young Students'
Racial Salvation Group and addressed to himself, stating
that one Chiu Nyung Chuen (the 1st accused), had on ~~and~~ 12th
August, 1937, transported to the Japanese Army a large
quantity of property for military use, and that being a
traitor, he should be arrested and dealt with in accordance
with the regulations issued by the Shanghai Political Organs.
This letter was shown to the complainant as proof of their
assertions.
    Although the accused all deny the charges, it would
appear from investigations that the accused meant to imply
that having arrested the 1st accused for the offence of
supplying the Japanese Military Authorities with material
for military use, they were desirous of arresting his
accomplice, i.e. complainant's husband. No doubt the 1st
accused voluntarily acted the part of an accused person in
order to lend conviction to the charge involving complainant's
husband.
    The complainant, suspecting the trick, thereupon
summoned C.D.C.135 of Sinza Station, who lives in the same
house. C.D.C.135 asked the accused to produce their Warrant
Cards and being unable to do so, then stated that they were
acting on the instructions of Inspector Yang Fong Chih

除第一被告外，所有人都告诉报案人，她的丈夫将被逮捕并被指控为汉奸，而他们作为吴淞上海卫戍司令部的成员，有权逮捕他。他们还向她索要200.00元。此时，第五被告出示了一封信（附译文），声称盖有青年学生救亡团的印章，并写给他本人，信中指出邱荣泉（即第一被告）曾于~~和~~1937年8月12日向日军运送大量军用物资，因其身为汉奸，应根据上海政治机关发布的规章予以逮捕和处理。这封信被出示给报案人，作为他们说法的证据。
    尽管所有被告均否认指控，但调查显示，被告似乎意在暗示，既然他们已因向日本军方提供军用物资的罪行逮捕了第一被告，他们希望逮捕其同伙，即报案人的丈夫。毫无疑问，第一被告自愿扮演被告角色，以使涉及报案人丈夫的指控更具说服力。
    报案人识破此诡计，随即召来同住该屋的新闸捕房刑事侦缉队第135号警员。刑事侦缉队第135号警员要求被告出示委任证，因被告无法出示，便称他们是奉吴淞上海卫戍司令部杨凤池 (Yang Fong Chih) 巡捕之命行事。

Not being aware of the C.D.C.'s occupation, the accused
repeated their demands to him, whereupon he placed the
accused under arrest and informed Sinza with the result
already related.
        Whilst escorting the seven men to the Station
detectives discovered the 5th accused in the act of
destroying a school certificate in his name bearing a large
official looking chop which it is suspected he had originally
intended to produce as a Warrant of Arrest, though it could
not have born close scrutiny.
        Inspector Yang Fong Chih came to Sinza Station shortly
after the arrest of the accused and denied that he had given
any of the accused authority to arrest anyone in the Settlement
and furthermore denied all knowledge of the two documents
referred to above.
        D.I. Boddy explained the circumstances of the case to
the D.O. "B" Division with whose permission it was arranged
that the seven accused would appear before the Shanghai First
Special District Court on September 6, when Inspector Yang
Fong Chih would make application for their handing over to
the Woosung Shanghai Garrison Commander's Headquarters to
be dealt with.
        As regards the Young Students' Racial Salvation Group,
there is every indication that if such a society does really
exist it is of mushroom growth, without organization or
proper leadership, is unregistered with the Chinese Authorities
and though formed on the outbreak of local hostilities there
has as yet been no formal meeting of inauguration. According

        在护送七人前往捕房途中，侦探发现第五被告正在销毁一张以其名义开具、盖有一枚看似官方大印的学校证书。据怀疑，他原本打算将此证书作为逮捕令出示，尽管它经不起仔细查验。
        杨凤池巡捕在被告被捕后不久来到新闸捕房，否认他曾授权任何被告在租界内逮捕任何人，并且进一步否认对上述两份文件有任何了解。

to three of the accused who claim to be members of the
Group the objects of the Society are :-
(1) To recruit men for the Army.
(2) To enroll those unfit for active service in relief
work behind the lines.
The following names were obtained :-
President : Tsao Kang Nyi (趙岡毅)
Vice President: Liang Dong-faung (梁桐芳)
Committee members: Fan Reu Liang (范仁良)
Fan Tien Chin (范天九).
No membership fees have so far been collected by

The offices of the Group are stated to be situated
in the Kwan Tih Miao, Zau Chiao Road, West Gate, Nantao,
where the above mentioned members are all at present living.
This "Society" is not to be confused with the Shanghai
Youths' National Salvation Service Group which was also
located in the Kwan Tih Miao and assisted the Chinese
Authorities in searching pedestrians and suspicious
characters until August 20, on which date the members were
disbanded on the instructions of the Chinese Authorities
and ordered to carry out first aid work.
So far as has been ascertained there is not a branch
of the former Group in the Settlement.
Further enquiries are proceeding.

1

Re. male Chinese arrested for Looting.

At 8.30a.m. 31-8-37, F.S. Wells, No. 257, escorted
to Bubbling Well Station a male Chinese named Wu Pah
Tsung (吴伯春 ), age 33 years, native of Hupeh, whom
the former mentioned Police Officer arrested on Jessfield
Road Railway Crossing at 8a.m. even date in possession
of 6 silver ornaments (broken), 1 silver serviette ring,
1 silver hand mirror and 5 silver shields.

Subsequent enquiries ascertained that Wu Pah Tsung
(who incidently when arrested was attired in civilian
clothes) is a cook attached to the 88th. Route Army and
he alleges that the above mentioned silver was handed
to him by another Chinese soldier who instructed the
former to proceed into the International Settlement and
exchange the silver for vegetables.

The defendant and property, together with a
Chinese charge sheet explaining the full details, when
and how arrested, etc. will be handed over to the
Chinese Authorities at 3p.m. 31-8-37.

Statement attached and finger printed.

Senior Detective i/c.

关于一名因抢劫被捕的中国男子。

1937年8月31日上午8时30分，福生 Wells (F.S. Wells，编号257) 将一名名叫吴伯春 (Wu Pah Tsung) 的中国男子护送至静安寺捕房。该男子33岁，湖北籍。前述警官于同日早上8时在极司菲尔路铁路道口将其逮捕，当时他持有6件银饰（破损）、1个银餐巾环、1面银手镜和5个银盾。
后续调查查明，吴伯春（顺便提一下，被捕时身着便服）是第八十八路军的一名炊事员，他声称上述银器是另一名中国士兵交给他的，该士兵指示他进入国际租界，用银器交换蔬菜。
被告及财物，连同详细说明逮捕时间、方式等情况的中文起诉书，将于1937年8月31日下午3时移交中国当局。
附陈述书并按有指纹。

高级侦探主管。
R. Lynstone

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wu Pah Tsung ( )
native of Hupeh taken by me C.D.C. 278
at Bowell Station on the 31-8-37 and interpreted by D.S.I. T'ang Tzu Hung

States:
I reside in Bang Pu Village and at present am employed
as a cook in the 52nd. and 53rd. Battalion of the 83th. Division
(Chinese Army). At 4a.m. 31-8-37, another soldier gave me a
parcel of silver ware and instructed me to proceed into the
International Settlement and exchange same for vegetables.
At about 8a.m. even date, whilst on the above mentioned
mission, I was arrested on Jessfield Road Railway Crossing by a
foreign Policeman. I did not steal the silverware.

Signed and crossed marked by
Wu Pah Tsung.

At about 8 a.m. 30-8-37, two Customs examiners named Yung Wen Hoon (杨文龙) & Staud Lo Ying Chiu (杨云之) of SCD, arrested two men named Yao Tao (姚桃), 49, and Chiang Ka Hong, (蒋乾坤), 36, Tung-chow, Shanghai, in possession of four rolls of calico, marked by the Nippon Weaving Co, Pootung, suspected of having smuggled same.

Enquiries by Det. Bretherton revealed that the two named accused had yesterday 29-8-37 gone over to Pootung and purchased the four rolls of calico (door) for $16.00, namely, $4.00 per roll, the bag of opium, about 7 lbs. they allege was given to them.

With reference to the report contained in this file
of a male Chinese arrested at 21 Amoy Road 9.20 p.m.
28-8-37 and afterwards handed over to the S.C.G.P.B. in
connection with the firing of a flare on Amoy Road,
Mr. Liu Hwai, Chief of Detectives S.C.G.P.B. sent the
following letter and result of interrogations of the
suspect:-
To C.D.I. Sharman
Louza Station. 30-8-37.

Dear Sir,
with reference to the Chinese traitor
Sze Wei Eng (施為恩) handed over to the
Detective Department of the S.C.G. Police Bureau
together with exhibits of three signal bamboo
tubes by your station yesterday, we beg to
inform you that the said person Sze Wei Eng,
after having been carefully interrogated by
this Department, has been found to be definitely
a Chinese traitor enticed with money by the
enemy.
We have already escorted the said
traitor Sze Wei Eng together with the exhibits
to the Shanghai & Woosung Garrison Commissioner's
Headquarters for their discretion.
We enclose herewith a copy of our
interrogations on the said traitor for your
perusal.

I am, Sir,
Yours, etc.
Liu Hwai
Chief of Detective Dept.
S. C. G. P. B.

Translation of interrogations of Sze Wei Eng at the
Detective Department of the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau.

Sze Wei Eng, age 58, native of Tungchow, residing at 21
Amoy Road, employed as a handtrolley coolie.

关于本卷宗内所载报告，一名中国男子于1937年8月28日晚上9时20分在厦门路21号被捕，随后因涉及在厦门路发射信号弹一事被移交给上海市公安局（S.C.G.P.B.），上海市公安局侦缉处处长刘怀先生发来以下信函及对该嫌疑人的审讯结果：-
致刑事侦缉督察夏曼（Sharman）
老闸捕房。1937年8月30日。

敬启者，
关于昨日由贵局移交给上海市公安局侦缉处的中国汉奸施为恩（Sze Wei Eng）以及三根信号竹管等证物，谨此通知阁下，经本部门仔细审讯，该人施为恩确系受敌人金钱诱骗的中国汉奸。
我们已将该汉奸施为恩连同证物押送至上海吴淞区戒严司令部，由其酌情处理。
随函附上我们对上述汉奸的审讯记录副本，供阁下查阅。

此致
敬礼
刘怀
侦缉处处长
上海市公安局

上海市政府警察局侦缉处对施为恩的审讯译文。

施为恩，58岁，通州人，住厦门路21号，职业为手推车苦力。

问：谁给了你这根信号竹管？

pages.en:
"A"
Misc:562/37.         Leung
                     August, 31st.    37.
19 (3/sheet 2)

A. This signal bamboo tube was given to me by one named
   Zung Lau Sai.
Q. What nativity is Zung Lau Sai and where he stays?
A. Zung Lau Sai is a native of Kangteh and resides in a
   house next to a lodging house situated on Amoy Road.
Q. How you took the signal bamboo tube to your home?
A. Zung Lau Sai advised me to put the signal bamboo
   together with a bundle of fire weed and then conveyed
   to my home.
Q. When you took this signal bamboo to your home?
A. At about 4 p.m. yesterday (28-8-37).
Q. For what purpose did Zung Lau Sai ask you to take the
   signal bamboo to your home?
A. Zung Lau Sai told me that can use same to frighten
   some-one and also to frighten the aeroplane.
Q. How much did Zung Lau Sai give for your sending the
   signal?
A. Zung Lau Sai did not speak to me about the money.
Q. You say Zung Lau Sai did not mention about money, then
   why you ask Keng Hai Heu to send the signal and gave
   him ten coppers?
A. There was no such happening, it was implicated by Kong
   Hai Heu.
Q. Are you still trying to deny when all witnesses and
   evidences against you are obtained?
A. -------- No definite answer.
                     Dated 29-8-37.

"A"
杂项:562/37。         Leung
                     1937年8月31日。
19 (3/第2页)

答：这根信号竹管是一个名叫钟留西（Zung Lau Sai）的人给我的。
问：钟留西是哪里人？住在哪里？
答：钟留西是康德（Kangteh）人，住在厦门路一家旅馆旁边的一所房子里。
问：你是怎么把信号竹管拿回家的？
答：钟留西建议我把信号竹管和一堆火草捆在一起，然后运回我家。
问：你什么时候把这根信号竹管拿回家的？
答：昨天（1937年8月28日）下午4点左右。
问：钟留西让你把信号竹管拿回家有什么目的？
答：钟留西告诉我，可以用它来吓唬某人，也可以用来吓唬飞机。
问：钟留西给你多少钱让你发送信号？
答：钟留西没跟我提钱的事。
问：你说钟留西没提钱，那你为什么让耿海厚（Keng Hai Heu）去发信号，还给了他十个铜板？
答：没有这回事，是孔海厚（Kong Hai Heu）诬陷我。
问：在所有针对你的证人和证据都齐全的情况下，你还想抵赖吗？
答：-------- 无明确回答。

刑事侦缉督察夏曼（Sharman）随后将详情告知 "A" 区警务总监罗伯逊（Robertson）先生，后者指示将第一嫌疑人施为恩（Sz Wei King）移送西区边界以外，并释放第二嫌疑人江海候（Kong Hoi Hou）。

Subject....................Handing over of alleged "traitors" to Chinese Authorities.

Made by....................and....................Forwarded by....Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Enquiries made by detectives at Hongkew Station
elicit that the Tomiya Shirts Shop does not exist at 302
Woosung Road. It is a barber shop at this address.
Enquiries at Louza show that Peu Siao Mow(潘小毛),
age 16, and Peu Foo Hai(潘富海), age 30, were handed over to
detectives of the Police Bureau (not Woosung-Shanghai Garrison
Commander) shortly after they were brought in. The Chief
Detective, Mr. Liu Hwa, having received information of the
arrest, applied for the handing over.
From investigations made by the detective department
of the Police Bureau under Mr. Liu Hwa, it appears that Peu Siao
Mow, 1st named, stated that he had been given the printed paper
by his brother Peu Foo Hai (?) to be put on the trucks. When
questioned the elder brother stated that he received the paper
from one Zang Tse Kiu Sz(常七九子), native of Kompo, age about 40, a
follower of Koo Sz(顧四) garbage contractor of Chapei, Sinza
Tao, and ricsha owner by profession. He is known to detectives
of the Police Bureau as living in an alleyway behind the New
World and opposite the Sun Company, Yu Ya Ching Road.
An attempt was made to arrest him by Police Bureau
detectives with the cooperation of S.M.P. (?) on the night of
August 30 without success and it is believed that a watch is
being maintained at the address by the same detectives.

（印：FILED SEP. 1937）

虹口捕房警探进行的查询查明，吴淞路302号并无富家衬衫店（Tomiya Shirts Shop）。该地址是一家理发店。
老闸捕房的查询显示，潘小毛（Peu Siao Mow），16岁，和潘富海（Peu Foo Hai），30岁，在被带入后不久即被移交给警察局（非吴淞-上海戒严司令部）的警探。首席侦探刘华（Liu Hwa）先生在获悉逮捕情况后，申请移交。
根据刘华先生领导下警察局侦缉处的调查，第一嫌疑人潘小毛称，这些印刷纸条是他的兄弟潘富海（？）给他的，让他放在卡车上。经讯问，兄长称他从常七九子（Zang Tse Kiu Sz）处收到纸条，此人约40岁，康波（Kompo）人，是闸北新闸头垃圾承包商顾四（Koo Sz）的追随者，职业为黄包车车主。警察局警探知道他就住在虞洽卿路新世界后面、先施公司对面的一条弄堂里。
8月30日晚，警察局警探在工部局警务处（?）的配合下试图逮捕他，但未成功，据信同一批警探正在该地址进行监视。

Sir,
The two Chinese named Wong Hsu Tsang ( 汪秀章 ) and
Tong Sing Yue ( 湯星有 ) who were arrested in the Sinza
District by detectives attached to Sinza at 6.30 p.m. on August
20, 1937 at the instance of the Shanghai City Government Police
Bureau were brought before the S.S.D.Court on the morning of
August 21, on an application for a writ of detention. In view
of the fact that they had been implicated by one Ying Ah Kung
( 印阿根 ) in the custody of the City Government Police
Bureau as being concerned with him in allegedly poisoning
street tea urns the court ordered that they be handed over to
the Chinese authorities.

Enquiries made by Supt. Tan, Special Branch, ascertain
that all three men were held in the custody of the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau, until the morning of 23-8-37
when they were handed over to the Martial Law Commander's Office,
Chiengkee Road, Lunghwa. Here they will be tried by Court
Martial and in all probability will be executed at the command
of this tribunal.

The circumstances surrounding this case, as will be seen
from previous reports on the subject, fail to establish the guilt
of either the person arrested by the Police Bureau or his two
friends who were arrested in the Settlement as a consequence of
a confession exacted from him.

In another report I hope to be able to show that although
many alleged poisoning cases have come to light in the Settlement
and notwithstanding that one of the suspects confessed to being
engaged in distributing poisonous cakes, there is as yet no
proof forthcoming to convince the S.M.Police that the persons

Subject Assistance rendered to Shanghai City Government Police Bureau.
Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by C. Cranston. A.D.

At 6.30 p.m. August 20, on instructions from C.D.I.
Ross, D.S. Lockwood and C.D.C. 360 (Special Branch)
accompanied D.S.I. Taylor (Sinza) and detectives of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, Nantao, and
arrested two Chinese named (1) Wong Hsu Tsang(汪許章) and
(2) Tong Sing Yue(湯成月), who had been implicated by
one already in custody.
When questioned the men corroborated each other's
statements to the effect that they were employed by a
Japanese concern in Chapei. They, however, denied the
allegation that they had been engaged by the Japanese to
poison tea urns. They stated that they were unemployed
as a result of the Sino-Japanese hostilities and that
since August 14th, they had been residing in the Settlement.
The impression gained by detectives is that this is a

1937年8月20日下午6时30分，奉首席督察长 Ross 指示，侦探长 Lockwood 和特务处首席侦探主任 360 号陪同新闸区副督察长 Taylor 及上海市政府警察局南市分局的侦探，逮捕了两名华人，分别为 (1) 汪許章（Wong Hsu Tsang）和 (2) 湯成月（Tong Sing Yue），此二人已被一名已在押人员牵连。
经讯问，两人的供词相互印证，称他们受雇于闸北的一家日本商号。然而，他们否认了受日本人雇佣在茶桶中投毒的指控。他们表示，由于中日敌对行动，他们处于失业状态，且自8月14日以来一直居住在租界内。
侦探们得到的印象是，这是中国当局故意陷害无辜华人为汉奸的行为。

侦探长 Lockwood.
侦探长。

副处长（特务处） 刑事侦缉处副处长

being handed over to Nantao Chinese Authorities, on the
authority of Mr. Robertson, D.O."A"

At 5.40.p.m. 21-8-37, F.S.303 Nadeyeff and C.P.C.
296 arrested one named Tseh Lah Sai (趙老三), 38,Wusih,
S/unemployed, N.F.A. on Fokien Road Bridge, who was in
possession of a book, entitled "Present Day Impressions
of THE EAST at Home & Abroad." Suspecting him of having
looted same.
pages.zh:
12/3.

1937年8月21日下午5时30分，巡官（F.S.）303号 Nadeyeff 和警长（C.P.C.）2637号在福建路桥逮捕了一名名为姜子海（Chiang Tai Hai）的男子，21岁，丹阳人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.），当时其持有一台留声机，涉嫌抢劫所得。

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）237号和侦探警司（D.S.）Bretherton 调查，情况如下：嫌疑人在被问及如何获得该留声机时称，是一名不知名的广东男子在靠近市场的北河南路乘坐人力车时送给他的。

鉴于目前北河南路并无居民居住，且该地区实际上已禁止行人通行，人力车夫也不在此区域揽客，根据“A”区副督察长（D.O. "A"）Robertson 先生的指示，嫌疑人将于1937年8月22日上午10时被送往宾乍路巡捕房（Binza Station），以便移交给南市中国当局。

1937年8月21日下午5时40分，巡官（F.S.）303号 Nadeyeff 和警长（C.P.C.）296号在福建路桥逮捕了一名名为趙老三（Tseh Lah Sai）的男子，38岁，无锡人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.），当时其持有一本名为《东西方印象录》（Present Day Impressions of THE EAST at Home & Abroad）的书籍，涉嫌抢劫所得。

pages.en:
12/4.

Enquiries by C.D.S. 7 and D.S. Bretherton. Suspect
when questioned denied having looted the above described
book, but stated that he had purchased the book for
$1.50 from a second hand hawker on North Haining Road.
In view of the fact that at present there are no
second hand dealers operating in the vicinity of North
Haining Road together with the fact that suspect cannot
read English, in which language the book, an encyclopedia,
is printed, he will, on instructions of the D.O. "A" Mr.
Robertson, be sent to Sinsa Station preparatory to being
handed over to the Nantao Chinese Authorities for
disposal.

At 7.p.m. 21-8-37, F.S.305 Madeyeff and C.P.C.295
arrested two named Eung Zai Fong (郑瑞芳), 30, Ningpo,
S/unemployed, N.F.A. and Ting Sou San (丁秀山) 34, Che-
kiang, S/unemployed, N.F.A., 1st. named was in possession
of 34 pieces of crockery and a quantity of clothing,
2nd. named possessed three table clothes and one towel,
both of whom are suspected of having stolen same.

Enquiries by C.D.C.162 and D.S. Bretherton. 1st.
named, when questioned stated that he had taken the
above mentioned articles from the ruins of a devastated
dwelling on Haining Road. 2nd. named stated that he
bought the articles, in his possession, from a hawker
for 20 cents on North Honan Road.
pages.zh:
12/4.

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.S.）7号和侦探警司（D.S.）Bretherton 调查。嫌疑人在受审时否认抢劫上述书籍，但称其是在北海宁路从一名二手小贩处以1.50元的价格购买的。鉴于目前北海宁路附近并无二手商贩经营，且嫌疑人不懂英文，而该书（一部百科全书）正是用英文印刷的，根据“A”区副督察长（D.O. "A"）Robertson 先生的指示，他将被送往新闸路巡捕房（Sinsa Station），以便移交给南市中国当局处理。

1937年8月21日晚上7时，巡官（F.S.）305号 Madeyeff 和警长（C.P.C.）295号逮捕了两名男子，分别名为郑瑞芳（Eung Zai Fong），30岁，宁波人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.）；以及丁秀山（Ting Sou San），34岁，浙江人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.）。前者持有34件瓷器和一批衣物，后者持有三块桌布和一条毛巾，两人均涉嫌盗窃上述物品。

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）162号和侦探警司（D.S.）Bretherton 调查。第一名嫌疑人在受审时称，上述物品是从海宁路一处被毁房屋的废墟中拿走的。第二名嫌疑人称，其持有的物品是在北河南路以20美分的价格从一名小贩处购买的。

pages.en:
12/5.

Both the above named suspects on instructions of
Mr. Robertson D.O."A" will be sent to Sinsa Station at
10.a.m. on the morning of the 22-8-37 preparatory to
being handed over to Nantao Chinese Authorities for
disposal.

At 7.p.m. 21-8-37, P.S.332 Hargreaves and C.P.C.294
arrested one named Wong Yui Zai (王有才), 36, Yangchow,
s/unemployed, N.F.A. on Chekiang Road Bridge in posses-
sion of three lengths of calico, one axe and one chopping
block, suspected of having looted same.

Enquiries by C.D.S.164 and D.S. Bretherton.
Suspect when questioned admitted having looted the above
mentioned articles from a deserted dwelling house situa-
ted on North Haining Road at about 5.p.m. 21-8-37.

Suspect on instructions of Mr. Robertson D.O."A"
will be handed over at 10.a.m. on the morning of the
22-8-37 preparatory to be handed over to the Nantao
Chinese Authorities.

At 8.45.p.m. 21-8-37, C.P.C.1635 attached Louza
Station arrested one named Li Sang Yuan (李長源) 16,
Ningpo, s/unemployed, N.F.A. on Fukien Road Bridge in
possession of six articles of clothing, suspected of
having looted same.
pages.zh:
12/5.

根据“A”区副督察长（D.O. "A"）Robertson 先生的指示，上述两名嫌疑人将于1937年8月22日上午10时被送往新闸路巡捕房（Sinsa Station），以便移交给南市中国当局处理。

1937年8月21日晚上7时，巡官（P.S.）332号 Hargreaves 和警长（C.P.C.）294号在浙江路桥逮捕了一名名为王有才（Wong Yui Zai）的男子，36岁，扬州人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.），当时其持有三匹白布、一把斧头和一个砧板，涉嫌抢劫所得。

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.S.）164号和侦探警司（D.S.）Bretherton 调查。嫌疑人在受审时承认，于1937年8月21日下午5时左右，从北海宁路一处无人居住的房屋中抢劫了上述物品。

根据“A”区副督察长（D.O. "A"）Robertson 先生的指示，嫌疑人将于1937年8月22日上午10时被移交，以便转交给南市中国当局。

1937年8月21日晚上8时45分，隶属老闸巡捕房（Louza Station）的警长（C.P.C.）1635号在福建路桥逮捕了一名名为李長源（Li Sang Yuan）的男子，16岁，宁波人，无业，非上海籍居民（N.F.A.），当时其持有六件衣物，涉嫌抢劫所得。

pages.en:
12/6.

Enquiries by C.D.C.127 and D.S. Brotherton.
Suspect when questioned admitted having stolen the
articles from a deserted dwelling situated on North
Haining Road at about 8.p.m. 21-8-37.

In view of the above, Mr. Robertson was communi-
cated with and on his instructions the above described
suspect will be sent to Sinsa Station at 10.a.m. on the
morning of the 22-8-37 preparatory to being handed over
to Nantao Chinese Authorities.

Reference a telephone message received from the
Lester Chinese Hospital at 7.10p.m. 21-8-37 to the
effect that the following persons had been admitted
and treated suffering from wounds, C.D.C.161 attended
and ascertained the following:-

At 5.25 p.m. 21-8-37 one named Pai Ai Yuen(潘爱娟)
F/Female, 18, Cantonese, resident 795 Nanking Road had
sustained injuries from falling fragments of shrapnel,
whilst she was sitting in a top room in front of an
open window, above address. Treated at the Hospital
for slight injuries to her left arm and discharged.

At 6.30 p.m. 21-8-37 one named Vong Yue Li(黄有禮)
30, M/unemployed, native of Kiangsu, resident 70 Sai
King Fung, Yangchow Road, whilst walking on Fukien
Road near Hankow Road was hit by falling shrapnel and
sustained injuries to the head, conveyed to Lester
pages.zh:
12/6.

经刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）127号和侦探警司（D.S.）Brotherton 调查。嫌疑人在受审时承认，于1937年8月21日晚上8时左右，从北海宁路一处无人居住的房屋中偷窃了上述物品。

鉴于上述情况，已与 Robertson 先生联系，根据其指示，上述嫌疑人将于1937年8月22日上午10时被送往新闸路巡捕房（Sinsa Station），以便移交给南市中国当局。

关于1937年8月21日晚上7时10分收到莱斯特尔华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）的电话留言，称以下人员因受伤入院接受治疗，刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）161号前往并查明情况如下：

1937年8月21日下午5时25分，一名名为潘爱娟（Pai Ai Yuen）的女性，18岁，广东人，居住于南京路795号，在上述地址楼上房间坐在敞开的窗户前时，被坠落的弹片碎片击伤。在医院接受左臂轻伤治疗后出院。

1937年8月21日下午6时30分，一名名为黄有禮（Vong Yue Li）的男子，30岁，无业，江苏籍，居住于扬州路赛金丰70号（70 Sai King Fung, Yangchow Road），在靠近汉口路的福建路上行走时被坠落的弹片击中，头部受伤，由消防队（S.F.B.）救护车送往莱斯特尔

pages.en:
12/7.

Chinese Hospital by S.F.B. Ambulance, Dr.'s Chit reads:-
Laceration of scalp, fractured skull, serious, detained.
Relatives attended Hospital.

At 6.45 p.m. 21-8-37 one named Tseu Ya Sz(周葉氏),
55, M/Female, Pootung, resident Pootung was admitted
to the Lester Hospital, suffering from wounds to the
shoulder. The above named received her injuries to the
shoulder at about 2 p.m. 21-8-37 during an air raid
over Pootung as the result of a bomb explosion, Detained.
Escorted by relatives.

At 7 p.m. 21-8-37 one named Wong Ching Sung(王正生)
29, coolie, Ningpo , 7 North Szechuen Road was admitted
to the Lester Chinese Hospital suffering from a fractured
left elbow, which he had sustained whilst jumping from
an upper window out into the street to escape fire on
the night of the 19-8-37. Treated and discharged.

At 5 p.m. 21-8-37 the S.F.B. Ambulance attended
Yangtzepoo Road near Whashing Road and conveyed in two
ambulances 14 male Chinese, who, had been allegedly been
fired upon by a squad of Japanese marines. C.D.S.245
attended and ascertained the names of the victims as
follows:-

(1) Chen Heng Ching (陳項清) age 34.
(2) Chu Hua Tyang (朱華堂) age 19.
(3) Van Kwai Sang (閔桂生) age 34.
(4) Kung Tsao Tau (孔招韜) age 34.
pages.zh:
12/7.

华人医院，医生诊断书显示：头皮撕裂，颅骨骨折，伤势严重，留院观察。亲属已到医院探视。

1937年8月21日下午6时45分，一名名为周葉氏（Tseu Ya Sz）的女性，55岁，浦东人，居住于浦东，因肩部受伤入住莱斯特尔医院。上述人员于1937年8月21日下午2时左右，在浦东空袭期间因炸弹爆炸导致肩部受伤，留院观察。由亲属陪同。

1937年8月21日晚上7时，一名名为王正生（Wong Ching Sung）的男子，29岁，苦力，宁波人，居住于四川北路7号，因左肘骨折入住莱斯特尔华人医院，该伤系其于1937年8月19日晚为躲避火灾从楼上窗户跳至街道时所致。经治疗后出院。

1937年8月21日下午5时，消防队（S.F.B.）救护车前往杨树浦路靠近华盛路处，用两辆救护车运送了14名中国男性，据称他们遭到一队日本海军陆战队员的射击。刑事侦缉处（C.D.S.）245号前往并查明了受害者姓名如下：

(1) 陳項清 (Chen Heng Ching)，34岁。
(2) 朱華堂 (Chu Hua Tyang)，19岁。
(3) 閔桂生 (Van Kwai Sang)，34岁。
(4) 孔招韜 (Kung Tsao Tau)，34岁。

pages.en:
12/8.

(5)Hoo Ah Loh (胡阿六),age 46.
(6)Chang Yuen Pao (張元寶),age 33.
(7)Chang Kee Yuen (張基友),age 37.
(8)Wang Kyung Foo (王慶富),age 41.
(9)Hoo Zai Zien (胡賜全),age 62.
(10)Wang Yoong Zung (王永成),age 30.
(11)Ying Tsung Ling (殷宗林),age 33.
(12)Chow Zai Sung (周賜生),age 28.
(13)Chu Mei Ling (朱美林),age 38.
(14)Tang Sing Foh (唐新福),age 31.

All the victims are employed at the Shanghai
Waterworks as fitters, and as far as can be ascertained
were out on a sightseeing expedition at the time, when
they ran into the Japanese Marines.

The 1st named Chen Hong Ching, age 34, native of
Ningpo, residing 270/31 Bubbling Well Road, succumbed to
gunshot wounds, Dr.'s chit and death certificate, up to
date not available until the morning of the 22-8-37.
Deceased' relatives have been warned to attend the in
quest to be held on the morning of the 23-8-37.

The 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th named are still
detained in Hospital, Dr.'s chit not available. The
remaining eight who's injuries are of a superficial
nature were allowed to go after treatment.

At 7:30 p.m. 21-8-37 C.C.R. reported that the
fragment of a shell had lodged in the roof of the Sing
Ngoh Ming Lodging House, 25 Shanse Road.

C.D.C. 161 and D.S. Brotherton attended, but the
fragment of shell could not be located, no person injur-
ed; damage a small hole in the roof.

（签名）
D.R. 86.

Sen.Det.1/c.

D.D.O."A".

12/8.

(5) 胡阿六 (Hoo Ah Loh)，46岁。
(6) 張元寶 (Chang Yuen Pao)，33岁。
(7) 張基友 (Chang Kee Yuen)，37岁。
(8) 王慶富 (Wang Kyung Foo)，41岁。
(9) 胡賜全 (Hoo Zai Zien)，62岁。
(10) 王永成 (Wang Yoong Zung)，30岁。
(11) 殷宗林 (Ying Tsung Ling)，33岁。
(12) 周賜生 (Chow Zai Sung)，28岁。
(13) 朱美林 (Chu Mei Ling)，38岁。
(14) 唐新福 (Tang Sing Foh)，31岁。

所有受害者均受雇于上海自来水公司，担任装配工，据查，他们在外出观光时遭遇了日本海军陆战队。

第一名死者陈项清（原文此处拼写为 Chen Hong Ching，与前文 Chen Heng Ching 略有差异，依上下文应为同一人），34岁，宁波籍，居住于静安寺路270/31号，因枪伤死亡。截至1937年8月22日上午，医生诊断书和死亡证明尚未出具。已通知死者亲属出席将于1937年8月23日上午举行的死因研讯。

第二、三、四、五和六名受害者仍留在医院，医生诊断书尚未出具。其余八名伤者伤势轻微，经治疗后获准离开。

1937年8月21日晚上7时30分，中央无线电接收站（C.C.R.）报告称，一枚炮弹碎片嵌入了山西路25号新五明旅社（Sing Ngoh Ming Lodging House）的屋顶。

刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）161号和侦探警司（D.S.）Brotherton 前往现场，但未能找到炮弹碎片，无人受伤；屋顶仅有一个小洞受损。

（签名）
D.R. 86.

高级侦探 1/c.

“A”区副助理总监。

At 7.30p.m. 21-8-37 C.D.C.s 182, 163, 219 and 114, attached to the S.C.G.P.B. Headquarters, Nantao, came to this station and requested assistance to arrest one named Yao Tien Yuin(姚天恩), Proprietor of a rice shop, No. 85, Feng Gee Moo Doo, Nantao, on suspicion of being a "traitor".

1937年8月21日晚上7时30分，隶属于南市上海市政府警察局总部的刑事侦缉处警员182、163、219和114号来到本巡捕房，请求协助逮捕一名名为姚天恩 (Yao Tien Yuin) 的男子，其为南市凤吉慕杜85号米店店主，涉嫌为“汉奸”。

about 13-8-37, to Japanese soldiers through the medium
of his salesman named Ching Yoong Sung, already referred

selves that the information was correct, accordingly

At 2.30p.m. 21-8-37 the S.C.G.P.B. arrested the

further stated that Yao Tien Yuin had absconded from
the shop on or about 13-8-37 and was at present living
in Room No. 11 of the Loh Ding Sung Lodging House, No.4,
Lane 141, Fekien Road.
The salesman was accordingly led by the S.C.G.P.B.
C.D.C.s to this station at 7.30p.m. 21-8-37 where
assistance was requested to arrest the shop-master, Yao
Tien Yuin.
Assistance was rendered by C.D.C.342 and the
undersigned resulting in the shop-master being arrested
in Room No. 11 of the said Lodging House at 8 p.m.
21-8-37.
When questioned the shop-master admitted being

刑事侦缉处警员342号及签署人提供了协助，结果于1937年8月21日晚上8时在该旅社11室逮捕了店主。

Subject Arrangements made re the handing over of persons arrested
in connection with looting and assaults on alleged traitors.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Glover.

Sir,

A communication was received from Mr. Loh
Chin Sze ( ), President of the Military Court, attached
to the Headquarters of the Shanghai and Woosung Garrison
Commander, during the afternoon of the 21st. August, 1937,
stating that the prisoners arrested in connection with the
above offences should be handed over at the barricade situated
at the intersection of Boulevard Montigny and Rue Lafayette,
French Concession ( Nan-yeng Jiao ), instead of the
place mentioned in the previous report. Also that the
prisoners sent over during the afternoon should reach the
barricade not later than 3:30 p.m.

In view of the above, I would suggest that
the times and point of entry indicated in Headquarters Circular
No.68, be amended accordingly.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
H. Q. C. B. Station,
REPORT
Date August 21, 19 37.
Subject Arrangements made re the handing over of persons arrested in
connection with looting and assaults of alleged traitors.
Made by D.I. Glover Forwarded by C.D.I. Prince.

Sir,
With the approval of the 1st. S.S.D.C. arrangements
have been made whereby the S.M.P. will hand over to representatives
of the Shanghai and Woosung Garrison Commander all persons subject
to Chinese law, who have been arrested in the Settlement on
charges of looting and riotous behaviour.
Such will be escorted twice daily, namely at 11 a.m.
and 4 p.m. by the Stations concerned to the compound of the S.M.C.
Polytechnic School, Pakhoi Road, after which, they will be conveyed
by a party of uniform police and detectives attached to C.I. to
the West Gate Barricade, at the intersection of Rue Lafayette,
French Concession, and Faung Zia Road, O.C.L.
Here they will be taken over into Chinese Territory
by representatives of the Shanghai and Woosung Garrison Commander.
Acting on instructions the undersigned interviewed
the Municipal Advocate on the 21st. Aug. 1937, when the question
regarding the handing over of loot found in possession of these
persons was discussed.
He stated that seized property which could not be
identified as belonging to the residents of the Settlement, should
be handed over together with the prisoners, and a receipt obtained
therefor.
It is essential that C.C.R. be notified about one
hour in advance of the number of prisoners to be handed over so
that the Garrison Commander can arrange for their transportation.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

D. I.

中央捕房总部，
报告
日期：1937年8月21日。
事由：关于移交因抢劫及袭击所谓汉奸而被捕人员的安排。
由督察格洛弗（Glover）撰写，由首席副督察普林斯（Prince）呈报。

先生：

经第一特别高级警司批准，已作出安排，由上海公共租界工部局警务处将所有受中国法律管辖、在租界内因抢劫和暴乱行为被捕的人员，移交给上海及吴淞警备司令部的代表。

此类人员每日两次，即上午11时和下午4时，由相关捕房护送至北海路工部局理工学校大院，随后，由隶属于刑事调查处的制服警察和便衣侦探组成的队伍将其押送至法租界拉斐特路与华界方斜路（Faung Zia Road）交叉口的西门路障。

在此处，他们将由上海及吴淞警备司令部的代表接收，进入中国领土。

根据指示，具名者于1937年8月21日会见了市公诉人，讨论了关于移交在这些人员身上发现的赃物的问题。

他表示，无法确认为租界居民所有的扣押财产，应随囚犯一并移交，并须取得收据。

必须提前一小时通知中央无线电室（C.C.R.）待移交囚犯的人数，以便警备司令部安排运输。

此致，
敬礼

Crime Branch H.Q. Station,
REPORT
Date Aug., 19, 1937.
Subject Arrangements made re: the handing over of persons arrested in con-
nection with looting, and assaults on alleged traitors.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Glover.

Sir,
During the afternoon of the 19th Aug., 1937, Mr. Loh Chin Sze
(陸京士), President of the Military Court attached to the H.Q.
of the Shanghai and Woosung Garrison Commander, Bah Yuen Kwei Miau
(白雲觀廟), West Gate, Chinese City called on Supt. Loh Lien Kwei
at Police H.Qb. when the subject of handing over persons arrested
by the S.M.P. for looting, and assaulting alleged traitors was
discussed. Mr. Loh Chin Sze stated that he had been directed by
General Yang Hu to inform the S.M.P. that he was willing to deal
with these people.
He suggested that persons arrested for the above offences be
daily escorted by the S.M.P. to the above address, where they would
be taken over.
So that no difficulty would be experienced by the officers
escorting these prisoners he stated he would notify the Officer i/c
of the 2nd Division of the S.C.G.P.B. who is in charge of the Police
manning the barricades in this locality.

D. I.

先生：

1937年8月19日下午，上海及吴淞警备司令部总部附属军事法庭庭长罗金四（陸京士）先生，在华界西门白云观庙（Bah Yuen Kwei Miau），拜访了警务处总部的罗连贵（Loh Lien Kwei）巡官，讨论了移交由上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕的抢劫及袭击所谓汉奸人员的事宜。罗金四先生表示，他奉杨虎将军之命通知上海公共租界工部局警务处，他愿意处理这些人。

他建议，将因上述罪行被捕的人员由上海公共租界工部局警务处每日护送至上述地址，在那里进行移交。

为了使护送这些囚犯的警官不遇到困难，他表示将通知负责该地区路障警力部署的上海市警察局第二分局主管警官。

Assistance to Chinese Authorities, following Assault by Mob.
At 10:0 p.m. on the 19/8/37, a Boy Scout named Tih Pau (狄乡), in company with Mr. Wade, attached to the C.V.S. Enquiries by the undersigned and C.D.C. 65 ascertained the following information.
At about 10 p.m. the Boy Scout had been passing by Chungking Road near Avenue Edward VII, when he observed a crowd of Chinese assaulting a male Chinese, whom they stated was giving away poisoned cakes.
The Scout rendered assistance, and managed to effect the rescue of the victim, whom he placed in the car of Mr. Wade who was passing by.
A glass container with 8 rice cakes covered with a reddish substance were also conveyed to station.
Interrogated at the station, the arrested man admitted that the cakes were poisoned, and that he had given away about 10 of the cakes before being assaulted.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Assistance to Chinese Authorities.

At 3.15 p.m. 17/8/37, a telephone message was
received that there was a disturbance taking place on
Avenue Foch, near Chengtu Road, F.S. Bevan, F.S. Philmore
and C.D.C. 254 attended and discovered that two male
Chinese were being assaulted by a large crowd, they having
been denounced as traitors and accused of poisoning the
water placed on the streets for the use of ricksha coolies.

As the crowd was in a hostile mood assistance was
rendered by several members of the French Volunteer Corps
armed with rifles and fixed bayonets, who were in the
vicinity, and eventually the crowd were placated and the
two men were brought to the station by the two foreign
sergeants, they were then sent to the Red Cross Hospital,
Ave. Haig.

It appeared that they had already been searched,
as their pockets were turned inside out.

Later at 5.10 p.m., they were returned to the
station by the hospital authorities, and at the same time,
a male Chinese, a member of the Pootung Guild, one Sung
Bai Yoong (宋百荣), brought to the station several
articles which he said were the property of the two
unknown male Chinese, as these articles were all placed
together, it could not be established as to which articles
belonged to any one of them.

The articles in question consisted of $113.30 in

1937年8月17日下午3时15分，接到电话消息称福煦路靠近成都路处发生骚乱，F.S.贝文（Bevan）、F.S.菲尔莫尔（Philmore）和第254号刑事侦缉处长到场，发现两名中国男子正遭到一大群人的袭击，他们被指为汉奸，并被指控在向街道上放置供人力车夫饮用的水中投毒。

由于人群情绪敌对，附近几名携带步枪并装上刺刀的法国义勇队成员提供了援助，最终人群平息，这两名男子由两名外籍巡佐带至捕房，随后被送往海格路红十字会医院。

看来他们此前已被搜身，因为他们的口袋都被翻了出来。

后来在下午5时10分，医院当局将他们送回捕房，同时，一名浦东同乡会成员、名为宋百荣（Sung Bai Yoong）的中国男子，将几件物品带至捕房，称这些是两名身份不明的中国男子的财产，由于这些物品都放在一起，无法确定哪些物品属于哪一个人。

pages.en:
TRANSLATION.

Despite official warnings of the French Authorities,
certain persons are endeavouring to provoke meetings
or to organise non-authorised groups. The Public are
reminded that during the present period the Police are
responsible for the security of the population, and that
in consequence of this they must oppose, by every possible
means, everyting that tends to break this security.
Therefore, the French Authorities have decided to
discontinue affording protection to any person who will
make use of this protection to create agitation. They
will be expelled from the Concession.
pages.zh:
译文。

尽管法国当局已发出正式警告，仍有个别人士试图煽动集会或组织未经授权的团体。特此提醒公众，在当前时期，警察负有保障民众安全的责任，因此他们必须采取一切可能手段，反对任何破坏这种安全的行为。
因此，法国当局决定，不再保护任何利用此种保护制造骚乱的人员。此类人员将被驱逐出法租界。

pages.en:
Malgré les avertissements officiels des
Autorités Françaises, certains individus cherchent
à provoquer des réunions ou à organiser des groupe-
ments non autorisés. Il est rappelé au Public que
pendant la période actuelle la Police est responsable
de la sécurité de la population, et qu'elle doit par
tous les moyens s'opposer à ce qui peut nuire à cette
sécurité.
En conséquence, les Autorités Françaises ont
décidé de ne plus continuer à protéger les individus
qui se servent de cette protection pour créer de l'a-
gitation. Ils seront expulsés de la Concession./.
pages.zh:
尽管法国当局发出正式警告，某些个人仍试图煽动集会或组织未经授权的团体。特此提醒公众，在当前时期，警察对民众的安全负有责任，并且必须通过一切手段反对任何可能损害这种安全的行为。
因此，法国当局决定不再继续保护那些利用这种保护制造骚乱的个人。他们将被驱逐出法租界。/.

In spite of the proclamation by the French
Authorities prohibiting the holding of meetings or
the organization of bodies there are still cases of
persons attempting to conduct meetings or organize
bodies without permission being first obtained. During
the present period the French Police are responsible
for ensuring the safety of the residents and any attempt
at endangering their safety shall be prohibited by every
means. It is hereby proclaimed that any one who takes
advantage of the protection by the French Authorities
by creating disturbances shall be deprived of protection
and expelled from the Concession.

（印：3rd Sep. 1937）

Chief of Police,
French Concession,
Shanghai.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford
Discreet enquiries have been carried out in an
effort to ascertain whether the examination of alleged
"traitors" had taken place in the office of the Shanghai
Various Circles Support Committee - War Time Special Service
Corps (上海各界後援會戰時服務團特務隊), Room 317 of the Footung Guild Building,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, but so far those efforts have
failed to discover any evidence which would tend to confirm
the report.
The Shanghai Various Circles Support Committee
War Time Special Service Corps, which recently came into
existence with an office at the above address, has removed
to the Tsung Yin Girls' Middle School, 162 Avenue Foch
(正行女中)
(Chengtu Road District), where a small room has been allotted
for the use of the committee as an office. In this school,
a hospital for wounded soldiers under the control of the Red
Cross Society of China is also located.

come to the notice of the Police, in which people suspected
of being traitors, were taken to the Shanghai Municipality
Relief Committee, which is also located in the Footung Guild
Building, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. Enquiries are being made
at present into the activities of this committee, and further
information obtained will form the subject of a further
report.

Subject Lyric Theatre Refugee Camp - Meeting in commemoration
of the "September 18" Anniversary.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Crawford

In commemoration of the 6th Anniversary of the
Mukden Incident, 400 refugees staying in the Lyric Theatre,
780 Peking Road, held a meeting on the theatre premises
between 10.30 a.m. and 12.30 p.m. September 18. Zung Ching-te
(鄭清之), a staff member of the refugee camp, presided.
During the meeting, speeches bearing on the
Anniversary and urging the people to support resistance
against Japanese aggression and to overthrow the Japanese
Imperialists, were made by Ho Shiao-chwang (何孝章) and Ho
Kia-tai (何家堆), members of the Cultural Circles Race
Salvation Association, 270 Chungking Road. In addition,
seven songs including "Beat them back home" (打回老家去)
(of an anti-Japanese nature) were sung and copies of two
handbills were distributed among the refugees. Both
handbills purport to emanate from the Cultural Circles Race
Salvation Association (copies attached). One is addressed
to the refugees, advising them to assist the National Government
in resisting the enemy, and the other is entitled "Outline of
Propaganda in connection with the September 18 Incident"
emphasizing the following three points :-
a) That the hostilities in Shanghai are the commencement of
a war of resistance on all fronts.
b) That the people should unite in their efforts against
Japan.
c) That the people should secure alliance with neutral
countries and weak and oppressed races.

National Herald - 19.9.37(A.M.)

Seven or eight dramatic groups of the Shanghai
Cultural Circles' National Extinction Aversion Association
went to the various hospitals for wounded soldiers and
refugee camps yesterday and performed plays of a national
salvation nature.
Commencing at 9 a.m., two dramatic groups performed
national salvation plays at the Lyric Theatre Refugee Camp;
one was the 12th Party of the National Extinction Aversion
Dramatic Group and the other the Children's Dramatic Group.
Prior to the performance of the plays, the refugees
led by the People's National Extinction Aversion Chorus,
sang a number of songs including the "March of the
Volunteers," "Fight Back to the Old Home," "813" and
"Refugee Song."
The following four plays were staged, the first
two by the Children's Dramatic Group and the last two by
the 12th Party of the National Extinction Aversion Dramatic
Group:-
(1) "Big Sword Corps" (大刀隊), in which the killing of
Japanese soldiers was depicted.
(2) "Arrest the Traitors" (捉漢奸).
(3) "Revenge" (復仇), which dealt with the flight of
refugees and the killing of the wife of one of the
refugees by a stray bullet.
(4) "Return to the Front" (再上前綫), which dealt with
a wounded soldier who upon recovery returned to the
front to kill the enemy.

上海文化界救亡协会的七八个戏剧团体昨天前往各伤兵医院和难民收容所，演出了具有救国性质的话剧。

With reference to the anti-Japanese propaganda
carried out by the "Ta Kung Stage Play and Motion Picture"
Readers' Society, Lane 256, 6 Avenue Dubail, in the Lyric
Theatre Refugee Camp, 780 Peking Road, on September 5,
Mr. Hsu Ying-ts (許華之), a professor of the Great China
University, Chung Shan Road, who is in charge of the said
refugee camp, declared that the propaganda was conducted
by the "Ta Kung Stage Play and Motion Picture" Readers'
Society without his knowledge and permission.

a reporter of the Ta Kung Pao, 181 Avenue Edward VII. French
Concession, and concurrently a responsible member of the "Ta
Kung Stage Play and Motion Picture" Readers' Society, was
interviewed on September 11. Mr. Tang stated that the
Society obtained consent of Mr. Hsu Ying-ts prior to the
performance and that Mr. Hsu was ~~in person~~ present when the
performance was being staged. Mr. Tang stated that the
Society is at present engaged in paying periodical visits
to the different refugee camps and hospitals for wounded
soldiers in the Settlement and the French Concession and
staging similar programmes. On being informed that anything
of a political or objectionable nature would not be tolerated
in the Settlement, he promised to inform the Municipal Police
in advance, should the Society intend to stage any play in
the future.
