THREE MALE REFUGEES MOBBED ON YU YA CHING ROAD
OUTSIDE THE NINGPO GUILD AS "TRAITORS".

At 3.27.p.m. 16-8-37, a telephone message was
received from the Ningpo Guild, Yu Ya Ching Road
stating that a man had been injured outside on the street.

Enquiries by D.S.I. Chang Yuen Ching, C.D.S.316, and
D.S. Macadie ascertained the following facts:-

At about 3.10.p.m. 16-8-37 a rumour was started on
Yu Ya Ching Road outside the Metropole Theatre by
newsboys hawkers etc. to the effect that a male Chinese
refugee named Zee Ah Kung (徐阿根) aged 20, native of
Yu Yao was engaged in putting poison into the public
tea kongs on the roadside. Immediately a shout of
"traitor" went up and the man was set upon by a crowd
of Chinese. Two other refugees who were on the spot were
also attacked. The latter two named Sung Kwong Ming
(陳廣明) aged 50, native of Ningpo and Wong Siao King
(王小林) aged 55, native of Ningpo took refuge in the
Ningpo Guild. The refugee Zee Ah Kung was knocked
unconscious and some bystanders unknown placed a strip
of paper by his side with an inscription, a free trans-
lation of which follows:-"Notice - traitor putting poison
into the tea kongs." A party of Police under Insp.
White was called to the scene and owing to the ugly
attitude of the crowd was compelled to make a baton

三名男性难民在宁波同乡会外的虞洽卿路被当作“汉奸”遭暴徒殴打。

1937年8月16日下午3时27分，接到虞洽卿路宁波同乡会的电话消息，称街上有人受伤。

经D.S.I. Chang Yuen Ching、C.D.S.316及D.S. Macadie调查，查明以下事实：-

1937年8月16日下午3时10分左右，报童和小贩等人在大都会戏院（Metropole Theatre）外的虞洽卿路上散布谣言，称一名名叫徐阿根（Zee Ah Kung）、20岁、余姚籍的中国男性难民正在向路边的公共茶缸（tea kongs）里投毒。随即有人高喊“汉奸”，该男子遭到一群中国人的攻击。现场另外两名难民也遭到攻击。后两人名为陈广明（Sung Kwong Ming，注：拼音与中文名不符，依中文名译）、50岁、宁波人，和王小林（Wong Siao King，注：拼音与中文名不符，依中文名译）、55岁、宁波人，逃入宁波同乡会避难。难民徐阿根被打昏，一些不知名的旁观者在他身边放了一张纸条，上面写着字，大意如下：“通告——向茶缸投毒的汉奸。”怀特（White）巡佐率领一队警察赶到现场，由于人群态度恶劣，警方被迫使用警棍

charge to disperse them.
Zee Ah King was removed by ambulance to the Paulun
Hospital, Burkill Road where he was detained. Doctor's
certificate stated "Bruise of forehead." The other two
were removed from the Ningpo Guild to the Lester Chinese
Hospital.
Doctor's certificates state"Wong Siao Ling- Laceration
of scalp - not serious, three days treatment in O.P.D."
Zung Kwong King-"Bruise cheek - not serious, 7 days
treatment in O.P.D."
No evidence of the allegations of the crowd could be
found. However, one article was found by Zee Ah King
which might have been the origin of the rumour. This
was a cigarette tin, the lid of which had been sealed
on with two holes punched in the top as if it was used as
a sprinkler.
Enquiries at the Ningpo Guild ascertained that Sung
Kwong King and Wong Siao Ling were refugees staying in
the Guild for the past few days. Zee Ah King was not
known to the Guild. He regained consciousness for a
while but relapsed on reaching Hospital and detectives
were unable to question him thoroughly.
Enquiries proceeding.
R.W. MacCrie
D.S.P.

徐阿根（Zee Ah King，注：此处拼写与前文略有不同）由救护车送往伯基尔路的宝隆医院，并被留院观察。医生证明书写道：“前额挫伤。”另外两人从宁波同乡会被送往莱斯中国医院。
医生证明书写道：“王小林（Wong Siao Ling，注：拼写差异）——头皮裂伤——不严重，门诊治疗三天。” 陈广明（Zung Kwong King，注：拼写差异）——脸颊挫伤——不严重，门诊治疗七天。”
未能找到任何证据证实人群的指控。然而，在徐阿根身上发现了一件物品，可能是谣言的起源。这是一个香烟盒，盖子上封着，顶部打了两个孔，仿佛被用作洒水器。
在宁波同乡会进行的查询查明，陈广明（Sung Kwong King，注：拼写差异）和王小林（Wong Siao Ling，注：拼写差异）是过去几天住在同乡会的难民。同乡会不认识徐阿根。他曾短暂恢复意识，但在到达医院后又陷入昏迷，侦探们无法对他进行彻底讯问。
调查正在进行中。
R.W. MacCrie

Alleged "traitor" mobbed.

At 8.30p.m. 16-8-37, Special Police Sergeants
88, 44 and 888, all attached to S.M.P.(S) Headquarters,
brought to Lousa Station a male Chinese:
(1) Chang Sz Yue(張世裕), 31, Yangchow, N.P.A.

S/hawker, N.P.A.

whom they had rescued from a mob of Chinese on Foochow
Rd near Chekiang Rd.

First named stated he was walking past the
mentioned place when he was suddenly attacked by a crowd
who called out that he was a Japanese and a "traitor"
and had been employed by the Japanese to put poisonous

涉嫌“汉奸”遭暴徒殴打。

1937年8月16日晚上8时30分，隶属于工部局警务处（S）总局的特务警长88号、44号和888号，将一名中国男子带至老闸捕房：
(1) 张世裕（Chang Sz Yue），31岁，扬州人，无业。
(2) 王福生（Wong Foh Sung），34岁，清江（Tsing-kiang，音译）人，小贩。

他们是从浙江路附近的福州路上一群中国暴徒手中救出这两人的。

第一人陈述称，当他路过上述地点时，突然遭到一群人的攻击，这些人叫嚷说他是日本人和“汉奸”，受日本人雇佣在街上的人力车夫公共茶水桶里投放有毒液体。他否认这些指控，并声称不知道袭击的动机。第二人陈述称，他不知道第一人为何遭到攻击，但在听到人群发出上述指控后，他在混乱中被推倒。两人都否认互相认识。

由于缺乏任何证据或证人来证实这些指控，两人均被释放。

关于一名涉嫌叛徒死亡一事，据称其在虞洽卿路遭“群众殴打”。
1937年8月16日下午7时25分，接新闸捕房电话通知，称一名在老闸区遭袭击的中国男子已被送入宝隆医院，身负伤痛。
刑事侦缉处警长127号前往新闸捕房，在那里收到一份关于伤者伤情的医疗证明，内容如下：“颈部及肩部等处受伤。”（留院）。
随后，该刑事侦缉处警长询问了新闸捕房巡官302号，后者提供了以下信息：
约在下午7时（1937年8月16日），新闸捕房接到电话通知，称上述病人已送入宝隆医院。该刑事侦缉处警长302号立即前往，并从医院侍役处获悉，该病人于下午3时30分（1937年8月16日）由工部局警务处救护车从靠近南京路的虞洽卿路西侧送往医院。病人入院时，手中紧攥着一个空的50支装香烟铁盒，但在查询时，该铁盒在医院内未能找到。他在入院时能够说话，

刑事侦缉处警长127号与本报告签署人前往据称事发地点虞洽卿路，进行了谨慎的调查，但未找到任何目击者在当时当地目睹与本案有关的事件。此外，由于工部局警务处人员今日极度繁忙，无法向他们核实是否确实是由他们将这名特定病人从虞洽卿路送往宝隆医院。

鉴于病人持有上述香烟铁盒，而该铁盒目前不在警方手中，上述侦探认为，盒内曾装有液体，该病人试图将其倒入租界内的各个茶水桶中；给人的印象是，他以某种方式与日本人有关联，且该

THREE MALE REFUGEES MOBBED ON YU YA CHING ROAD
OUTSIDE THE NINGPO GUILD AS "TRAITORS".

At 3.27.p.m. 16-8-37, a telephone message was
received from the Ningpo Guild, Yu Ya Ching Road
stating that a man had been injured outside on the street.
Enquiries by D.S.I. Chang Yuen Ching, C.D.E.316, and
D.S. MacAule ascertained the following facts:-
At about 3.10.p.m. 16-8-37 a rumour was started on
Yu Ya Ching Road outside the Metropole Theatre by
newsboys hawkers etc. to the effect that a male Chinese
refugee named Zee Ah Kung (谢阿公) aged 20, native of
Yu Yao was engaged in putting poison into the public
tea kongs on the roadside. Immediately a shout of
"traitor" went up and the man was set upon by a crowd
of Chinese. Two other refugees who were on the spot were
also attacked. The latter two named Zung Kwong Ming
(陈光明) aged 50, native of Ningpo and Wong Siao Ling
(王小林) aged 55, native of Ningpo took refuge in the
Ningpo Guild. The Refugee Zee Ah Kung was knocked
unconscious and some bystanders unknown placed a strip
of paper by his side with an inscription, a free trans-
lation of which follows:-"Notice - traitor putting poison
into the tea kongs." A party of Police under Inspt.
White was called to the scene and owing to the ugly
attitude of the crowd was compelled to make a baton

3(Addendum)

Re alleged "traitors" mobbed outside
Ningpo Guild.

Further to this case, at 8.10p.m. 16-8-37 C.P.C.
2713 telephoned Louza Station to the effect that a
"traitor" was being mobbed on Yu Ya Ching Rd near Burkill
Rd.

A party of Police attended and found one Zee Oong
Si (鏡鳴臺), 16, Kompo, S/Unemployed, N.F.A., had been
slightly injured by the mob. Nearby was a box containing
2 phials of "Salso-Brosunen" and on the ground a similar
empty phial. The male Chinese was brought to Louza
Station and questioned, he admitting that he had been
given the box of phials and instructed to place them in
public ricksha coolie's tea urns in the Settlement. He
states that the man giving him the phials had later
been mobbed on Yu Ya Ching Road some time previously
and had been rescued by Police and taken to hospital.
Owing to the confusion existing at present, it was
useless to attempt identification in any hospital,
however accused will appear before the S.S.M. Court
at a.m. on 17-8-37 when application will be made for
a Writ of Detention for one week, pending analysis of the
seized liquid.

关于一名涉嫌叛徒死亡一事，据称其在虞洽卿路遭“群众殴打”。
1937年8月16日下午7时25分，接新闸捕房电话通知，称一名在老闸区遭袭击的中国男子已被送入宝隆医院，身负伤痛。
刑事侦缉处警长127号前往新闸捕房，在那里收到一份关于伤者伤情的医疗证明，内容如下：“颈部及肩部等处受伤。”（留院）。
随后，该刑事侦缉处警长询问了新闸捕房刑事侦缉处警长302号，后者提供了以下信息：
约在下午7时（1937年8月16日），新闸捕房接到电话通知，称上述病人已送入宝隆医院。该刑事侦缉处警长302号立即前往，并从医院侍役处获悉，该病人于下午3时20分（1937年8月16日）由工部局消防队救护车从靠近南京路的虞洽卿路西侧送往医院。病人入院时，手中紧攥着一个空的50支装香烟铁盒，但在查询时，该铁盒在医院内未能找到。他在入院时能够说话，

hospital and when questioned by an attendant named Sze

conscious with the result that no further information
was obtained.

The patient was likewise unable to speak when
C.D.C. 302(Sinza) visited him in hospital or when C.D.C.
127 attended the hospital on receipt of the telephone
message from Sinza.

C.D.C. 127 and the undersigned proceeded to Yu Ya
Ching Road, the alleged scene, and conducted discreet
enquiries but no person was located who had witnessed
any incident, bearing on this case, happen there at
the time in question and, due to the S.F.B. staff being
extremely busy to-day, it could not be ascertained from
them as to whether they had actually removed this
particular patient from Yu Ya Ching Road to the Paulun
Hospital.

In view of the patient having been in possession
of the cigarette tin, referred to, which tin is not in
possession of police, it is the opinion of the said
detectives that the tin had contained a liquid which
the patient had attempted to put in coolies tea urns
in the Settlement, it being the impression that he was,
in some way, connected with the Japanese and that the

当新闸捕房刑事侦缉处警长302号去医院探视，以及刑事侦缉处警长127号接到新闸电话后前往医院时，该病人均无法说话。

刑事侦缉处警长127号与本报告签署人前往据称事发地点虞洽卿路，进行了谨慎的调查，但未找到任何目击者在当时当地目睹与本案有关的事件。此外，由于工部局消防队人员今日极度繁忙，无法向他们核实是否确实是由他们将这名特定病人从虞洽卿路送往宝隆医院。

鉴于病人持有上述香烟铁盒，而该铁盒目前不在警方手中，上述侦探认为，盒内曾装有液体，该病人试图将其倒入租界内苦力的茶水桶中；给人的印象是，他以某种方式与日本人有关联，且该

liquid might prove detrimental to the coolies health.
Being thus caught in the act by patriotic Chinese they
probably inflicted the injuries which resulted in his

The body has been removed to the temporary

1937年8月14日下午1时35分，中央巡捕房警员2708号将下列人员经莱斯特医院带至警局，他发现这些人正在九江路附近外滩遭到一群华人的袭击：-

1. 鐘松法 (Tsong Sung Fah)，听差，17岁，宁波人。
2. 沈萬生 (Sung Van Sun)，苦力，20岁，宜兴人。

经刑事侦缉处警员312号及本报告签署人调查，查明情况如下。

上述两人均受雇于杨树浦路裕豐棉纺厂，该厂于14日上午11时许疏散撤离。他们与该厂另一名听差李祖基 (Lee Zeu Kyi) 一同前往南市。抵达外滩公园时，遇到两名身份不明的男性华人，此二人亦为该厂雇员，他们交给鐘松法一面印有文字的白色布旗，大意是公大纱厂及裕豐棉纺厂的雇员应跟随此旗行动。

鐘松法将旗帜举过头顶，与沈萬生 (Sung Van Sung) 一同沿外滩向南市方向行走。抵达九江路转角处时，

Road he was attacked by a number of male Chinese and
Sung Van Sun who attempted to intervene was also assault-
ed.
C.P.C. 2702 arrived on the scene and stopped the
affray after which the two victims were conveyed by the
Fire Brigade Ambulance to the Lester Hospital where
they received treatment.
No certificate was issued in respect of the
injuries received by Sung Van Sun whilst Tseong Sung
Fah was certified to be suffering from "Laceration of the
chest not serious".
At the time of the affray Tseong Sung Fah was
wearing an open necked shirt and foreign style pants and
had the appearance of a Japanese which, coupled with the
fact that he was carrying a flag bearing the names of
two Japanese Mills, presumably accounts for the attack
made upon him.
Neither of the victims knew where they were going
on leaving the Station and could furnish no address for
purpose of reference.

The Chang Hwa Youth's War Time Service Group with
an office at 4 Tao Yuan Fang, Siao Tao Yuan Ka, Old West Gate,
came into existence on August 25. It is sub-divided into
the following sections :-
1. Propaganda Department
Office : 1 Dah Chih Road, West Gate.
Duty : To publish propaganda matter and deliver
lectures bearing on the national salvation
movement throughout Shanghai.
Activities: Cartoons and posters were recently
exhibited in populated areas throughout
Shanghai, including the advertisement board
at the corner of Yu Ya Ching Road and
Avenue Edward VII.
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 4 OCT. 1937 (C)）
2. Engineering Department
Office : Nanziang.
Duty : To assist Chinese military in procuring
labourers.
Activities: Members are engaged in trench digging, etc.
at Chenju at present.
3. First Aid Corps
Office : 850 Avenue Edward VII (Chengtu Road District)
Duty : To rescue wounded soldiers.
Activities: Two parties each consisting of eight
members are assisting the authorities of
the Chinese Red Cross Society in rescuing
wounded soldiers from the war zone.

some of whom took an active part in the work of the "Youth's

Under the auspices of the Bureau of Social Affairs,
a new organization entitled the "Shanghai Municipality People's
Education Circles' National Salvation Association"
(上海市民衆教育救亡協會) has come into existence with

districts, refugee camps being the principal centres, to
read Chinese characters, and to further the national salvation
movement.

在社会局的主持下，一个新成立的组织“上海市民众教育救亡协会”（上海市民衆教育救亡協會）应运而生，办事处位于辣斐德路500号，通讯地址为北河南路206号皮革业同业公会。目前约有会员20人，大多为社会局职员。该协会的宗旨是登记失业教师，并派遣他们到各区教不识字的民众识字，难民收容所是主要中心，以推进救国运动。

以下是该新协会的主要成员：-

Date Sept. 5, 19 37.

Subject Shanghai Municipality Educationalists' Race Salvation Associations meeting.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

Seven committee members of the Shanghai Municipality
Educationalists' Race Salvation Association, which was
recently organized by local educationalists for the purpose
of carrying out work to assist the national cause during the
present crisis, held a meeting in their office, 500 Rue
Lafayette, between 2 p.m. and 3.30 p.m., September 4, and
passed the following resolutions:-

1) That the people connected with educational circles
throughout the country be advised to purchase as many
national salvation bonds as possible and to promote the
movement of contributing gold and silver articles to the
Government for national salvation purposes.

2) That preparations be made to form propaganda groups for
the purpose of conducting national salvation propaganda
at places in the interior.

3) That the Kwen Van (坤範) Middle School for Girls, 331
Avenue Duburgh Road, and the Tseng Ying (正行) Middle School
for Girls, 162 Avenue Foch, be selected as depots for the
reception of comforts for wounded soldiers.
（印：6 SEP 1937 (C)）

4) That a further meeting be held on September 11.

Subject Cyclists' National Salvation Group (飛輪救國團).
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by S Gauda i.d.

The Cyclists' National Salvation Group, 270
Chungking Road (Sing Kwai Vocational School), which was
sponsored by the Cultural Circles' Race Salvation Association,
came into existence on August 22, with a membership of 45
persons. Each member must supply a bicycle.
The work of the group is outlined hereunder :-
1. To assist national salvation associations in the delivery
of messages and to assist the authorities in maintaining
peace and order.
2. The detection of unscrupulous merchants, traitors and
spies.
3. To comfort soldiers engaged in fighting and to assist
refugees in difficulties.
4. To deliver articles for the "Shanghai Various Circles
Committee to Support Resistance against the Enemy".
This group of 45 cyclists is divided into 9 parties
of 5 each. The affairs of the group are controlled by the
following persons :-
Woo Yi Kung (胡毅公)
Tseu Zau Chi (周肇基) x See also D 7944 & D 8961
Dong Yee (唐毅)
Liu Woo Yuan (柳和元)

It will be recalled that Tseu Zau Chi is one of the
leaders of the national salvation movement in Shanghai and
was the founder of the Shanghai Amateur Travelling Group in
May, 1937. He was arrested on June 9, 1937, by the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau on suspicion of being a
reactionary, but later released on bail, owing to lack of
evidence.

Date August 25, 1937.
Subject 'September 18th' & 'January 28th' Anti-Enemy Comrades Federation.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by C Crawford D.D.

A 'September 18th' & 'January 28th' Anti-Enemy Comrades
Federation recently came into existence with offices established
at No.6, Chengtu Road. The following persons, who are the
chief promoters of the Federation, claim to have participated
in the anti-enemy movement during the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in 1931 and 1932:-
Ai Kuo (艾 国), an ex-student of the Futan University,
residing at No.292 Rue du Marche.
Liu Chien Hwa (刘 建 华), an ex-student of the Voong Yung
University, residing at No.254 Sing Sing Li, Route Pere
Robert.
Fee Kwan Hwa (费 关 华), an ex-student of the Kiang Nan
College, residing at No.4 Li Yuen Fang, Rue Capitain
Rabier.
Zung Hao Poo (宗 好 浦), a member of the Chinese Seamen's
Union, residing at No.1 Zoong Ching Li, Dah Chih Road,
Nantao.
Yao Tsaung (姚 藏), an ex-student of the Tse Kiang
University, Hangchow.
The sole object of the Federation is (1) to conduct first-
aid service in the front and (2) to assist Chinese troops in
creating defensive works. Up to the present this Federation
has organized two first-aid service corps of 20 persons each
and is contemplating formation of nine labour corps of 6 persons
each. It is learned that the two first-aid service corps
are already functioning in the war affected area.
This Federation claims to have a membership of some 110
persons. Each member is required to pay a membership fee of
$0.10 per mensem.

After the withdrawal of our troops, Shanghai was
surrounded by the enemy, and we cannot participate in the
war so gloriously as we did during the three months
following the outbreak of hostilities on August 13. During
those months, it will be recalled, we engaged in comforting
our soldiers by sending them food and drinks and in
attending to the wounded. To-day we only find a gloomy
atmosphere pervading the whole of Shanghai. What a contrast!
This phenomenon is temporary. We shall see sooner or later
a day which is clear and bright. In the meantime, the
great majority of the people in Shanghai are placed in the
same position as Chinese resident in foreign countries,
having been deprived of the opportunity of participating
in the war. The only service they can render the country
is through indirect means. Do we not feel that in such
a big war for the liberation of our race, the efforts we
make are too insignificant? Are we willing to allow the
soldiers and brethren of the country to leave where we are?
We believe that not one of us has the feeling of downhearted-
ness. We will certainly exert ourselves to our utmost
to bring the human and all material resources which are
available in Shanghai so that they can be utilized at the
front and in the rear. In order to show the people throughout
our country that the people in Shanghai are also eager to
avenge themselves on the enemy, it is proposed that a
"Shanghai War Time Service Corps" be formed.
pages.zh:
译文

“上海战时服务团”章程
......

1) 宗旨
我军撤退后，上海被敌人包围，我们无法像8月13日战事爆发后的三个月内
那样光荣地参战。回想那几个月，我们通过向前线士兵输送食物和饮料来慰问他们，
并照料伤员。如今，整个上海只弥漫着一种阴郁的气氛。反差何其巨大！
这种现象是暂时的。我们迟早会看到云开雾散、光明重现的一天。与此同时，
上海绝大多数民众处于与海外华侨相同的境地，被剥夺了参战的机会。
他们能为国家提供的服务只能通过间接方式。难道我们不觉得，在这场关乎民族解放
的大战中，我们的努力太过微不足道吗？我们是否愿意让国家的士兵和同胞
离开我们所在的地方？我们相信，没有人会有沮丧之感。我们将竭尽全力，
调动上海可用的人力和物力资源，使其能在前线和大后方得到利用。
为了向全国民众表明上海人民也渴望向敌人复仇，提议成立
“上海战时服务团”。

pages.en:
-2-
2) Duty
One of the advantages which we have over our enemy is
that we have many more people. In order to produce
strength, the people must be organized, otherwise they
will be like a tray of sand. The purpose of this service
corps is, therefore, to conduct propaganda among the people
in the interior and to organize and arm them. Another
advantage we have over the enemy is that the enemy's
aggression is denounced by all the people of the world,
while the resistance offered by us is extolled and said
to be a sacred duty in the interests of the welfare
of mankind. The death of the enemy on the field of battle,
numerous though they are, pass without comment, but our
own sacrifices are glorified. The service corps will go
into the interior and attend the wounded, at the same time
explaining the significance of the war of resistance to
the people. To bring about a final victory, the people
in the country and the armed forces must support the
National Government and General Chiang Kai-shek, and the
service corps will at the same time direct its attention
to the unification of the people.
3) Facilities
The service corps will avail itself of the services
of persons in Shanghai who specialize in political science
and enlist them as members. We will also utilize scientific
instruments such as wireless apparatus, broadcasting
equipment, cinematograph and medical appliances in the
service of propaganda. We are opposed to the adoption of
"incidents" which only create noise and which have no
relation to the organization of the people.
Staffed with capable members and equipped with scientific
inventions, we can do the maximum amount of good work
among the people in inland cities and districts at minimum
expense and in the minimum period of time.
pages.zh:
-2-
2) 职责
我们优于敌人的优势之一是我们人口众多。为了产生力量，必须将民众组织起来，
否则他们将如同一盘散沙。因此，本服务团的目的是在内地民众中进行宣传，
并组织并武装他们。我们优于敌人的另一优势是，敌人的侵略受到全世界人民的谴责，
而我们的抵抗则受到颂扬，被称为为了人类福祉的神圣职责。
敌人在战场上的死亡，尽管数量众多，却无人评论，而我们自己的牺牲则被 glorified（ glorified 此处意为颂扬/美化）。
服务团将进入内地，照料伤员，同时向民众解释抗战的意义。
为了取得最终胜利，全国民众和武装部队必须支持国民政府和蒋介石将军，
服务团也将同时致力于民众的团结统一。
3) 设施
服务团将利用上海专门从事政治学的人士的服务，并聘请他们为成员。
我们还将利用科学仪器，如无线电器材、广播设备、电影放映机和医疗器具，
服务于宣传工作。我们反对采取那些只制造噪音而与民众组织无关的“事件”。
凭借能干的成员和配备的科学发明，我们可以在最短的时间内、以最低的费用，
在内陆城市和地区的民众中做最大量的有益工作。

pages.en:
-3-
we can show the people a spirit characteristic of the
cultural and industrial centre of China - Shanghai.
4) Enlistment of members
Members of this service corps will be recruited by the
preparatory committee. To be a member, the applicant must
have a clear understanding of the international situation
and the crisis facing the nation. He must be possessed of
a spirit and willing to sacrifice every thing. He must
specialize in some kind of work and must obey the regulations
of the corps.
5) Organization
This service corps will adopt the democratic method
of electing directing officers.
a) A standing committee composed of five members will be
elected by members.
b) The chairman of the standing committee will be elected
from among the five members.
c) Under the standing committee will be formed the following
sections:-
1) General Affairs Section.
2) Organization Section.
3) Propaganda Section.
4) Supplies Section.
5) Technical Service Section.
The chiefs of these sections will be members of the
standing committee, and the chairman of the standing committee
will be head of the General Affairs Section.
6) Equipment
Equipment required in producing dramas
Cinematograph with films.
Small generator required in showing motion
pictures and broadcasting programmes.
pages.zh:
-3-
我们可以向民众展示一种体现中国文化和工业中心——上海特质的精神。
4) 成员招募
本服务团的成员将由筹备委员会招募。申请人必须对国际局势和国家面临的危机有清晰的认识。必须具备牺牲一切的精神和意愿。必须专攻某项工作，并遵守本团的规章。
5) 组织
本服务团将采用民主方式选举主管官员。
a) 由成员选举产生一个由五名成员组成的常务委员会。
b) 常务委员会主席将从这五名成员中选出。
c) 在常务委员会之下设立以下各组：-
1) 总务组。
2) 组织组。
3) 宣传组。
4) 供应组。
5) 技术服务组。
各组组长均为常务委员会成员，常务委员会主席兼任总务组组长。
6) 设备
演出戏剧所需设备
电影放映机及影片。

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C Crawford D.J.

Further enquiries have been made regarding the
Young Chinese Salvation Society which is alleged to be
located at 11 Peace Terrace, Avenue Joffre, but no
information has been obtained to throw light on the
matter, nor have any further activities of this Society
come to the notice of this Branch.

It has been ascertained that the block of houses
located in the Peace Terrace, Avenue Joffre actually
belong to Mr. Dzung Pah Chao (鄭伯昭 ), Manager of
the Wing Tai Vo Tobacco Corporation, Shanghai,
Distributing Agent for the Yee Tsoong Tobacco Company
and the particular house, No.11 of the Terrace, where
this Society is alleged to be situated is occupied by
Mr. Dzung Pah-chao's nephew named Dzung Shou-ling
(鄭寿齡 ) alias Dzung Doong-tsung (鄭同春 ),
and his family. The household of Dzung Shou-ling
at 11 Peace Terrace consists of the following :-

Mr. Dzung Shou-ling, age 50;
Mrs. Dzung Shou-ling, age 50;
Dzung's three sons aged between 11 and 15;
Dzung's unmarried daughter named Zuan-ching, age 25;
Dzung's son-in-law named Loo Ji-siang (盧綺湘),
age 23 and his wife, age 23, and two sons.
Mr. Loo recently came to Shanghai from
Hongkong where his parents are still
residing and is very well off.

（左侧批注：False）
（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 25 JAN 1938 m3）

针对据称位于霞飞路和平里11号的“中国青年救亡社”进行了进一步查询，但未获得任何有助于澄清此事的信息，该社的任何进一步活动也未引起本支部的注意。

经查实，位于霞飞路和平里的这排房屋实际上属于上海永泰和烟草公司经理、义中烟草公司分销代理商郑伯昭 (Dzung Pah Chao) 先生所有，而据称该社所在的和平里11号房屋，由郑伯昭先生的侄子郑寿龄 (Dzung Shou-ling)，别名郑同春 (Dzung Doong-tsung) 及其家人居住。郑寿龄在和平里11号的家庭成员如下：-

郑寿龄先生，50岁；
郑寿龄夫人，50岁；
郑的三个儿子，年龄在11至15岁之间；
郑的未婚女儿，名Zuan-ching，25岁；
郑的女婿卢绮湘 (Loo Ji-siang)，23岁，及其妻子，23岁，还有两个儿子。
卢先生最近从香港来到上海，其父母仍居住在香港，家境富裕。

family named Dzung. The owner being one named Dzung Doong-

that this Chong Nyi Co. which has no office, is owned jointly
by a number of Chinese employees of Mustard & Co., and one

by a certain cigarette company. The latter named is the
brother of Dzung Doong-tsung(鄭同春), the occupant of
the house in question, and owing to the close connection,
Dzung Doong-tsung is exempt from paying rent for the house.

had he noticed at any time visitors of student type
attending the place.

who was a Standing Committee member of the Youth's National
Salvation Service Group, one of the organizations mentioned

Date December 21, 1937.

Subject Letter from "Shanghai Young Writers' National Salvation
Propaganda Group" (now in South China).

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Crawford. D S

The attached letter dated November 27, 1937,
from the Shanghai Young Writers' National Salvation Propaganda
Group intimates that the Group is now quartered in the
Kuomintang Office at Chung San Hsien, Kwangtung, and that the
Commander of the Group, Mr. Siao Chien-ching (蕭劍青), had
not absconded as reported in the Shanghai press. Also that
if this report had been circulated by ex-members of the Group
still in Shanghai, they were operating without authority
from the headquarters of the Group.

With a view to elucidating the contents of the
letter, Mr. Chu Ta-chun (朱大鈞), Manager of the Dah Yah
(大亞) Bookstore, 10/12 Yung Chih Li, Weihaiwei Road, and
Mr. Liu Yuan-tsao (刘元釗), now unemployed, living in
Room 14, 2nd floor, Liang An (良安) Lodging House, Rue
Baron Gros, both of whom are ex-leading members of the Group,
were interviewed. According to them, the Group was
dissolved in the middle of November following the withdrawal
of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, and the ex-members are
no longer active in Shanghai with the national salvation
movement.

Messrs Chu and Liu further explained that before
the dissolution of the Group, a number of members, totalling
12, suggested that all remaining funds of the Group should
be turned over to local refugee relief organizations.
Altogether the Group, during its existence in Shanghai,
obtained about $600, 30% being raised by public donations
and 70% through the sale of publications bearing on first aid
and national salvation work. When expenses had been

附件中日期为1937年11月27日、来自“上海青年作家救亡宣传团”的信件暗示，该团目前驻扎在广东中山县国民党办公室，且该团指挥官萧剑青 (Siao Chien-ching) 先生并未如上海报刊报道的那样潜逃。还指出，如果此报道是由仍留在上海的前团员散布的，那么他们的行动未经该团总部授权。

为了阐明信件内容，面谈了威海卫路永志里10/12号大亚书店经理朱大钧 (Chu Ta-chun) 先生，以及目前失业、居住在格罗西男爵路良安寄宿舍二楼14室的刘元釗 (Liu Yuan-tsao) 先生，两人均为该团前主要成员。据他们称，随着中国军队撤离上海，该团于11月中旬解散，前成员不再在上海从事救亡运动活动。

Translation of an article appearing in the Da Kung Pao
Evening Edition dated November 15, 1937

-----

A Youth Misappropriates Money - the Propaganda Group is
investigating the matter

(Local News) Following the outbreak of the war of
resistance, one Siao Chien-ching, aged 29, a native of
Chung San Hsien, Kwangtung, and an ex-editor of a certain
bookstore, joined the "Shanghai Young Writers' National
Salvation Propaganda Group" and served as an accountant.
When the Chinese forces withdrew from
the Woosung-Shanghai area and consequently various national
salvation bodies suspended activities, he availed himself
of the opportunity and absconded with the funds of the
Group amounting to $300 in addition to the effects of the
Group. His whereabouts are at present unknown. The
Group intends reporting the matter to the police with a
view to arresting and bringing him to justice.

1937年11月15日《大公报》晚刊刊登文章的译文

-----

青年挪用公款——宣传团正在调查此事

（本地新闻）抗战爆发后，一名叫萧剑青、29岁、广东中山县人、前某书店编辑的人，加入了“上海青年作家救亡宣传团”并担任会计。当中国军队从吴淞-上海地区撤退，导致各救亡团体停止活动时，他趁机潜逃，卷走该团资金300元及该团物品。目前其下落不明。该团拟向警方报案，以便将其逮捕并绳之以法。

COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.
Precis of letter from Juvenile Authors National Salvation
Translation of Propaganda League, Chungshan, Kwantung Province.
November 27, 1937.
To
The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.
Sir,
We left Shanghai for the South in accordance
with the policy of the Council to close down anti-
Japanese organizations in the Settlement following
the withdrawal of Chinese Forces from Shanghai and
have now settled down in Chungshan, Kwantung. Mean-
time we learned from newspapers published in Shang-
hai that Liu Yuan Chao, Kiang Chu Lin and Hu Huai
Lee, ex-members of the League, are still active
in Shanghai and caused to publish a libel in news-
papers against Hsiao Chien Ch'ing, Commander of
the League, alleging that Mr. Hsiao had absconded.
In this connection we would make it known to you
that there is no truth whatever in the allegation,
for we all followed him to the South, were given
warm reception en route and have now quartered at
the office of the local Kuomintang. In order to
redouble our effort our membership of the League
has increased to 50. Newspaper cuttings giving
accounts of activities here are attached herewith.
(Seal of): Juvenile Authors National Salvation
Propaganda League.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Gamba 22

A new organization entitled the "Shanghai Young
Writers' National Salvation Propaganda Group" (上海青年作家救亡宣傳團)
has come into existence with a communication address in the
Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association, Room 519 Pootung
Guild Building, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. It has twelve
members with the following persons as its leaders :-

Mr. Siao Chien-ching (蕭劍青), an editor
of the Ching Wei (經緯) Bookstore, 156
Shantung Road.

Mr. Liu Yuan-tsao (劉元操), a reporter
of the China Times, 130 Avenue Edward VII.

Mr. Chu Ta-chun (朱大鈞), Manager of
the Dah Yah (大亞) Bookstore, 10/12 Yung
Chih Li (永吉里), Weihaiwei Road.

The object of the Group is to carry out propaganda
work bearing on the national salvation movement in inland
places.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Re the closure of Chinese Patriotic Institutions

At 9.45 a.m. on 16.11.37, D.S. Hocking, and S.S.I. Shu Zou Kvi, attached to Special Branch (Political) came to Pootoo Road Station and requested assistance in order to close two patriotic institutions to wit:-
The Shanghai Western District Middle and Primary Schools National Extinction Aversion Association, No. 4200 Robison Road and the Peoples War Time Service Corps, No. 40 Hung Zou Fong, Ferry Road.

Accordingly C.D.C. 256, C.P.C. 3185 and the undersigned rendered the necessary assistance first proceeding to 4200 Robison Road where one Lung Kwei Ngoh (任青鹤) was interviewed and stated that at a meeting held at that place on 14.11.37, by members of the Shanghai Western District Middle and Primary Schools National Extinction Aversion Association, it had been decided to cease any further activities, he produced the minute book of the association in which this decision was recorded. During a search conducted of the premises propaganda matter and one chop was seized.

Continuing the party proceeded to the Hui Kwang Primary School, No. 40 Hung Zou Fong, Ferry Road, where the headmaster one Hong Hung Ts (杭衡之), was interviewed and stated that the Peoples War Time Service Corps had operated an office on the school premises until 14.11.37,

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No....

REPORT    Date.... Oct.18, 1937.
Subject.... Untrue report in "Battle Line" (戰綫), a five-day
periodical.
Made by.... C. A. Loh Sih-kya.    Forwarded by.... [Signature]

Further to the attached file, and remarks of D. C.
(Crime) thereon, Lieu Wei-tse (劉惠之), an editor of the
"Battle Line," a five-day periodical, upon being asked on
12.10.37 by the undersigned as to the situation of refugee
camps established by the "Shanghai Western District Middle
and Primary Schools' National Extinction Aggression Association," explained
that the article published by his periodical was sent in by
an unknown contributor and that he was not aware that the
Association in question had conducted false propaganda relative
to the refugee camps. He therefore offered to make a
correction (translation attached) in his periodical.

The "Battle Line" is published and edited by a
committee consisting of the following eight persons:-
Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器), Yen Sz-chi (艾思奇),
Tsang Han-fu (章漢夫), Hsia Tsen-nung (夏征農),
Wong Ta-fu (王達夫), Lieu Wei-tse (劉惠之),
Woo Min (吳敏) and Chen Chu-yuin (陳楚雲).

This Committee has a communication office in the
premises of the Tou Su Sun Huo Zoen ("Life Reading Society"
讀書生活社), No.71 Love Lane, Bubbling Well Road.
Application for registration has already been forwarded to the
Chinese authorities.

The first issue of this periodical appeared on
13.9.37 and about 5,000 copies per issue are printed; the
printing is done at the China Science Corporation (中國科學儀器公司),
No.649 Avenue Foch, French Concession.

[Signature]    Loh Sih Kya
Clerical Assistant.
D. C. (Special Branch).    19/10

继附件档案及刑事情报科总监对此的批注之后，《战线》五日刊编辑刘惠之（劉惠之）于1937年10月12日经本人询问有关“上海西区中小学灭敌会”设立的难民营情况时，解释说其刊物刊登的文章是由一位匿名投稿人寄来的，他并不知道该协会就难民营进行了虚假宣传。因此，他提出在其刊物上进行更正（译文附后）。

《战线》由以下八人组成的委员会出版和编辑：
章乃器（Tsang Nai-chi）、艾思奇（Yen Sz-chi）、
章汉夫（Tsang Han-fu）、夏征农（Hsia Tsen-nung）、
王达夫（Wong Ta-fu）、刘惠之（Lieu Wei-tse）、
吴敏（Woo Min）和陈楚云（Chen Chu-yuin）。

该委员会在南京路爱文义路71号读书生活社（Tou Su Sun Huo Zoen，“Life Reading Society”） premises 设有通讯处。注册申请已提交给中国当局。

该刊第一期于1937年9月13日出版，每期印刷约5000份；印刷工作在法租界福煦路649号中国科学仪器公司（中國科學儀器公司）进行。

[签名]    Loh Sih Kya
文书助理。

The "Battle Line" (戰綫) published the following
correction in its issue No. 7 dated October 16 :-

SHANGHAI WESTERN DISTRICT PRIMARY AND MIDDLE
SCHOOLS NATIONAL EXTINCTION AVERSION ASSN.
FORMED

In our Issue No. 3, we published an
article under the above heading, in which it was
stated that the Association in question is at
present operating several refugee camps in the
Western District. Enquiries made reveal that
this is untrue and that the Association is
merely proposing the establishment of the camps.
We therefore deem it necessary to publish this
correction.
pages.zh:
《战线》（戰綫）在10月16日出版的第7期中刊登了以下更正：

上海西区中小学灭敌会
成立

在我刊第3期中，我们在上述标题下发表了一篇文章，文中称该协会目前在西区运营着数个难民营。经查询，此说法不实，该协会 merely 提议建立难民营。因此，我们认为有必要刊登此更正。

Under the auspices of the following schools, a "Shanghai
Western District Middle and Primary Schools National Extinction
Aversion Association" (沪西中小学民族灭敌会) has been recently form-
ed with an office at No.4200 Robison Road, the premises of the
Chinese Y.M.C.A. Western District Social Centre:-
1. Y.M.C.A. Western District Social Centre Supplementary
School, 4200 Robison Road.
2. Vung Hwa (文化) Middle School, No.11 Gordon Road.
3. Dz Dai (時代) Middle School, 135 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.
4. Ai Kwang (愛光) Primary School, Lane 234, No.40
Mapai Road.
5. Sung Wuh Primary School (生活), 1085 Gordon Road.
.6. Jiu Zuh (求實) Supplementary School, No.56 Kao Ka
Zah, off Connaught Road, O.O.L.
7. Zao Man (曹南) Primary School (曹南小學), No.25 Loo
Sz Zah, off Brenan Road, O.O.L.

This Association claims that its sole object is to unite
middle and primary schools situated in the Western District
and to carry out national extinction/aversion activities under the
guidance of the Chinese Government. At present it is con-
templating formation of the following corps:-
1. First-aid Corps.
2. Propaganda Corps.
3. Detective Corps (for suppressing traitors).
4. Contribution Soliciting Corps.

The Association did not meet with the support of the
schools in that district as is evidenced by the fact that
since its formation no educational institutions have ever
applied to it for membership.

在以下学校的赞助下，“上海西区中小学灭敌会”（沪西中小学民族灭敌会）最近成立，办公室设在罗宾森路4200号基督教青年会西区社会中心 premises：
1. 基督教青年会西区社会中心补习学校，罗宾森路4200号。
2. 文华中学（Vung Hwa），戈登路11号。
3. 时代中学（Dz Dai），极司菲尔路135号，越界筑路区。
4. 爱光小学（Ai Kwang），马白路40号234弄。
5. 生活小学（Sung Wuh Primary School (生活)），戈登路1085号。
6. 求实补习学校（Jiu Zuh），康纳路旁高卡扎56号，越界筑路区。
7. 曹南小学（Zao Man (曹南) Primary School (曹南小學)），布伦南路旁路斯扎25号，越界筑路区。

该会声称其唯一宗旨是团结位于西区的中学和小学，并在中国政府的指导下开展灭敌/抗日活动。目前正考虑组建以下队伍：
1. 急救队。
2. 宣传队。
3. 侦缉队（用于镇压汉奸）。
4. 募捐队。

该会未获得该区学校的支持，事实证明，自其成立以来，没有任何教育机构申请加入。

"Battle Line" (戰綫), a 5-day periodical, published the
following article in its issue No.3 :- 28-9-37 (211)

SHANGHAI WESTERN DISTRICT PRIMARY AND MIDDLE SCHOOLS NATIONAL
EXTINCTION AVERSION ASSOCIATION FORMED

A new body known as the "Shanghai Western
District Primary and Middle Schools National Extinction
Aversion Association," which was formed by the Y.M.C.A.
Western District Social Centre (青年會沪西公社), the Dz Dai
Vocational Middle School (時代職業中學), the Wen Hua Middle
School (文化中學), the Ai Kwang Primary School (愛光小學) and
10 other schools in the Western district, was inaugurated at
a meeting held on August 22. This Association, whose address
is not given, is now operating several refugee camps in the
Western district.

上海西区中小学救亡协会成立

一个名为“上海西区中小学救亡协会”的新团体，由青年会沪西公社、时代职业中学、文化中学、爱光小学以及西区其他10所学校组成，于8月22日举行的会议上正式成立。该会地址未详，目前正于西区运营数个难民收容所。

October 25, 1937.
- 5 -
The People's Lecture Party to Save the Country
- delivering national salvation lectures

Members of the People's Lecture Party to Save
the Country, No.10 Sing Ping Li (信平里 ), Lungmen
Road, started on October 23 to deliver lectures on the
significance of the present war of resistance and the
duty of the people in purchasing liberty bonds. The
lectures are being given at tho following places between
10 a.m. and 10 p.m. daily :-

Tien Zoen Story Tellers (天蟾书场), 220 Foochow Road,
corner of Yu Ya
Ching Road.

Tien Sien Story Tellors (天仙书场), 391 Kiukiang Ro :.
Siao Kwang Yuan Story Tellers(小广寒书场), corner of Foochow
and Chekiang
Roads.

New World Refugee Camp, corner of Yu Ya Ching and
Bubbling Well Road.

Zauchow Guild Refugee Camp, 371 Rue Porte de l'Ouest.

No.1 Refugee Camp of the International Refugee Committee,
corner of Rue Massenet and
Avenue Dubail.

Local National Salvation Organizations conduct a drive
to solicit contributions from the public

Under the auspices of the Vocational Circles
Association to Save the Nation , Lane 132, 4 Park Road, and
other bodies of a similar nature, a campaign entitled the
"Shanghai Municipality Defence Solicitation Movement" was
scheduled to commence on October 24, but were ordered to
desist by the Police. Members of the local national
salvation organizations were to be detailed to visit public
places in Shanghai to lecture and solicit contributions
from the people towards the fund for the purchase of gloves
and cotton padded vests for the Chinese troops, and the
drive was to last two weeks.

- 进行救亡演讲

救国宣讲团成员（地址：龙门路信平里10号）自10月23日起，开始就当前抗战的意义及民众购买公债的义务发表演讲。演讲每日上午10时至晚上10时在以下地点举行：-

天蟾书场 (Tien Zoen Story Tellers)，福州路220号，虞洽卿路转角。

天仙书场 (Tien Sien Story Tellors)，九江路391号。

小广寒书场 (Siao Kwang Yuan Story Tellers)，福州路与浙江路转角。

新世界难民收容所，虞洽卿路与静安寺路转角。

潮州会馆难民收容所，西门口路 (Rue Porte de l'Ouest) 371号。

国际难民委员会第一难民收容所，马思南路 (Rue Massenet) 与杜美路 (Avenue Dubail) 转角。

本地救亡团体开展公众募捐活动

在职业界救国会（地址：派克路132弄）及其他类似团体的主持下，一项名为“上海市防务募捐运动”的活动原定于10月24日开始，但被警方勒令停止。本地救亡团体的成员本计划分批前往上海公共场所进行演讲，并向民众募集捐款，用于为中国军队购买手套和棉背心，该活动原定持续两周。

A new organization entitled the "People's National Salvation Lecturing Group" (民眾救亡演說團 ) has come into existence with an office at Lane 38, 10 Lungmen Road. Its object is to carry out propaganda in favour of the National Salvation Movement in inland places. It claims to have a membership of 31 persons. Mr. Zung Te-liang (鄭子良), one of the local "Green Paungs" leader, and Chairman of the Yah Nyi Zoe (義友社), a Cantonese athletic club situated at Lane 38, 10 Lungmen Road. Formerly he operated opium hongs in the French Concession.

Mr. Chiang I-ming (一鳴), proprietor of the Tai Yih (太乙) Silk Weaving Factory, Lane 772 Ward Road.

Mr. Yang Yen-loong (楊彥龍), a school teacher living at 35 Hart Terrace, Hart Road.

Mr. Tu Chi-yen (杜志賢), a school teacher at Kading.

（印：TELEPRINTER 8 SEP. 1937）
Mr. Woo Yung-wu (胡庸武), an interpreter of the Shanghai District Court.

Mr. Pan Tung-dzu (潘東如), an employee of the Advertisement Department of the Shun Pao, 309 Hankow Road.

Mr. Yao Tien-liang (姚天涼), a clerk of the Yah Nyi Zoe Club, Lane 38, 10 Lungmen Road.

The Group claims that Mr. Tu Yueh-sung, Chairman of the French Concession Chinese Ratepayers' Association, Mr. Ling Kong-hou, Secretary of the Chinese Bankers' Association, and Mr. Wu Kai-sien, a committee member of the local Kuomintang, will serve as honorary advisers to the Group.

Made by D.S.I. Laurier. Forwarded by C G...
In accordance with the instructions of D. C. (Special
Branch) appended to this Section's report on the above subject
of 26 October, detectives attached to this branch, accompanied
by police of Sinza Station, at 3.30 p.m. October 27, proceeded
to house 59, Lane 565, Sinza Road and interviewed one Chong
Sing Yih (龔星怡), the occupier, from whom it was ascertained
that the house in question was a communication address and
registration centre for the above society. He was therefore
told that he should not permit the use of his house for the
purpose mentioned unless and until the Shanghai Hot Blood
National Salvation Corps had been duly registered with the
Shanghai Municipal Council. He agreed to obey these
instructions.
A visit was then paid to house 109, Lane 565, Sinza
Road, the address of several of the executive members of the
Corps, when it was ascertained that the members in question
were ejected from the premises on October 26 for non-payment
of rent.
Laurier

Subject The Shanghai Hot Blood National Salvation Corps - a newly established organization. (上海熱血救亡宣傳團)
Made By S.I. Shih Seu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford J.

A new political organization entitled "The Shanghai Hot Blood National Salvation Corps" has recently come into existence with an office at No. 59, Lane 565, Sinza Road (Sinza District). The principle organizer is one Mr. Woo Kyien Hau (吴钦豪), who is a member of the Shanghai Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. The object of organizing the above corps is to recruit members for the latter mentioned Association. At present about 40 persons have registered with the said corps.

The executive members of the corps are as follows:-
1/. Woo Kyien Hau (吴钦豪), age 17, native of Kiangying, a graduate of the Kiangying Teeng Sung Middle School, Kiangyin. Resides at No. 109, Lane 565 Sinza Road.
2/. Kyu Tsien Yu (邱健友), age 19, native of Chekiang. A graduate of the Wei Lan Middle School, Hangchow. Resides at No. 7 Yenping Terrace, Yenping Road.
3/. Teu Pang Yoeh (朱伴月), age 19, native of Kading. A member of a former dramatic club. Resides at the above address.
4/. Van Poo Ping (范波平), age 21, native of Ningpo. Unemployed tailor-shop assistant, resides at above address.
5/. Wong Sung Kyi (王承基), age 19, native of Peiping. Member of the editorial staff of the Hwa Mei Evening Post. Resides at No. 44, Sing Shu An Lee, Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession.

(b) Propagate the significance of National Day and

establishing branches of this group.

(a) Our principal task is to conduct propaganda by

(b) While conducting propaganda work, efforts will be

(c) The various parties of this group will exert their

Methods for the detection of traitors in foreign
settlements by the Detection Section of the Youths'
National Salvation Group.

Disregarding the existence of the nation, Chinese traitors
have done much harm at the front and in the rear. They are
the enemies of China, and should be exterminated. When you
suspect a man on the street of being a traitor, you must exercise
great care in watching him. If you are in Chinese controlled
territory, the question of searching the suspected man is
easily solved. But if you are in the French Concession or
the International Settlement, your attempt to search the man
will certainly be frustrated by the authorities of the
foreign settlements. You may even lose your own freedom.
We must, therefore, employ the following methods. When you
suspect a man of being a traitor, speak to him in a gentle
manner: "Friend, we are brethren. If we find a man behaving
suspiciously, ought we to ask the man to submit to a search?"
The man will reply: "Certainly." Then you continue, "If
a person accuses you of being a traitor, are you willing to
submit to a search?" If the man replies in the affirmative,
you must talk to him like this, "Friend, please go to a
nearby alleyway or to a private house (when going to a private
house, you should explain the purpose of your visit to the
owner), because if the search is to be carried out on the
street, we may be interfered with by the police." A man
who is willing to submit to search is not really a traitor.
When you find a suspected man who is not willing to submit to
a search, you can ask a pedestrian who is strong or any
boyscout who happens to pass by to help you. Any pedestrian
who is patriotic will certainly help you. Then you must
follow the man, with the assistance of the pedestrian or the
boyscout. When you see the man going into a house, one of
you must go into the house too, leaving the other to keep
watch outside. If the inmates of the house help the man in
doing you harm, the man standing guard outside must report
to a superior organ by telephone, when representatives of
the organ will be sent to help him out of his difficulty.

Necessary information for detection work

1) Members of this section must watch the activities of traitors,
ronins and spies.

2) Places where detection work is to be carried out include tea
houses, restaurants, markets, cinemas, official organs and
congested alleyways.

3) When you suspect a man of being a traitor, jot down the name
of the road, the name of the alleyway and the number of the
house where you find the man.

4) When you see a man being set upon by a mob, you must separate
the man from the crowd, and ask the man to produce papers to
support his innocence if innocent he is. Any clash with
the police must be avoided.

5) Any important incident must be reported to the Detection
Section.

6) Members must find out from where Japanese goods are being
smuggled and guard against the supply of foodstuffs, gunny
bags and iron to the enemy by traitorous merchants.

附于11月6日关于关闭爱多亚路870号青年救国服务团之特务科报告清单中的第20项译文。

青年救国团侦缉队在外国租界侦缉汉奸的方法。

中国汉奸无视国家的存在，在前线和后方造成了极大危害。他们是中国的敌人，应予消灭。当你在街上怀疑某人是汉奸时，必须非常小心地监视他。如果你在中国控制的领土上，搜查嫌疑人的问题很容易解决。但如果你在法租界或公共租界，你试图搜查此人肯定会受到外国租界当局的阻挠。你甚至可能失去自己的人身自由。因此，我们必须采用以下方法。当你怀疑某人是汉奸时，温和地对他说：“朋友，我们是同胞。如果我们发现一个人行为可疑，我们是否应该要求此人接受搜查？”此人会回答：“当然。”然后你继续说，“如果有人指控你是汉奸，你愿意接受搜查吗？”如果此人肯定回答，你必须这样对他说，“朋友，请去附近的弄堂或私人住宅（去私人住宅时，应向屋主说明来意），因为如果在街上进行搜查，我们可能会受到警察的干涉。”愿意接受搜查的人并不是真正的汉奸。当你发现不愿接受搜查的嫌疑人时，你可以请求路过的强壮行人或任何童子军帮助你。任何爱国的行人肯定会帮助你。然后你必须在行人或童子军的协助下跟踪此人。当你看到此人进入一所房子时，你们中的一人也必须进入房子，另一人留在外面望风。如果屋内的人帮助此人对你们造成伤害，外面望风的人必须通过电话向上级机关报告，届时该机关将派代表来帮助他摆脱困境。

侦缉工作的必要信息

1) 本队成员必须监视汉奸、浪人和间谍的活动。

2) 开展侦缉工作的地点包括茶馆、餐馆、市场、电影院、官方机构和拥挤的弄堂。

3) 当你怀疑某人是汉奸时，记下你发现此人的马路名称、弄堂名称和门牌号码。

4) 当你看到某人被暴民围攻时，你必须将此人与人群分开，并要求此人出示证明其清白的证件（如果他是无辜的话）。必须避免与警察发生任何冲突。

5) 任何重要事件必须向侦缉队报告。

6) 成员必须查明日本货物走私的来源，并警惕奸商向敌人供应食品、麻袋和铁器。

7) Members must observe the regulations of the section and be
responsible for any incident caused through their own fault.

8) Members must keep the organization of this section secret.

9) Armbands and badges issued by this section must be well
kept.

10) Important telephone numbers must be borne in mind.

11) When you search a man, you must search him in from behind.
Should a policeman interfere, you can tell the policeman
that you have lost something and ask the policeman to

12) When you meet with difficulties in following a suspected

Regulations governing the organization of the
Guerilla Warfare Research Society of the Youths'
National Salvation Service Group

1. The Guerilla Warfare Research Society is specially
organized for the purpose of enabling the members
of the Group to acquire war knowledge with the
object of arming the people to participate in the
guerilla fighting against Japan.

2. All members of the Group should join the Guerilla
Warfare Research Society.

3. The objects of the Society are as follows :-
(a) to make the members understand the tactics to
be adopted against Japan.
(b) to train members in a knowledge of organizing
the people to join the guerilla fighting against
Japan.
(c) to foster staff members for training the people
in guerilla fighting.

4. The organization of the Society is as follows :-
(a) Section : A section consists of five to ten members,
with a chairman and a vice chairman.
(b) Branch : A branch may be organized where no less
than three sections exist. Each branch
should be governed by a chairman and a
vice chairman assisted by several other
members.
(c) Society : A society controls various branches and
is governed by a chairman and a vice
chairman assisted by several other members.
(d) Sections and branches are designated with figures.

5. A section is subdivided into small corps; a branch is
subdivided into departments and a society is subdivided
into groups.

6. The chief of a section is elected by members; the
chairman of a branch is elected by section chiefs;
and the chairman of a society is elected by the
chairmen of branches.

7. Section offices may be established in the home of a
member, or in a shop or factory where the members
are working; while the offices of a branch or a
society can be established by members at suitable
places.

青年救国服务团游击战研究会组织章程

1. 游击战研究会专为使本团成员获得战争知识而设立，旨在武装民众参与抗日游击战。

2. 本团所有成员均应加入游击战研究会。

3. 本会宗旨如下：
(a) 使成员了解对日作战应采取的战术。
(b) 训练成员掌握组织民众参加抗日游击战的知识。
(c) 培养培训民众进行游击战的干部人员。

4. 本会组织结构如下：
(a) 分队：一个分队由五至十名成员组成，设正、副队长各一名。
(b) 支队：凡有三个及以上分队的地方可组建支队。每个支队由正、副支队长管理，并由其他若干成员协助。
(c) 总会：总会管辖各个支队，由正、副会长管理，并由其他若干成员协助。
(d) 分队和支队以数字编号。

5. 分队下设小队；支队下设各部；总会下设各组。

6. 分队长由队员选举产生；支队长由分队长选举产生；总会长由支队长选举产生。

7. 分队办事处可设在队员家中，或队员工作的商店、工厂内；而支队或总会的办事处可由会员在适当地点设立。

pages.en:
- 2 -

8. The programme of the Society is as follows :-
(A) Guerilla fighting :
(a) tactics to be adopted in the war for the
emancipation of our race.
(b) how to start guerilla fighting.
(c) measures for the execution of guerilla fighting.
(d) tactics to be adopted by guerilla parties.
(B) General politics :
(a) common sense required in the struggle for
the emancipation of our race.
(b) general knowledge for propaganda.
(c) methods to organize people.

9. Sections should hold research meetings twice a week,
each lasting two hours; branches should hold two
meetings every month; and the society should convene
lecture meetings once a week.

10. Discipline of the Society :
(a) study hard.
(b) be punctual: do not absent yourself from meetings,
or retire before the conclusion of a meeting.

11. General principles for research are to be published
by the Society.

12. The following are the sources of income of the
Guerilla Warfare Research Society :-
(a) two cents a month to be collected from each member.
(b) expenses to be paid in accordance with the estimate
approved by the Executive Committee.
(c) personal contributions.
(d) the income and expenditure of the Society should
be published monthly for information of members.

13. These regulations shall be submitted by the Military
Affairs Department to the Executive Committee and
enforced with the latter's approval.

8. 本会课程安排如下：
(A) 游击战：
(a) 民族解放战争中应采取的战术。
(b) 如何发动游击战。
(c) 执行游击战的措施。
(d) 游击队应采取的战术。
(B) 一般政治：
(a) 民族解放斗争中所需的常识。
(b) 宣传所需的一般知识。
(c) 组织民众的方法。

9. 分队每周举行两次研究会议，每次两小时；支队每月举行两次会议；总会每周召开一次讲习会。

10. 本会纪律：
(a) 努力学习。
(b) 准时：不得缺席会议，或在会议结束前退场。

11. 研究通则将由总会公布。

12. 游击战研究会的收入来源如下：
(a) 向每位成员每月收取二分钱。
(b) 开支按照执行委员会批准的预算支付。
(c) 个人捐款。
(d) 本会的收支情况应每月公布，以供成员知晓。

13. 本章程由军事部提交执行委员会，经批准后施行。

Date... November 6, 'o 37.
Subject... Closure of the Youths National Salvation Service Group
(青年救国服务团), 870 Avenue Edward VII.
Made by D.S.I. Laurier Forwarded by C. Gaus... D. I.

Between 2.30 p.m. and 4.40 p.m., November 5, detectives
attached to this branch with the assitance of detective and
uniform personnel attached to Chengtu Road Station, proceeded
to 870 Avenue Edward VII, the offices of the Youths National
Salvation Service Group, and seized and brought to headquarters
a quantity of pamphlets, correspondence, books etc., connected
with the group.
Mr. Fih Pah (畢伯 ), Executive Committee member ,
and Mr. Sze Zao Chien, committee member of the Group, who
were present during the police visit, were instructed that
their organization, by order of the Shanghai Municipal Council,
would not be permitted to function in the Settlement in view
of the strong political nature of its activities and its
refusal to adhere to the regulations of the Council. It was
made clear that the Council had no objection to relief work
provided that this was performed in an orderly and proper
manner. Two C.P.C.s have been posted on the premises to
ensure that the instructions of the police are obeyed.
A list of the documents seized is attached hereto.
Translations of a mimeographed pamphlet and a report
on the defence of Greater Shanghai are also attached hereto.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH - 8 NOV 1937）

Translation of a handwritten report on the "Defence Of
Greater Shanghai" Movement Conducted by the Youths War
Time Service Group on November 2.

During the day, two groups of five persons each were
despatched to Avenue Dubail, Route Vallon and Rue Pascal Beau
to conduct propaganda. Due to inclement weather, the work
was slightly affected but as a whole it was satisfactory
and no untoward incident occurred.

In accordance with the instructions ordering us to
refrain from conducting "mass" demonstrations, we only
disseminated propaganda matter to people on streets and
pasted posters on walls, talked with the people separately
or when they were in small groups and impressed upon them
the necessity for the severance of relations with Japan,
application of sanctions against Japan, defending Greater
Shanghai and opposing mediation and compromise.

The listeners were in general very much moved by our
speeches.

From investigations made by us while we were conducting
the propaganda, we have come to the conclusion that the
people in Shanghai generally have an adequate knowledge of
the present hostilities but they lack organization.

The number of shop assistants and hawkers in Shanghai
comprises 70% of the local population, but they have almost
no organization. Their strength, if properly utilized,
would greatly assist the war of resistance.

Finally we advocate that the labour classes be
organized to support the war of resistance.
pages.zh:
11月2日青年战时服务团开展“大上海防卫”运动的手写报告译文。

白天，派出两组人员，每组五人，分别前往杜美路（Avenue Dubail）、华伦路（Route Vallon）和鲍思高路（Rue Pascal Beau）进行宣传。由于天气恶劣，工作受到轻微影响，但总体令人满意，未发生任何意外事件。

根据命令我们不得进行“大规模”示威的指示，我们仅向街上行人分发宣传材料，在墙上张贴海报，单独或与三五成群的人们交谈，并向他们强调断绝与日本关系、对日制裁、保卫大上海以及反对调解和妥协的必要性。

听众普遍对我们的演讲深受感动。

通过我们在进行宣传期间的调查，我们得出结论：上海民众普遍对当前的敌对行动有足够的了解，但缺乏组织。

上海的店员和小贩占当地人口的70%，但他们几乎没有任何组织。如果加以适当利用，他们的力量将极大地援助抗战。

最后，我们主张组织劳工阶级以支持抗战。

"Second Meeting of the Preparatory Committee of
the Youth Circles' National Salvation Association"
seized at 870 Avenue Edward VII, on November 5, 1937
............

Date : October 30.

Place: National Crisis Youths' Service Group offices.

Attendance: The entire body of the Preparatory Committee,
and Mr. Tang Seu Yu (唐守愚), a member of
the Shanghai Municipality Cultural Circles
Race Salvation Association.

President : Pih Pah (畢伯)
Secretary : Zung Yuen (陳原).

Discussions and Resolutions :-

1. The Preparatory Committee should notify various
organizations to undertake a movement with effect
from November 2 to demand that the Nine Power
Conference apply sanctions against Japan and to
start a campaign of oath-taking to sever relations
with Japan. That the Youths' National Salvation
Service Group be appointed to decide upon the course
of action to be undertaken in connection with the
above movement.

2. That members of the "Youths' National Salvation
Service Group" and the "Youths Conference" be elected
directors of the Movement and that a member of the
first mentioned Group be appointed Chief.

3. That the "Youths' National Salvation League" be
appointed the "Chief Picket" or principal organization
of the Movement.

4. That the Preparatory Committee prepare propaganda for
distribution and the various organizations be instructed
to obtain same from the Shanghai Municipality Cultural
Circles' Race Salvation Association.

5. That the Preparatory Committee be entrusted with the
task of drafting a manifesto, the draft to be completed
within two days.

6. That the various organizations be requested to visit the
Preparatory Committee and affix their seals to a
petition to be submitted to the All Shanghai Association
for the Support of Armed Resistance.

7. That a temporary office be established at the premises
of the Youths' National Salvation Group.
Office Hours :- 1 p.m. to 5 p.m.

REPORT
Date. November 3, 1937.
Subject Youths' National Salvation Service Group - meeting of members.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C Garside DJ

The Youths' National Salvation Service Group
(青年救國服務團), 870 Avenue Edward VII, held a meeting of
members between 8 a.m. and 12 noon October 31 on the premises
of the Ming Tse (民智) Primary School, 601 Weihaiwei Road,
when about one hundred persons including representatives from
the Bureau of Social Affairs and the All Shanghai Association
for the Support of Armed Resistance (抗敵後援會) attended.
Mr. Chang Yu-liang (張裕良), leader of the Group, presided.
Speeches in which those present were exhorted to continue
their work in the interests of the war of resistance were
delivered.

Between 1 p.m. and 5 p.m. the same day, another
meeting which was attended by 60 members of the Youths
National Salvation Service Group took place at the same venue.
A general discussion of the regulations of the Group and the
programme of work to be undertaken was held, but no resolutions
were passed.

Attached to this report are one copy of the
regulations and one of the programme of work with translations.

Kao Yen-ken
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch). CP

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 27 NOV. 1937）

Translation

Regulations of the Youths' National Salvation
Service Group

1. The name of this Group is the Youths' National Salvation
Service Group.

2. The object of this Group is to enlist all youths engaged
in various walks of life in war time service and to organize
the people behind the front lines for national salvation
work in order to obtain the freedom and emancipation of
the Chinese Race.

3. Any youth, irrespective of sex or creed, who desires to
offer his or her service to national salvation, may become
a member on the recommendation of two or more members, or
on the certification of a person of standing and upon
approval by the executive committee. Members are required
to obey the regulations of the Group and observe any
resolutions passed by the organization. They are entitled
to vote at the election of officers. Any member who has
violated the regulations of the Group or has done anything
detrimental to the reputation of the organization can be
expelled by the executive committee.

4. The highest authorities of the Group is the general meeting
of representatives of members, and the functions of the
meeting will consist of passing resolutions, deciding upon
the policy of the Group, electing or impeaching members of
the executive committee, examining reports on work performed
and the financial state of the Group. An executive committee
of 21 persons will be elected at a general meeting of

who will be elected from among the members of the executive
committee will be the chief executive organ of the Group.
A leader to act for the Group and to have charge of the
Group will be elected at a general meeting of representatives
of members. The executive committee will have under its

译文

青年救国服务团章程

1. 本团名称为青年救国服务团。

2. 本团宗旨是动员从事各行各业的青年投入战时服务，并组织后方民众进行救国工作，以求得中华民族的解放与自由。

3. 凡有志于救国服务的青年，不分性别或信仰，经两名或以上成员推荐，或由有名望者证明，并经执行委员会批准，即可成为会员。会员须遵守本团章程及本组织通过的决议。会员享有选举职员时的投票权。任何违反本团章程或有损本组织声誉的会员，可由执行委员会予以除名。

4. 本团最高权力机构为成员代表大会，其职权包括通过决议、决定本团政策、选举或罢免执行委员会委员、审查工作报告及本团财务状况。执行委员会由21人组成，由成员代表大会选举产生。常务委员会由7人组成，从执行委员会委员中选出，为本团最高执行机关。团长一人，代表本团并负责管理本团事务，由成员代表大会选举产生。执行委员会下设

pages.en:

charge seven sections, namely, secretariat, organization,
propaganda, training, contribution canvassing, military
affairs, first aid and detection. Special committee will
be appointed in case of need. Leading residents who are
in sympathy with the object of the Group will be invited to
become its advisors.
5. The tenure of office of the leader of the Group and members
of the executive committee is one year, but they are eligible
for re-election.
6. A general meeting of representatives of members is to be
held every three months. In case of necessity an extra-
ordinary general meeting of representatives of members may
be convoked at the written request of one fifth of the
representatives of members. Meetings of the executive
committee will be held semi-monthly. An extra-ordinary
meeting of the executive committee may be convoked in case
of necessity and at the written request of one third of
the members of the committee.
The revenue of the Group will be provided as follows :-
Initiation fee - ten cents per member.
Monthly subscription - ten cents per member.
(Poor members are exempt from paying subscriptions).
Special contributions:
Special contributions will be canvassed among members and
non-members.
8. Branches of the Group may be established in other cities.
pages.zh:

七个部门，即：秘书处、组织部、宣传部、训练部、募捐部、军事部、救护部和侦察部。必要时可设立特别委员会。邀请同情本团宗旨的社会知名人士担任顾问。
5. 团长及执行委员会委员任期为一年，但可连选连任。
6. 成员代表大会每三个月召开一次。如有必要，经五分之一成员代表书面请求，可召开临时成员代表大会。执行委员会会议每半月召开一次。如有必要，经三分之一执行委员会委员书面请求，可召开临时执行委员会会议。
本团经费来源如下：-
入会费 - 每名会员一角。
月费 - 每名会员一角。
（贫困会员免缴月费）。
特别捐款：
向会员及非会员募集特别捐款。
8. 本团可在其他城市设立分部。

Translation

Draft programme of work to be undertaken by the
Youths' National Salvation Service Group.

The war of resistance against Japan which broke
out in Shanghai on August 13 is a war, the outcome of which
will decide the survival or extinction of the Chinese Race.
To agree to a compromise is tantamount to a surrender to the
Japanese. We insist on the severance of diplomatic
relations with Japan, waging the war of resistance to the
last man, and driving the Japanese imperialists out of
China. We consider that the military action taken by the
Government is not sufficient to overcome the Japanese
imperialistic aggressors. We must mobilize the people of
the whole country. We insist that the following steps should
be carried out:-

1. That all the races and classes of people of China must
unite and engage in national salvation.

2. That rights to conduct patriotic movements must be granted
to the people.

3. That the people must be armed in order to enable them to
participate in the war of resistance.

4. That the property of the enemy must be confiscated and the
life of the people ameliorated.

5. That national defence education be enforced.

6. That all traitors and pro-Japanese elements must be
eliminated.

We consider that the war of resistance waged by
China is in the interests of world peace. It will take a
longer time for China to secure a final victory if she fights
against Japan unaided. We insist that the following steps
must be taken:-

1. That a mutual aid treaty between China and the U.S.S.R.
be concluded.
pages.zh:
译文

青年救国服务团拟开展工作计划草案。

8月13日在上海爆发的抗日战争是一场决定中华民族生死存亡的战争。同意妥协无异于向日本投降。我们坚持与日本断绝外交关系，抗战到底，将日本帝国主义驱逐出中国。我们认为政府采取的军事行动不足以战胜日本帝国主义侵略者。我们必须动员全国民众。我们坚持应采取以下步骤：-

1. 全中国各民族、各阶级人民必须团结起来，投身救国运动。

2. 必须赋予人民进行爱国运动的权利。

3. 必须武装人民，使其能够参与抗战。

4. 必须没收敌产，改善人民生活。

5. 必须推行国防教育。

6. 必须清除所有汉奸及亲日分子。

我们认为中国进行的抗战符合世界和平的利益。如果中国单独对日作战，取得最终胜利将需要更长的时间。我们坚持必须采取以下步骤：-

1. 缔结中苏互助条约。

pages.en:
-,2 -

2. That China must ally herself with Britain, America,
France and the U.S.S.R. in establishing collective
security for the Pacific.

3. That China must federate with the oppressed of the world
for the purpose of dealing with aggressors.

Our duties

Our duties, as young people, are heavy. The future
of the Chinese race lies in our hands. In order to save the
nation from destruction, we must support the war of resistance,
we must unite all young people and participate in war time
service. We must organize the people and educate them in
order to reinforce the resistance. We must struggle for the
enforcement of free education for the people. We must struggle
for an improvement in the life of young people.

Our work

Members of this Group are required to carry out
the following assignments:-

1. To assist the people in organizing national salvation
associations.

2. To instruct the people in political subjects.

3. To conduct propaganda in the form of lectures, dramatics,
choral singing, periodicals, posters and newspapers.

4/ To collect contributions, to render first aid, to comfort
and rescue the wounded, to transport military supplies,
to detect traitors, to assist in the boycott of enemy goods
and to assist the police in the maintenance of peace and order.

5. To undergo a course of military training in order to be
ready for service at the front.

Our organization

The following table shows the internal organization
of our group :-

Executive Committee

2. 中国必须与英国、美国、法国和苏联结盟，建立太平洋集体安全体系。

3. 中国必须与世界被压迫民族联合，以对付侵略者。

我们的责任

作为青年，我们的责任重大。中华民族的未来掌握在我们手中。为了拯救国家免于灭亡，我们必须支持抗战，必须团结所有青年，参与战时服务。我们必须组织民众并对其进行教育，以加强抵抗力量。我们必须争取实行民众免费教育。我们必须争取改善青年的生活状况。

我们的工作

本团成员须执行以下任务：-

1. 协助民众组织救国会。

2. 对民众进行政治教育。

3. 通过演讲、戏剧、合唱、期刊、海报和报纸等形式开展宣传。

4. 募集捐款，提供急救，慰问和救助伤员，运输军需物资，侦察汉奸，协助抵制敌货，并协助警方维持治安秩序。

5. 接受军事训练课程，以便随时准备上前线服役。

我们的组织

下表显示本团的内部组织结构：-

成员代表大会
执行委员会

Our life
We must live a collective life. We must discard
individualism. Each unit must hold a meeting every week to
discuss the current events and every day problems.

Privileges of members
Members of this Group will be entitled to the
following privileges :-
1. To participate in the activities of this Group.
2. To vote at the election of officers and to exercise the
right of recall.
3. To exercise the right of impeachment.
4. To request information regarding the administration of
this group;
5. To submit suggestion.

Our commandments
1. We must be loyal to the Chinese Race. We must carry out
war time service in the interests of the war of resistance.
2. We must observe the regulations of the Group, and its
resolutions.
3. We must not do anything to the detriment of the reputation
or interests of the Group.
4. We, as senior members, must listen to the opinions of junior
members and the junior members must obey the orders of

我们的生活
我们必须过集体生活。我们必须摒弃个人主义。每个单位每周必须举行会议，讨论时事和日常问题。

会员权利
本团会员享有以下权利：-
1. 参加本团活动。
2. 在选举职员时投票，并行使罢免权。
3. 行使弹劾权。
4. 查询本团行政管理情况；
5. 提出建议。

我们的戒律
1. 我们必须忠于中华民族。我们必须为抗战利益履行战时服务。
2. 我们必须遵守本团章程及其决议。
3. 我们不得做任何有损本团声誉或利益的事情。
4. 作为资深成员，我们必须听取初级成员的意见，而初级成员必须服从

Youths' National Salvation Service Group - meeting of members
The Youths' National Salvation Service Group (青年救国服务团),
870 Avenue Edward VII, held a meeting of members between
8 a.m. and 12 noon October 31 on the premises of the Ming Tse
Primary School, 601 Weihaiwei Road. About one hundred
persons including representatives from the Bureau of Social
Affairs and the All Shanghai Association for the Support of
Armed Resistance attended. Mr. Chang Yue-liang (张裕良),
leader of the group, presided. Speeches in which those
present were exhorted to continue their work in the interests
of the war of resistance were delivered.
Between 1 p.m. and 5 p.m. the same day, another meeting
which was attended by 60 members of the Youths' National
Salvation Service Group took place at the same venue. A
general discussion on the regulations of the group and the
programme of work to be undertaken was held, but no resolutions
were passed.
With a view to discussing and passing the following
proposals, the Youths' National Salvation Service Group will
hold another meeting at 2 p.m. November 1 on the premises of
the Pootung Fellow Countrymen's Association, 1454 Avenue
Edward VII:-
1) That the executive committee be reorganized.
2) That a supervisory committee be appointed.

Report dated October 25, 1937, Mr. Chu Tai Yao (朱泰耀),
a representative of the Youths' National Salvation Service
Group, Room 519 Pootung Guild, No. 1454 Avenue Edward VII,

of investigation and approval.

Youths' National Salvation Service Group - meeting

A meeting which was attended by eighteen persons
representing various local youths' war time service groups
took place at 3 p.m. October 23 in Room 519, Pootung Guild,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, under the auspices of the Youths'
National Salvation Service Group situated at 870 Avenue
Edward VII. The following resolutions were discussed
and passed :-

1. That the National Government be requested to sever
diplomatic relations with Japan immediately.

2. That the week between October 24 and October 30 be
set aside as a Propaganda Week.

3. That a circular telegram be despatched on October 30
to the people throughout the country requesting them
to take an oath to sever all economic relations with
the Japanese.

4. That 10,000 posters bearing slogans be prepared.

5. That a meeting to discuss the formation of a youth
circles national salvation association be held at
2 p.m. October 24 in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., 123
Boulevard de Montigny.

6. That the various local national salvation associations
be requested to co-operate with the youths' war time
service groups in carrying out propaganda work.

J. R.    1937年10月25日

青年救国服务团——会议

10月23日下午3时，在爱德华七世路1454号浦东公会519室，
由位于爱德华七世路870号的青年救国服务团主持，
举行了一次会议，出席会议的有代表各地方青年战时服务团的
十八人。讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 请求国民政府立即与日本断绝外交关系。

2. 将10月24日至10月30日这一周定为
宣传周。

3. 于10月30日向全国民众发出通函电报，
请求他们宣誓与日本断绝一切经济往来。

Subject Youth's National Salvation Service Group - drive for funds
for the purchase of stretchers and medicine bags.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. G...

The Youth's National Salvation Service Group with
a head office in the Loong Shu Temple, Lane 476, 8 Fang Zia
Road, Nantao, and registration offices at Lane 27, 20 Yunnan
Road and Lane 606, 5 Medhurst Road, is conducting a drive
for $800 for the purpose of purchasing 100 stretchers and 100
medicine bags to be used by the nursing parties of the Group.
Apart from soliciting contributions over Radio
Station X L H N, 359 Rue Amiral Bayle, the Group has, since
September 24, sent three parties, each consisting of six
members, to the Metropole Gardens, 56 Gordon Road, Merryland
Cabaret, 377 Yu Ya Ching Road, and the Yangtze Ball Room,
87 Yunnan Road, to collect contributions from their patrons.
The Group has decided to collect contributions at these dance
halls for one more day, that is, on September 26. At the
time of solicitation, the Group members distributed copies of
a handbill containing a manifesto bearing on the drive (Specimen
attached). In the manifesto, the attention of the people
is drawn to the importance of rescuing wounded soldiers in
the present campaign of resistance against the enemy and
forming nursing parties to undertake the rescue work.
It is also learned that on September 16, the Group
attempted to collect contributions from inhabitants in
alleyways throughout Shanghai. This soon came to the notice
of the Bureau of Social Affairs, who immediately ordered the
prohibition of the drive.

Chengtu Road Station,
REPORT
Date Sept. 24, 19 37.
Subject Persons soliciting money on behalf of Chinese Soldiers.
Made by D.S. Nicoll. Forwarded by [Signature]
Sir,
At 8.10 p.m. on 24-9-37, U.D.C. 313 telephoned this station,
stating that there were several unauthorised persons attempting
to solicit money from the patrons of the Merryland Cabaret 377 Yu
Ya Ching Road.
D.I. Hill, C.D.S. 3 and the undersigned attended and ascer-
tained that the persons in question were six in number, one female
and 5 male Chinese(not uniformed)named as follows:-
Lok Ling Ying(陸林英),
Seh Kye Tsung(石謙榮),
Yue Ts Yoong(葉知勇),
Tsha Jien Oong(蔡劍鴻),
Jing Kang (金耕),
Li Li Vung(李礼文),
It appeared that they had gone into the cabaret with the
intention of collecting money for the purchase of comforts for the
Chinese troops, and on their entering, a misunderstanding had arisen
when being questioned by the detectives on duty at this place in,
that they were believed to be connected with the Shanghai Woosung
Garrison, who had sent them collecting as aforesaid. This, however,
was proved to be incorrect and was amply borne out by the fact that
all six wore armlets issued by the Young People's National
Salvation Association(青年救國團)Headquarters located at
370 Avenue Edward VII. (Chengtu Road District).
On the position, as regards the public collecting of money for
patriotic purposes and the objections of the management of the
cabaret being explained to the six concerned they left the premises
in a quiet and orderly manner.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. S. 207.

先生，
1937年9月24日晚上8时10分，U.D.C. 313致电本站，
称有数名未经授权的人员试图向虞洽卿路377号快乐舞厅的顾客募款。
警探长 Hill、C.D.S. 3 及本人到场，
查明相关人员共六人，包括一名女性和五名男性华人（未着制服），姓名如下：-
陸林英(Lok Ling Ying),
石謙榮(Seh Kye Tsung),
葉知勇(Yue Ts Yoong),
蔡劍鴻(Tsha Jien Oong),
金耕(Jing Kang),
李礼文(Li Li Vung),
看来他们进入舞厅的目的是为中国军队募集慰劳品购款，
在他们进入时，因受到在该处执勤的侦探询问而产生误会，
误以为他们与上海吴淞驻军有关，是该驻军派来如上所述进行募捐的。
然而，事实证明这并不正确，充分的事实依据是这六人均佩戴
由位于爱德华七世路370号（成都路区）的青年救国团（Young People's National
Salvation Association）总部颁发的臂章。
在向上述六人解释了关于为爱国目的公开募款的立场
以及舞厅管理方的反对意见后，他们安静有序地离开了现场。
此致，
敬礼，
[签名]
D. S. 207.

Subject Youths' National Salvation Service Group.
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Cantoni S I

A new organization entitled the "Youths' National
Salvation Service Group" ( 青年救國服務團 ) was recently
formed by Mr. Mao Long-chia ( 毛 茂 棠 ), promoter of the
Shanghai Amateur Travelling Association, Mr. Liu Liu ( 劉 留 )
and Mr. Dao Chia-tse ( 陶 家 祉 ), both of whom are agents
of the Special Branch of the Shanghai City Government Police
Bureau.

The work of this group will be confined to delivering
lectures dealing with national salvation, detecting the
activities of traitors, assisting in the promotion of the
"enemy" goods boycott movement, soliciting contributions
towards the national salvation fund, organizing a volunteer
army and first aid units, forming a farmers service group,
and the publishing of periodicals and leaflets dealing with
the national crisis.

(印：TO 14 AUG. 1937 SHANGHAI)

On August 1, application forms and copies of the
regulations of the group were mailed to members of the Shanghai
Amateur Travelling Association. Recipients were invited
to register for the Youths' National Salvation Service
Group at (1) 318 Rue Cassini, the home of Mr. Mao Long-chia,
or (2) at Lane 476, No.8 Fang Zia Road, Nantao, or (3) at No.
23 Yen Ping Tsung, Yen Ping Road, where Mr. Zao Ka-tsing
( 趙 家 駿 ) is in charge of registration.

The regulation of the group makes it compulsory for each
member to pay a subscription of ten cents every month.

A copy of the application form and of the regulations
are attached hereto with translations.

Regulations governing the membership of the Youths' National
Salvation Group.

.............

1) The object of this group is to serve the nation, to
strengthen national defence, and to rouse the people to
national salvation.

2) Young people of both sexes and of any creed who are willing
to do national salvation work may join this group (when
applying, fill in application forms with real names,
addresses and what you are skilled in). An initiation fee
of ten cents must be paid.

3) This group will pledge itself to the observance of the
orders of the highest government authorities in dealing
with foreign aggression, and will be required to submit
to the supervision of the party and civil authorities.

4) Members of this group must observe discipline, and must not
do anything outwith the principles of national salvation
or contrary to the Three Principles of the People.

5) Members of this group are entitled to vote, and to see
the work of the executive officers. They are entitled to
read all periodicals provided by the group. They must
observe the regulations of the group and listen to the
advice of the executive officers.

6) The activities of this group are confined to the following:-

a) To organize a national salvation lecturing party for
the purpose of carrying out propaganda work regularly
in various districts.

b) To organize a traitor detecting section.

c) To assist in the promotion of the "enemy" goods boycott
movement.

d) To assist in the canvassing of contributions towards the
national salvation fund.

e) To organize a volunteer army to help maintain peace and
order and to participate in the war against aggression.

f) To organize a war zone service corps and a first aid corps.

g) To organize a village service corps.

h) To publish periodicals and leaflets dealing with the
national crisis.

7) An executive committee of nine persons will be appointed to
take charge of the affairs of this group.

8) A department consisting of fifteen secretaries will be formed
to carry out the daily routine of the group.

译文

青年救国团成员管理章程。

.............

1) 本团宗旨为服务国家，加强国防，并唤醒民众投身救国。

2) 凡愿意从事救国工作的男女青年，不分信仰，均可加入本团（申请时需用真名、地址及专长填写申请表）。须缴纳入会费一角。

3) 本团承诺在处理外来侵略事务时遵守最高政府当局的命令，并接受党和民政当局的监督。

4) 本团成员必须遵守纪律，不得做任何违背救国原则或违反三民主义的事情。

5) 本团成员享有投票权，并有权视察执行人员的工作。有权阅读本团提供的所有期刊。必须遵守本团章程，听从执行人员的建议。

6) 本团的活动限于以下内容：-

a) 组织救国演讲团，以便在各地区定期开展宣传工作。

b) 组织侦缉汉奸组。

c) 协助推动抵制“敌”货运动。

Date December 1, 1937.

Visit to No. 580 Foochow Road following a telephone message
from an unknown person, presumably a Japanese.
Made by D.S. Fitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

At 5 p.m. November 30, 1937, an unknown male
that his name was Nakamura and that he was connected with
the Japanese Secret Service, telephoned C.D.I. Ross informing
him that according to information received, an anti-Japanese
meeting was to be held by some 40 Chinese at a restaurant
located at No. 580 Foochow Road between 5 p.m. and 6.30 p.m.
November 30, 1937.

D.S. Fitts, D.I. Pan Lien-Pih and D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken
(Special Branch) proceeded to the indicated address at 5.10
p.m. which proved to be the Dah Yah Lur (大雅樓)
Restaurant. An interview with the accountant revealed
that two tables had been booked for dinner for a party of
26 persons. The two responsible members of the party,
who had arrived by the time the Police party came upon the
scene were questioned separately and in different rooms by
the undersigned in order to ascertain the object of the
dinner. The first Chinese stated that the party was being
held for the purpose of bidding farewell to a number of
Nipponese members of a cotton hong of which he was the owner.
The second stated that the object of the dinner was to cele-
brate the birth of his son. They were then called together
and confronted with their conflicting statements. They
then admitted they were members of the Shanghai Municipality
Unemployed Workers Relief Committee, which, prior to its
being closed down by the French Police on November 20, was
located at No. 482 Rue Auguste Boppe. Without further
questioning they both admitted they the real object of the
meeting was a farewell dinner party to bid adieu to the
members, most of whom were leaving for points inland in the

At 5.15 p.m. 30-11-37, C.D.I. Sharman was informed
by Dr. Robertson, D.C."A" Division, that he had been
informed by D.S.I. Ross, Special Branch, that informa-

that the management was to be requested by this Station
to refuse to allow the meeting to be held there.

D.S.I. Zia Soen Zien and the undersigned accord-
ingly proceeded to the said room where eighteen male
Chinese were found seated at two tables prepared for
dinner. D.S. Pitts and D.S.I. Kao, attached to the

quiries.

they were ex-members of the Shanghai Municipality Work-
ers Relief Committee, 482, Rue Auguste Boppe, which was
closed by the French Police on 20-11-37, and consequent-
ly they were having a farewell dinner to-day as most of
them have decided to leave Shanghai for inland places.

Subject Registration of un-employed workers - Further report of September 28.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Fan Shuo-liang.

Mr. Chu Hsueh Van, the Chairman of General Labour Union,
returned to Shanghai from Nanking on October 14 having evidently
attained very little success in his appeal to the Government
for financial assistance in repatriation of unemployed workers
from Shanghai.
Despite the broadcasting efforts through radios and
newspapers, little over 2,000 unemployed workers have been
registered in the Yangpu office, about half of these are
receiving 10 cents daily from the Relief Committee.
No measures have been taken or are being prepared to
send these labourers away from Shanghai. Mr. Chang En Chun
of the local Yangpu states that until the services of labourers
are required in the interior, nothing can be done for the
present.
The money to pay the idle workers is borrowed from the
various circles Relief Association and will be refunded by
Chu Hsueh Van as soon as he received remittance from Nanking.

尽管通过广播和报纸进行了宣传努力，但在杨树浦办事处登记的失业工人仅略超过2,000人，其中约有一半每天从救济委员会领取10分钱。
