Subject Unemployed Workers in Shanghai
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Goustead. (J. D)

Further to the attached report dated October 3, 1937,
it is estimated that of the 265,000 local unemployed workers,
shop assistants and coolies, approximately 60,000 have now
returned to their native places of their own accord or at
the expense of the benevolent societies and various fellow
countrymen's associations. With the re-opening of further
industrial concerns in the Western district and shops in the
Settlement, about 15,000 workers and shop assistants have
been given employment. In addition, some 10,000 have become
newspaper vendors, hawkers, etc., thus leaving approximately
180,000 unemployed persons in Shanghai. 150,000 of this
number are unemployed labourers presumably living with friends
and relatives, while the remaining 30,000 who it is safe to
say are without means, are being accommodated in various
refugee camps. It is feasible to believe that a number of
these unemployed persons will return in the near future to
their native places in view of the protracted hostilities
and its effect on the local situation. Measures have been
devised by the Chinese Authorities with a view to using

继附上的1937年10月3日报告之后，据估计，在265,000名本地失业工人、店员和苦力中，约有60,000人已自行或由慈善团体及各同乡会资助返回原籍。随着西区工业企业和租界内商店的重新开业，约有15,000名工人和店员获得了就业。此外，约有10,000人成为报贩、小贩等，因此上海仍有约180,000名失业人员。其中150,000人为失业劳工，推测与亲友同住，而其余30,000人可以说身无分文，正安置在各个难民收容所中。鉴于战事持久及其对当地局势的影响，相信这些失业人员中有一部分将在不久的将来返回原籍。中国当局已制定措施，旨在利用本地失业的技术工人服务于内地工厂，但目前难以评估其成效如何。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 18.10.37.

Shanghai Labourers In Front Line
To Help Chinese Army

Chinese leaders here in Shanghai say that the soldiers are not the only heroes in this man's war, and to prove it they point to the 2,000 labourers at the front. These men were recruited from the mass of jobless refugees and have been on duty up near the front lines ever since the war began. Just as necessary to the carrying on of a war as the men who squint down to the barrel of a rifle, it is their duty to build defence works and do a hundred handy things.

These sturdy diggers have their own organization known as the Workers' War Zone Service Corps, and they are as proud of their emblem as any other division at the front. Soldiers must have trenches to fight in, sandbags to hide behind or roads to march on. It is the Service Corps that provides these post haste.

The men doing defence work at the front were organized by the Shanghai General Labour Union, which is one of those organizations interested in Shanghai's refugee problem. There is a limit to the number of men that can be used at the front, however, and the union is thinking of other ways and means to solve the problem of finding work for Shanghai's 400,000 unemployed.

Many are of the opinion that the present war will be a long one, so industry must be fostered in the safety of the interior. At the present moment many young Chinese workers are being given special training in various trades and crafts, and eventually they will be sent to distant cities to wield the tools they have learned to use.

（批：C.D.Ld 12/10）
（批：CG 12/10）

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月18日。

上海劳工在前线
协助中国军队

驻沪中国领导人表示，在这场全民战争中，士兵并非唯一的英雄，为了证明这一点，他们指出了前线的2,000名劳工。这些人是从大批失业难民中招募而来的，自战争爆发以来一直在前线附近执勤。正如瞄准步枪枪管的人对于战争的继续进行同样必要一样，他们的职责是修筑防御工事和处理各种杂务。

这些强壮的挖掘者有自己的组织，称为“工人战区服务团”，他们对自己的徽章感到自豪，如同前线任何其他部队一样。士兵必须有战壕可战，有沙袋可藏，有道路可行。服务团迅速提供这些设施。

在前线从事防御工作的人员是由上海总工会组织的，该工会是关注上海难民问题的组织之一。然而，前线可用的人数有限，工会正在考虑其他方法和手段，以解决为上海40万失业者寻找工作的问题。

许多人认为目前的战争将是长期的，因此必须在安全的内地促进工业发展。目前，许多年轻的中国工人正在接受各种行业和技术方面的特殊培训，最终他们将被派往遥远的城市，使用他们学会使用的工具进行劳动。

（批：C.D.Ld 10月12日）
（批：CG 10月12日）

September 13, 1937.    4    Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers :-

DISTRICT ASSOCIATION SUGGESTS REGISTRATION OF UNEMPLOYED
WORKERS

The following letter has been sent by the Shanghai
District Association to the Shanghai Tangpu Headquarters
and the Bureau of Social Affairs :-
"Hundreds of thousands of workers have become
unemployed as a result of the outbreak of local hostilities.
In consideration of future rejuvenation, it seems
inadvisable to leave these trained workers to their own
fate.
"It is therefore suggested that these workers be
registered by the Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs
according to their respective trades so that they can be
applied to the factories when and as required. If
suitable relief could also be given to them, it would be
beneficial both from a public and a private point of view."

Social Evening News of Sept.12:

MR. CHU HSUEH-FAN ENGAGED IN LABOUR RELIEF WORK

In view of the fact that many factories have
suspended operations and several hundreds of thousands of
workers have been thereby affected ever since the outbreak
of the local hostilities, Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan (朱學範),
Chairman of the General Labour Union, is busily engaged
in the work for the relief of affected workers.
On the morning of September 11, our reporter
called on Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan and enquired whether he were
very active in certain special affairs work as was reported
recently.
Mr. Chu made the following reply:- "I have
already been very busy in the work for the relief of
workers from war affected zones as well as the international
labour publicity. I did not take part in any special
affairs work. Such a report as is current in this
locality is evidently aimed at misleading the public
and will be dismissed by competent observers.

China Times and other local newspapers:

PROFESSORS' AND WRITERS' ASSOCIATION REQUESTS
CONFISCATION OF ENEMY'S PROPERTY AND STOPPAGE OF
PAYMENT OF BOXER INDEMNITY

The War-Time Cultural Reconstruction Committee of
the Shanghai Professors' and Writers' Association held a
meeting yesterday, with Mr. Chen Shien-mo (陳憲謨)
presiding.
Besides passing a resolution to form a war-time
university, the meeting resolved to support the suggestions
of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the "Shun Pao" for
the confiscation of the enemy's property in China and
the stoppage of payment of the Boxer Indemnity to the
enemy, and to send telegraphic petitions to the National
Government and the Executive Yuan to that effect.

1937年9月13日。 4 上午译文。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

区协会建议登记失业工人

上海区协会已向上海汤浦总部及社会局发出如下信函：-
“由于本地战事爆发，数十万工人失业。考虑到未来的复兴，让这些受过训练的工人听天由命似乎是不明智的。
“因此，建议由汤浦总部和社会局按各自行业对这些工人进行登记，以便在需要时将其调配至工厂。如果还能给予适当的救济，无论从公共还是私人角度来看都是有益的。”

9月12日《社会晚报》：

朱学范先生从事劳工救济工作

鉴于自本地战事爆发以来，许多工厂停工，数十万工人因此受到影响，总工会主席朱学范先生正忙于从事受影响工人的救济工作。
9月11日上午，本报记者拜访了朱学范先生，询问他是否如近期报道的那样积极参与某些特种事务工作。
朱先生答复如下：“我一直忙于战区工人的救济工作以及国际劳工宣传工作。我并未参与任何特种事务工作。本地流传的这种报道显然是为了误导公众，有识之士自会不予理会。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

教授与作家联合会请求没收敌产并停止支付庚子赔款

上海教授与作家联合会的战时文化重建委员会昨日举行会议，由陈宪謨先生主持。
会议除通过组建战时大学的决议外，还决议支持上海总商会和《申报》关于没收敌人在华财产及停止向敌人支付庚子赔款的建议，并就此向国民政府和行政院发送电报请愿。

SOCIAL BUREAU ISSUES ORDER RE FORMATION OF UNEMPLOYED
WORKERS' RELIEF COMMITTEE

The Bureau of Social Affairs of the Shanghai City
Government publishes the following Order to Labour Unions
of Shanghai, No. Special 965, in to-day's "Sin Pao"(字报):-
"This Bureau is in receipt of the following letter,
No. 11, Character 'Chiu' (救), from the Shanghai Unemployed
Workers' Relief Committee :-
'Upon receipt of a telegram from the 6th Depart-
ment of the Military Affairs Commission, instructing
that organization of unemployed workers in Shanghai be
accelerated, the local Kuomintang, government and other
public organs held a meeting and decided to form this
Committee. Messrs. Pan Kung-chan (潘公展), Dao Pah-
chuen (陶百川), Tu Yueh-sung (杜月笙), Wong Shiao-lai
(王晓籁), Doong Ying-pah (董行台), Huang Pah-chiao
(黄柏樵), Sung Yi (沈怡), Tsoong Hwan (锺桓) and Loh
Ching-dz (陆京士) were appointed members of the Committee
and Messrs. Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范) and Chen Pu-hai
(陈步海) as Chief Secretary and Deputy Secretary
respectively, and regulations governing the registration
of unemployed workers and other matters were drawn up.
The Committee was formally inaugurated on September 21
with offices at 482 Rue Boppe, French Concession.
'Many offices for the registration of unemployed
workers have been established in this municipality and
have started functioning, while other works are also
being pushed.

of this Committee and request that you render assistance
to the Committee whenever required. It is also
requested that you will instruct your subordinate organs
accordingly.'

above.

在上海以店员、公共交通公司售票员和司机为生的人中，据信目前只有约50%在职，留下约75,000人失业。估计约有25,000人已离开上海返回原籍。
至于在上海从事苦力工作的10万人，大多数已失业。杨树浦、浦东和南市的码头已停止运作，但在法外滩和苏州河沿岸，估计约有20,000人在职。这些在职人员大多是临时工，靠日薪维持生计。他们中许多人没有家庭负担，满足于以这种方式生活。这使得约80,000人处于失业状态，据查，他们四处游荡，准备从事任何能维持生计的工作。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, September 29, 1937.

Industrial Population
Causes Major Problem
For Local Authorities

Thousands Workers, Thrown Out Of Old Jobs
By War, Now Homeless, Destitute; Efforts
Made To Get Relief For Laborers

Industrial District Razed By Fires

SOME 300,000 able-bodied men and women, representing one-tenth of the city's population, are today deprived of their rice bowls as direct result of the collapse of the industrial life of Shanghai since the start of the local war. One can easily grasp the gravity of the labor situation in Shanghai at present if one thinks of the fact that the number of unemployed workers is as great as the standing army of the United States.

This large number of men and women industrial workers, enough to man hundreds of factories, has to be sheltered, fed, and clothed. Their strength in sheer numerical reckoning and their welfare on an humanitarian basis are not to be denied. They simply cannot be let alone and left to steer their own courses. They constitute a potential danger to the public which the latter cannot ignore. They present unprecedented war in and around Shanghai has caused one of the most serious labor situations in the entire history of the city.

Relief Measures

Well aware of the situation, the Chinese authorities have made every effort for the relief of the destitute industrial workers. Apart from the relief work carried out by the various official and private organizations, a special committee for the assistance of the jobless workers has been formed recently by the local Kuomintang and City Government authorities with the aid of local civic leaders.

The newly formed committee boasts among its backers such well-known personalities as Mr. Pan Kung-chan, head of the Bureau of Social Affairs of the City Government, Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, managing director of the Chung Wai Bank and well-known philanthropist, and many equally well-known celebrities. The labor problem is now viewed with equal concern by the officials and public-minded citizenry as the problem of war refugees.

Situation Bad

Even prior to the war, the labor situation in Shanghai, hit by the depression following the 1932 hostilities, was going from bad to worse. Taking the statistics for the year 1936, some 700 factories closed down in Shanghai alone to reached the highest figure in a decade while there were only some 400 factories newly established during the year. As a result of the closure of these factories during 1936, thousands of industrial workers were thrown out of work. The situation was gradually picking up when the hostilities commenced a wholesale destruction.

Shanghai being the greatest industrial center in China, it has been the center of the labor union movement. According to the latest statistics, there are about 532 labor unions in Central China with the majority in Shanghai and members reach the figure of 264,186. The number of labor unions in the whole country is 829 and the number of their members 460,240. From these figures it can be seen that more than half of the industrial workers who are members of labor unions are in Shanghai.

In Touch With I. L. O.

The labor unions have been in close touch with the International Labor Office China, having sent her representatives to the international labor meetings since 1930. Only recently through the initiative of various seamen's union, a wholesale boycott by the Chinese seamen of the Japanese shipping firms has been witnessed. The seamen's union also appealed to the international labor body to withdraw transportation facilities from aggressor-states, which was meant to be Japan.

The labor unions have of late become a real strength for the championing of the rights of the industrial workers. Not only did these unions settle labor disputes on behalf of the laborers, but were instrumental in strengthening the position and prestige of the industrial workers. And at the same time exploitation in factories was kept to the minimum by these unions. On a percentage basis, 35 per cent of the labor disputes were wholly successful for the workers, 50 per cent partially successful, and 15 percent failures.

Razed to Ground

With the nation's greatest industrial center crippled by the war and about two-thirds of the factories in Shanghai razed to the ground by shells and fires, it will take years to build up again. Unless the authorities do something now to relieve the acute labor situation, serious repercussions are likely to take place.

Recently, the Chinese authorities made arrangements to open factories of basic industries in the interior provinces, such as Hunan, Kiangsi, Kwangsi, and others with semi-official backing. It is reliably reported that factory equipments are being moved from the Shanghai area to the interior provinces. But in spite of various relief measures given the large hordes of jobless industrial workers, there is still a large army of unemployed, remaining a Shanghai which calls grave concern to the authorities and the public alike.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年9月29日，星期三。

工业人口
给地方当局
造成重大问题

成千上万工人因战争失去旧职
如今无家可归，陷入赤贫；各方正努力
为劳工提供救济

工业区被大火夷为平地

约30万身强力壮的男女，占城市人口的十分之一，因自本地战事爆发以来上海工业生活的崩溃，今天直接失去了饭碗。如果想到失业工人的数量相当于美国的常备军，人们就不难理解目前上海劳工局势的严重性。

这批数量庞大的男女产业工人，足以配备数百家工厂，需要得到安置、供养和衣物。他们 sheer numerical reckoning（纯粹数量计算）上的力量以及基于人道主义的福利是不容否认的。绝不能对他们置之不理，任其自生自灭。他们构成了公众无法忽视的潜在危险。上海及其周边地区前所未有的战事造成了该市整个历史上最严重的劳工局势之一。

救济措施

中国当局深知这一局势，已竭尽全力救济贫困的产业工人。除了各官方和私人组织开展的救济工作外，当地国民党及市政府当局在当地社会名流的协助下，最近成立了一个专门委员会，以援助失业工人。

新成立的委员会的支持者中包括一些知名人士，如市政府社会局局长潘公展先生、中汇银行总经理兼著名慈善家杜月笙先生，以及许多同样著名的社会贤达。官员和有公益心的市民现在对劳工问题的关切程度，与对战时难民问题的关切程度相同。

局势恶劣

即使在战前，受1932年战事后萧条打击的上海劳工局势也每况愈下。以1936年的统计数据为例，仅上海就有约700家工厂倒闭，达到十年来的最高数字，而当年新成立的工厂只有约400家。由于1936年这些工厂的关闭，成千上万的产业工人失业。当战事开始造成大规模破坏时，局势本在逐渐好转。

上海作为中国最大的工业中心，一直是工会运动的中心。根据最新统计，华中地区约有532个工会，其中大多数在上海，会员人数达到264,186人。全国工会总数为829个，会员人数为460,240人。从这些数字可以看出，加入工会的产业工人中有一半以上在上海。

与国际劳工局保持联系

各工会一直与国际劳工局中国分局保持密切联系，自1930年以来一直派遣代表参加国际劳工会议。就在最近，在各海员工会的发起下，出现了中国海员全面抵制日本航运公司的情况。海员工会还呼吁国际劳工机构停止向侵略国——意指日本——提供运输便利。

近来，工会已成为捍卫产业工人权利的一股真正力量。这些工会不仅代表劳工解决劳资纠纷，而且在加强产业工人的地位和声望方面发挥了作用。同时，工厂里的剥削也被这些工会控制在最低限度。按比例计算，35%的劳资纠纷完全有利于工人，50%部分有利，15%失败。

夷为平地

随着国家最大的工业中心因战争而瘫痪，上海约三分之二的工厂被炮弹和大火夷为平地，重建将需要数年时间。除非当局现在就采取行动缓解严峻的劳工局势，否则可能会产生严重的后果。

最近，中国当局安排在内陆省份（如湖南、江西、广西等）开设基础工业工厂，并有半官方的支持。据可靠消息报道，工厂设备正从上海地区迁往内陆省份。但是，尽管采取了各种救济措施来应对大批失业的产业工人，仍有一支庞大的失业大军留在上海，这引起了当局和公众的严重关切。

September 30, 1937. Morning Translation

REGISTRATION OF UNEMPLOYED MALE WORKERS

The following notice inserted by the Shanghai Municipality Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee appears in the advertisement columns of the "Shun Pao" and other local newspapers to-day :-
"Since the outbreak of the hostilities in Shanghai, most of the factories have suspended their operations and in consequence large number of workers have been thrown out of employment. With a view to affording relief, this Committee has established in different districts offices for the registration of unemployed male workers. The registration has commenced from September 24 and those who have registered will be given temporary shelter and relief by this Committee. It is hereby notified that all unemployed workers must immediately call at the offices for registration.
"The rules for the registration of unemployed workers are as follows :-
"(1) All unemployed workers in this locality may apply for registration under these rules.
"(2) Unemployed workers who are qualified for registration must fall within the following categories :-
"(a) That they are actually unable to maintain their living after having been thrown out of their employment.
"(b) That they can produce reliable shop or individual guarantees.
"(3) Applicants for registration must observe the following procedure :-
"(a) They must personally call at the registration offices to apply for registration and to fill in the registration forms. (Those who cannot fill in the forms may be represented by the staff of the registration offices to do so, but they must sign their names or marks on the forms).
"(b) They must produce for examination documents of identification (such as badges, pass-books, certificates or membership cards of labour unions. In the event of the loss of such documents, they must produce reliable shop or individual guarantees to prove them).
"(4) Registration certificates will be issued by this Committee when the registration forms have been examined and found by this Committee to be correct.
"(5) Holders of registration certificates will be given relief or recommended for work by this Committee.
"(6) This Committee may, at its own discretion, undertake the registration or limit the number of unemployed workers to be registered.
"(7) No registration fee or other charges will be levied by this Committee for registration.
"Places of registration:- (a) The Shanghai Motor Car Drivers' Union, No.5 Heng An Faung(恆安坊), Faung Pang Road(方浜路), Nan Yang Jao(南陽橋), Nantao. (b) The 10th District Weavers' Union, Tseukajao(周家橋), Western district of Shanghai. (c) Kwan Ti Miao (關帝廟), Shao Chia Road(肇嘉浜), Old West Gate(老西門), Nantao. (d) Kung Wo Theatre(共和大戲院), Faung Pang Jao(方浜橋), Boulevard des Deux Republiques, Nantao. (e) Shanghai Western District Office of the Peasants' and Labourers' Livelihood Improvement Association, No.52 Khaung Foh Li (康福里), Ng Koh Zang(五商場), Zaokadoo(曹家渡)."

（批：Nancy G. 6/10 S.V. R.I.V. handing return of Chu Hsueh Jan from Nanking D.B.R. 1/10）

失业男工登记

上海市失业工人救济委员会发布的以下通知今日刊登在《申报》及其他本地报纸的广告栏中：
“自上海战事爆发以来，大多数工厂已停止运营，因此大量工人失业。为了提供救济，本委员会已在各区设立失业男工登记处。登记工作已于9月24日开始，已登记者将由本委员会提供临时住所和救济。特此通知，所有失业工人必须立即前往登记处进行登记。
“失业工人登记规则如下：
“(1) 本地区所有失业工人均可根据本规则申请登记。
“(2) 符合登记资格的失业工人必须属于以下类别：
“(a) 失业后确实无法维持生活。
“(b) 能提供可靠的店铺或个人担保。
“(3) 登记申请人必须遵守以下程序：
“(a) 必须亲自前往登记处申请登记并填写登记表。（不会填写表格者可由登记处工作人员代填，但必须在表格上签名或画押）。
“(b) 必须出示身份证明文件供查验（如徽章、通行证、证书或工会会员证。如此类文件遗失，必须提供可靠的店铺或个人担保以证明身份）。
“(4) 登记表经本委员会审查确认无误后，将由本委员会颁发登记证。
“(5) 持证人将由本委员会给予救济或推荐工作。
“(6) 本委员会可自行决定进行登记或限制登记的失业工人数量。
“(7) 本委员会不收取任何登记费或其他费用。
“登记地点：(a) 南市南阳桥方浜路恒安坊5号上海汽车司机工会。(b) 上海西区周家桥第十区织布工会。(c) 南市老西门肇嘉浜关帝庙。(d) 南市两共和国路（即今复兴东路）方浜桥共和大戏院。(e) 曹家渡五商场康福里52号农工生活改进协会上海西区办事处。”

（批注：Nancy G. 10月6日 S.V. R.I.V. 转交朱学然从南京返回 D.B.R. 10月1日）

Translation of letter to Council from the
Shanghai Unemployment Relief Committee
(會員喜助救人工業失市海上)。
Dated 25th September, 1937.
Shanghai Unemployment Relief Committee
Since the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai the majority
of the local factories engaged in various lines of business have
been closed down and several hundred thousand workers, pitiful to
say, have been deprived of their means of livelihood. To afford
relief to the unemployed and to maintain the good order of the
community the Shanghai Party and Government Authorities have in
conjunction with public-spirited people in various local circles
organized the Shanghai Unemployment Relief Committee. Apart from
giving relief the Committee will also attend to the task of sending
the labourers in batches to various inland places and secure work
for them. As the number of the unemployed now in Shanghai is very
large, we propose to establish from 5 to 10 offices in various
localities in Nantao, West Shanghai, French Concession and the
International Settlement to enable the labourers to apply for
registration at the nearest office. This will also prevent
congestion and other incidents detrimental to public order.
In affording relief to unemployed labourers this Committee is
solely actuated by the spirit of mutual help and humanitarian prin-
ciples; we have no other purpose. We hope therefore that our
activities will meet with the Council's approval. Apart from apply-
ing for registration to the Shanghai Kuomintang Headquarters and the
City Government, we forward to the Council herewith a copy each of our
Constitution and Regulations governing Registration of unemployed
workers. Kindly take note and instruct the various Police Stations
concerned to render us assistance from time to time.
(Signed) Shanghai Unemployment Relief Committee
P'eu Kung-tsen & 8 Others
Encls: 1 copy each of Constitution and Regulations
Address: No.7 Yuan Hsing Li, Rue Buissenet, Corner of Boulevard
de Montigny.
(Received for translation p.m. 27th Sept.1937.)

自上海战事爆发以来，本地从事各行各业的工厂大多已关闭，数十万工人不幸失去生计来源。为救济失业者并维持社会良好秩序，上海党政当局联合各界热心人士组织了上海失业工人救济委员会。除提供救济外，本会还将负责分批将劳工送往内地各处，并为他们谋取工作。鉴于目前上海失业人数众多，我们拟在南市、沪西、法租界及公共租界各地设立5至10个办事处，以便劳工在最近的办事处申请登记。此举亦可防止拥挤及其他有碍公共秩序的事件发生。
本会在救济失业劳工时，纯粹本着互助精神与人道主义原则行事，别无其他目的。因此，我们希望我们的活动能得到工部局的认可。除向上海国民党市党部和市政府申请备案外，现随函附上本会章程及《失业工人登记规则》各一份。请予知照，并指令各有关警察局不时给予协助。

Translation of enclosures.
1. Constitution of the Shanghai Unemployment Relief Committee.
--
A. The name of this Committee shall be 'the Shanghai Unemployment
Relief Committee'
2. The object of this Committee shall be to afford relief and education-
al facilities to unemployed workers in Shanghai.
3. The functions of this Committee shall be as follows :-
a. To undertake the registration of unemployed workers in
Shanghai .
b. To afford relief to unemployed workers in Shanghai
c. To afford educational facilities and render other services
to unemployed workers in Shanghai
4. This Committee shall consist of nine members appointed by the local
Kuomintang Headquarters and the City Government.
5. This Committee shall have one Chief Secretary, one Assistant Chief
Secretary and several Secretaries.
6. The following Sections shall come under the control of the Chief
Secretary and the Assistant Chief Secretary; the functions of the various
Sections shall be separately decided:
a. General Affairs Section
b. Relief Section
c. Registration Section
d. Statistics Section
e. Investigation Section
f. Auditing Section
g. Recommending Section
h. Education Section
i. Repatriation Section
7. Each Section shall be provided with one Chief of Section and several
Clerks; rules governing the work of the various Sections shall be separ-
ately drafted.

pages.en:
Regulations Governing Registration of
Unemployed Workers by the Shanghai
Unemployment Relief Committee
----
1. All unemployed workers in Shanghai may apply for registration
in accordance with these regulations.
2. Unemployed workers applying for registration should possess
the following qualifications:-
    1. Being definitely unable to make a living after losing
    employment.
    2. Ability to obtain suitable shop or personal guarantees.
3. Workers applying for registration shall observe the follow-
ing procedure:-
    1. The applicants shall personally call at the Registration
    office to report and to fill in registration forms.
    Where applicants are unable to fill in the forms them-
    selves same may be filled in on their behalf by the staff
    of the office, though the forms must be signed by the
    applicants.
    2. Applicants must submit evidence of employment such as
    factory brass badges, wage receipts, Labour Union Certifi-
    cates, membership certificates, etc., for examination. In
    case the articles have been lost the applicants may ask
    reliable shops or persons to bear testimony on their behalf.
4. This Committee shall determine and announce the place and date
of registration.
5. Registration certificates shall be issued after the registra-
tion forms have been verified by this Committee.
6. This Committee shall give holders of registration certificates
due relief and educational facilities and secure suitable work
for them.
7. This Committee if it deems necessary may specify different per-
iods for registration and may restrict the number of applicants
for each period.
8. These Regulations shall be enforced after they have been passed
by this Committee.

C. Klien
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 1 SEP 27 1937 / TRANSLATION OFFICE）
pages.zh:
上海失业工人救济委员会
失业工人登记规则
----
1. 上海所有失业工人均可依照本规则申请登记。
2. 申请登记的失业工人应具备以下资格：-
    1. 失业后确实无法维持生计。
    2. 能够获得适当的商号或个人担保。
3. 申请登记的工人须遵守以下程序：-
    1. 申请人须亲自前往登记处报到并填写登记表。
    若申请人无法自行填写表格，可由办事处工作人员代填，但表格须由申请人签字。
    2. 申请人须提交就业证明供查验，如工厂铜牌、工资收据、工会证书、会员证等。若证件遗失，申请人可请可靠商号或个人作证。
4. 本会将确定并公布登记地点及日期。
5. 登记表经本会核实后，发给登记证。
6. 本将对持证人给予适当救济和教育设施，并为其谋取合适工作。
7. 本会如认为必要，可规定不同的登记期限，并限制每期申请人数。
8. 本规则经本会通过後施行。

C. Klien
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 1 SEP 27 1937 / TRANSLATION OFFICE）

The office of the Committee is located at local
Tangpu Headquarters and the work of this Committee will be to
undertake the registration of all unemployed workers in
Shanghai who have been thrown out of employment in consequence
of the Sino-Japanese conflict in Shanghai. The ostensible
object of this movement is to facilitate measures for
affording them relief, and/or repatriating them to their
native places, but it is also learned that object will be
to select young and strong male applicants who have no
family burden, and to incorporate them in various units,
such as stretcher bearers, etc.. for work in the front line.

With this object in view, the Committee have
secretly fixed 45 years of age as the age limit for applicants,
and have also decided to exclude female and juvenile workers
from the registration. Particular attention will be paid
to health, intelligence, and capability of any applicant.
A blank form of registration which contains these points
and has to be filled in and finger-printed by applicants,
is attached to this report with a translation.

Up to the present, only two registration offices
have been established: one at No. 5 Hung An Fang, Fang Pang
Road, City, which opened on September 27 and another in the
10th District Cotton Spinners' Union, 1428 Brenan Road,
U.O.L., which started functioning at 2 p.m. September 27,
1937.

The office on Brenan Road, adjoining the
Settlement, is in charge of one named Chung Pai Yung (鍾丕雄),
a staff member of the local Tangpu, who is assisted by
members of the Standing Committee of the 10th District

Ta Kung Pao (Evening Edition):
REGISTRATION OF UNEMPLOYED WORKERS COMMENCED
As a means of relief for the large numbers
of workers who have been thrown out of employment as a
result of suspension of operations of various local
factories following the outbreak of the present hostilities,
the local Tangpu Headquarters, the Shanghai City Government
and other government organs have jointly set up a body
known as the Shanghai Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee
for the registration of unemployed workers.
Two offices for the registration of workers
have been established and have already commenced operations,
one at the Motor Car Drivers' Union at Nantao and the
other at the 10th District Weavers' Union in the Western
District.

Translation of letter received from Shanghai Municipality
Unemployed Workers Relief Committee, on September 24, 1937.
------------------
September 24, 1937.

To the Special Branch, S.M.P.

Since the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai,
all factories have closed down, thus depriving tens of
thousands of workers of their means of livelihood. In order
to afford relief to these unemployed workers and to maintain
peace and order of this locality, a committee has been formed
by the local Tangpu and government officials with the close
cooperation of leaders of the public community. This committee,
entitled the Shanghai Municipality Unemployed Workers' Relief
Committee, will, in addition to giving suitable relief to
the workers, also send them in batches to the interior where
suitable employment will be found for them. As there is
a large number of unemployed persons in Shanghai, it is
suggested to establish 5 to 10 registration offices at Nantao,
Western Shanghai, the French Concession and International
Settlement. In this way the workers can apply for registra-
tion in their respective areas without unnecessary crowding
or the danger of disturbances occurring among the workers.
This step has been taken purely with the object of mutual
assistance and humanity in view, and therefore the promoters
hope that you will give sympathetic support to the scheme.
Apart from writing to the Shanghai Tangpu and the Shanghai
City Government this letter is sent to you with a request
that the various police stations concerned be instructed to
render assistance to the registration offices.

Shanghai Municipality Unemployed Workers'
Relief Committee :

致上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处。

自上海战事爆发以来，所有工厂均已关闭，致使数万工人失去生计来源。为了救济这些失业工人并维持本地治安秩序，本地党部及政府官员在社会各界领袖的密切合作下组建了一个委员会。该委员会名为“上海市失业工人救济委员会”，除给予工人适当救济外，还将分批将他们送往内地，以便为他们寻找合适的工作。鉴于上海失业人数众多，建议在南市、上海西区、法租界及公共租界设立5至10个登记处。这样，工人们可以在各自区域申请登记，避免不必要的拥挤或工人中发生骚乱的危险。此举纯粹出于互助和人道主义的目的，因此发起者希望你们能对该计划给予同情和支持。
除致函上海党部和上海市政府外，特致函贵处，请求指示相关各警察局协助登记处的工作。

Shanghai Municipality Unemployed Workers Relief Committee.
Unemployed Workers' Registration Rules.

1. All unemployed workers in this Municipality may apply
for registration in accordance with these rules.

2. Unemployed workers applying for registration must be of
the following categories:
(a) After losing employment, they are actually unable to
maintain their livelihood;
(b) Those who can find reliable shop security or guarantors.

3. Applicants for registration must carry out the following
procedure :-
(a) To attend the registration office personally and fill
in the registration form(those who cannot write must
sign their names on the form after it has been filled in
by officers of the registration office).
(b) To produce documents or other articles for identification
purposes(Factory badges, wage books, labour union
certificates, membership cards, etc. If such identifica-
tion badges, etc. have been lost, applicant must find
shop security or guarantor to prove it).

4.The date and place of registration will be decided and
notified by the Committee.

5. The registration forms will be examined by the Committee
before registration badges are issued to applicants.

6. Those receiving registration badges will receive relief,
education or recommendation for suitable employment, from
the Committee.

7. The Committee will conduct several registrations according to
the necessity or otherwise of such registrations and will
limit the number of persons to be registered at each time.

8. The above rules will be enforced after they have been
passed by the Committee.

上海市失业工人救济委员会。
失业工人登记规则。

1. 本市所有失业工人均可依照本规则申请登记。

2. 申请登记的失业工人须符合下列类别：
(a) 失业后确实无法维持生计者；
(b) 能找到可靠商铺担保或保证人者。

3. 申请人须履行下列手续：-
(a) 亲自前往登记处填写登记表（不会写字者，须由登记处职员代填后，在表上签名）。
(b) 出示证件或其他物品以资证明身份（工厂徽章、工资簿、工会证书、会员证等。如此类身份证明徽章等遗失，申请人须找商铺担保或保证人予以证明）。

4. 登记的日期和地点由委员会决定并通知。

5. 登记表须经委员会审核后方可向申请人发放登记证。

6. 领取登记证者，将从委员会获得救济、教育或推荐合适工作。

7. 委员会将根据登记必要与否进行数次登记，并限制每次登记的人数。

8. 上述规则经委员会通过后施行。

September 25, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Ta Kung Pao (Evening Issue) :-

REGISTRATION OF UNEMPLOYED WORKERS IN SHANGHAI

No less than 400,000 workers have been thrown out of employment since the outbreak of the hostilities in Shanghai. In conjunction with the leaders of the General Labour Union, the district authorities have organized a "Shanghai Unemployed Workers Relief Committee" to undertake various works for the welfare of the unemployed workers.
In an interview with our reporter, an official of the local General Labour Union has given out the following information :-
"Prior to the hostilities, the General Labour Union had a membership of about 300,000 workers. There were another 300,000 workers who were not members of the Union. Following the outbreak of the war, about 200,000 workers left for their respective homes. Of these remaining in Shanghai, the majority are now putting up with their relatives or friends, while a number of them are either staying in refugee camps or in small lodging houses. Fortunately, due to the efforts of the district authorities no untoward incident has occurred.
"The Relief Committee is now considering the registration of unemployed workers and financial problems. The district authorities have promised that the government will make up the deficiency if the funds that are going to be raised are insufficient to meet the needs. As regards the registration of unemployed workers, the Relief Committee will secure permission from the authorities of the foreign Settlements for the establishment of registration offices in these areas in order to assist those unemployed workers residing in the foreign Settlements. As soon as they have registered, the unemployed workers will be provided with clothing and accommodation by the Relief Committee which will also endeavour to recommend them for employment either in Shanghai or in inland places. The registration will be conducted in several stages. It is contemplated to register 10,000 workers for the first batch. Those who wish to register themselves should preferably be workers of the poorer class. The Relief Committee is now canvassing for public subscriptions and the result so far is quite satisfactory."

Ta Kung Pao (Evening Issue) :-

JAPANESE COPPER COINS REPORTED IN CURRENCY IN THIS LOCALITY

According to information given out by certain persons connected with the cigarette and exchange circles, treacherous elements have of late circulated Japanese copper coins by mixing them up in Chinese copper coins with the object of causing disorder. It is hoped that the local residents will pay attention to this matter in order to avoid misunderstanding.

1937年9月25日。下午译文

《大公报》（晚刊）：-

上海失业工人登记

自上海战事爆发以来，失业工人不下40万人。各区当局联合总工会领袖组织了“上海失业工人救济委员会”，开展各项有利于失业工人的工作。
本地总工会的一位官员在接受本报记者采访时提供了以下信息：-
“战事爆发前，总工会拥有约30万名会员。另有30万名工人未加入工会。战争爆发后，约20万名工人返回各自家乡。留在上海的人中，大多数目前寄居在亲友家中，部分人则住在难民收容所或小旅馆里。幸运的是，由于各区当局的努力，未发生任何意外事件。
“救济委员会目前正在考虑失业工人登记及资金问题。各区当局已承诺，如果筹集的资金不足以满足需求，政府将补足差额。关于失业工人登记，救济委员会将争取外国租界当局的许可，在这些区域设立登记处，以协助居住在外租界的失业工人。一旦登记，救济委员会将为失业工人提供衣物和住宿，并努力推荐他们在上海或内地就业。登记将分几个阶段进行。计划第一批登记1万名工人。希望登记者最好是贫困阶层的工人。救济委员会目前正在募集公众捐款，目前的结果相当令人满意。”

REPORT
Date Sept. 22 1937.

Subject Proposed Repatriation of unemployed labourers in the Settlement.

Made by....................and............................Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan, Chairman of the General Labour
Union, telephoned this afternoon stating that roughly about
600,000 workers have been thrown out of employment since the
war broke out in Shanghai. Although the majority have gone
to their homes in the interior, the number of persons who
have been left idle and destitute must be great and in view
of their presence being a nuisance to the public, a committee
has been formed with members composed of representatives from the
City Government, the Tangpu and General Labour Union with the
object of repatriating these people to the interior where they
will be given employment in the factories. As a first step
registration will be carried out in the Settlement subject to
the approval and cooperation of S.M.C.

Tan Shao Liang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Crime & Special Branches)
C.O.T. Ree.

will be necessary before it can be

SHANGHAI TIMES - 26.9.37.
25685

Ambitious Scheme To Assist
Unemployed In Shanghai
Committee Formed To Take Care Of Thousands Who
Have Been Thrown Out Of Work; Many Will Be
Registered Soon; Ricsha Hong's Idea

Chinese officials and leaders of the
Shanghai General Labour Union
have organized the Shanghai Jobless
Workers Relief Committee for the
purpose of carrying out effective
relief measures for nearly 400,000
workers thrown out of work as a
result of the hostilities. The ques-
tion is receiving serious attention of
those interested in labour problems
and 10 registration depots are being
established for the purpose of mak-
ing a statistical study of the condi-
tions among destitute workers.
Interviewed by a representative
of "The Shanghai Times," several
leaders of the Shanghai General
Labour Union showed great interest
in the problem which, they said, they
thought was in keeping with their
policy of giving relief to workers
because most of the male refugees
are workers. Prior to the war there
were 300,000 union workers and
about the same number of non-
union workers in Shanghai. About
200,000 workers have left Shanghai
for their native districts.
While many unemployed workers
in Shanghai are remaining in re-
fugee camps most of them are in
homes of relatives and friends
and are living in a hand to mouth
manner. A small number who have
savings live in small hotels. Thanks
to the efforts of civic leaders and
officials these workers have not
created any trouble. About 100,000
who formerly worked in Japanese
cotton mills in the Yangtzepoo dis-
trict are receiving special care, since
local Chinese authorities have re-
peatedly declared that they would
pay particular attention to skilled
workers.

Systematic Relief Plan
Before carrying out any systematic
relief plan, the committee has de-
cided to register workers first, at the
same time tackling the financial
problem. In connection with the
latter question, it was stated that
the Government might be petitioned
for funds if money raised by philan-
thropists here should prove in-
sufficient. In connection with the
establishment of registration offices
permission will be secured from the
French Concession and Settlement
authorities, where most of the work-
ers stay.
At the time of registration all
workers must show badges or docu-
mentary proofs from their respective
unions. After obtaining registration
cards the workers will be given food
and shelter by the committee, which
will also undertake to introduce
them to work in factories in Shang-
hai or the interior. Registration
will be carried out in several
periods. It is planned that during
the first period only 10,000 workers
will be registered. Those workers
who register must be destitute
persons.
According to Mr. Chu Hsueh-
fang, chairman of the Shanghai
General Labour Union, the large-
scale philanthropic work being done
by officials and union leaders in-
dicates well that the Chinese people
are determined to put up a pro-
longed resistance against the Japan-
ese. Other leaders who are on or
supporting the committee are Messrs.
Tao Peh-chuan, Tung Hsing-pei,
Pang Kung-chan, Du Yueh-sen,
Wang Hsiao-lai and Lu Ching-shih.

Can Pull Ricshas
Jobless workers can pull ricshas

《字林西报》 - 1937年9月26日。
25685

协助上海失业者的宏大计划
成立委员会以照顾数千名失业工人；许多人即将登记；人力车行的想法

中国官员和上海市总工会领导人组织了“上海失业工人救济委员会”，旨在为因战事而失业的近40万名工人实施有效的救济措施。关心劳工问题的人士正认真关注此事，并正在设立10个登记站，以便对贫困工人的状况进行统计研究。

《字林西报》代表采访了几位上海市总工会领导人，他们对这一问题表现出极大兴趣，并表示认为这符合他们救济工人的政策，因为大多数男性难民都是工人。战前上海有30万名工会工人，以及大致相同数量的非工会工人。约20万名工人已离开上海返回原籍。

虽然上海许多失业工人仍留在难民收容所，但大多数人住在亲戚朋友家中，过着勉强糊口的生活。少数有积蓄的人住在小旅馆里。得益于市民领袖和官员的努力，这些工人未制造任何麻烦。约10万名此前在杨树浦地区日本棉纺厂工作的工人正受到特别照顾，因为当地中国当局已多次声明将特别关注熟练工人。

系统性的救济计划
在实施任何系统性救济计划之前，委员会决定首先对工人进行登记，同时解决资金问题。关于后者，据悉如果本地慈善家筹集的资金证明不足，可能会向政府请愿拨款。关于设立登记办事处，将从法租界和公共租界当局获得许可，因为大多数工人居住在这些区域。

登记时，所有工人必须出示各自工会的徽章或书面证明。获得登记卡后，工人将由委员会提供食物和住所，委员会还将负责介绍他们到上海或内地的工厂工作。登记将分几期进行。计划在第一期内仅登记10,000名工人。登记的工人必须是贫困人员。

据上海市总工会主席朱学芳（音译，应为朱学范）先生称，官员和工会领导人正在进行的大规模慈善工作充分表明，中国人民决心对日本进行持久抵抗。其他在委员会任职或支持委员会的领导人有陶百川、董星北（音译）、潘公展、杜月笙、王晓籁和陆京士。

可拉人力车
失业工人可以从位于渡轮路附近海丰路的普恩人力车公司以降低的租金租赁人力车。据《晶报》报道，该车行经理已向上海公共租界工部局请愿，免除难民车夫的登记费。据报道，工部局已接受该请愿。

More than 500,000 people have left
Shanghai since the outbreak of Sino-
Japanese hostilities on August 13, ac-

MEASURES FOR RELIEF OF UNEMPLOYED WORKERS

Since the outbreak of the local Sino-
Japanese hostilities, the number of unemployed workers
has risen to upwards of several tens of thousands.
In view of the fact that the livelihood of
these workers is at stake and that there should be no
further delay in devising ways and means for their relief,
the Shanghai Western District Citizens' Federation is
proposing in the interests of these unemployed the
establishment of temporary factories, the expenditure on
which is to be borne by the authorities concerned with
the assistance of various local public organizations,
and is appealing to local circles for support of its
proposal.

The local Tangpu and the Shanghai City
Government are jointly organizing a "Shanghai Municipality
Unemployed Workers Relief Committee." They will
establish first 5 to 10 registration offices in the
Western parts of Shanghai in the International Settlement
and the French Concession to deal with the registration
of unemployed workers. This being done, the registered
workers will either be given work or relief according
to their capacity.

《国民日报》及其他本地报纸

救济失业工人的措施

自本地中日敌对行动爆发以来，失业工人人数已上升至数万人以上。鉴于这些工人的生计岌岌可危，且制定救济他们的办法刻不容缓，上海西区市民联合会为了这些失业者的利益，提议建立临时工厂，费用由有关当局承担，并得到各地方公共团体的协助，同时呼吁本地各界支持其提议。

本地汤浦（音译）和上海市政府正在联合组织“上海市失业工人救济委员会”。他们将在国际租界和法租界的上海西部地区首先设立5至10个登记处，以处理失业工人的登记工作。完成登记后，将根据登记工人的能力为其安排工作或提供救济。

EXTRACT FROM INTELLIGENCE REPORT DATED JANUARY 29, 1938

Anniversary of January 28 Incident -
Posting of Handbills.

"In connection with the anniversary of the January
28 Incident, the following handbills in addition to those
mentioned in the Intelligence Report dated 28/1/38, were
found posted on walls of houses on Peking Road near Yu Ya
Ching Road and Avenue Joffre near Rue du Consulat.

(1) Handbill entitled "A letter to our Brethren on the
occasion of the 6th anniversary of the January 28
Incident." (mimeographed)

(2) Handbill urging the people to rise and resist
foreign aggression. (mimeographed)

Those handbills have no marks of identification.

In addition to the above propaganda matter, the
following pamphlets came into possession of the Municipal
Police on January 28 :-

(1) Weekly entitled "Unity" (團結), issue No. 7,
dated January 18, 1938. It contains articles
dealing with non-cooperation, the new schemes
of the Japanese and the education of refugees,
and is published by a printing establishment in
Ningpo.

(2) Handbill entitled "General principles governing
the conducting of propaganda on the 6th anniversary
of the January 28 Incident. (mimeographed)

(3) Handbill bearing national salvation slogans for
new year scrolls, published by the "Shanghai
Ya Kee Bookstore." (mimeographed)

Special Branch
January 27, 1938.

Anniversary of the January 28th Incident and the Lunar New
Year Holidays - proposed National Salvation Propaganda Movements

According to information obtained from various sources,
local national salvation elements are planning to conduct a
propaganda campaign between January 28 and February 4 in
connection with the anniversary of the January 28 Incident
(Sino-Japanese Hostilities in 1932) and the lunar New Year
Festival. The programme of the campaign has been ascertained
to consist of the following :-

(1) Hoisting of national flags at half mast on January 28 in
memory of the officers and men killed during the hostilities.
In this connection, members of local national salvation
bodies will approach their relatives and friends as well
as shop owners and householders whenever possible.

(2) All citizens to observe a three minute silence at 11 a.m.
January 28.

(3) Holding of memorial meetings at different places by small
groups.

(4) Publishing of articles bearing on the anniversary in
magazines, dailies and other periodicals.

(5) Comforting and organizing refugees for the purpose of

Subject... The Shanghai Vocational Circles National Salvation Association -

Made by... D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C Garsia Dd

The Shanghai Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association issued in the evening of January 26 a mimeographed
notice to its members in connection with the anniversary of
January 28th incident. A translation of this circular,
a copy of which is attached herewith, reads as follows:-

"Urgent Notice issued by the Shanghai various
public bodies in connection with the commemoration
of the 6th anniversary of 'January 28th'"

The 28th of this month is the 6th anniversary of
the glorious "January 28." The people's various
public bodies in Shanghai have decided to commemorate
the sacrifice of martyrs in the following ways:-
(1) Hoisting of national flags at half mast on
January 28 by shops and residences in memory of
martyrs killed in resisting Japan.
(2) All citizens to observe a three minute silence
at 11 a.m. January 28 in honour of these martyrs.
(Re-copying of this circular for distribution
is encouraged.)

TRANSLATION

General principles of work on the January 28th Anniversary
(From the 27th of the 12 moon of the lunar calendar -
28-1-38 to the 5th of the 1st moon, - 4-2-38.)

The January 28th Incident is one of the heroic
struggles of the Chinese people against the Japanese
imperialists. It shows the people the way to live, refutes
the theory that "military might alone is almighty," and
explains how cooperation between the people and the military
will produce great strength. It also serves to stir up
intense anti-Jap-nese sentiment among the masses. Therefore,
January 28th is a day of great significance and deserves
prominence in Chinese history. This day should be par-
ticularly vivid in the mind of the Shanghai citizens.

As this incident is closely related with Shanghai
citizens, we should commemorate this anniversary to the
utmost of our ability so that during this period of nation-
wide resistance against Japan, the residents of Shanghai will
assist to an even greater extent in the National Salvation
Movement.

The repercussions of the January 28th incident upon
the Shanghai citizens provide us with facilities in the
execution of our duty. Through an extensive anti-enemy
propaganda movement, we will proceed with the organization
of the masses, and through various activities relating
to the livelihood of the people such as relief for the
unemployed and preservation of employment, etc., we will
set the people on the move and have them organised.
Simultaneously we will endeavour to persuade the Chinese
capitalists, political and Kuomintang officers still in Shang-
hai, societies, associations, and trade associations to
take action in concert.

The week from the 27th of the 12th moon (28.1.38)
to the 5th of the 1st moon (4.2.38) will be our propaganda
week in connection with the anniversary of the January

一·二八周年纪念工作总原则
（自农历十二月二十七日——1938年1月28日至正月初五——1938年2月4日。）

一·二八事变是中国人民反抗日本帝国主义的英勇斗争之一。它向人民指明了生存之道，驳斥了“唯武力万能”论，并阐释了军民合作将产生巨大力量。它还有助于在民众中激起强烈的反日情绪。因此，一·二八是一个具有重大意义的日子，在中国历史上值得大书特书。这一天应在上海市民心中留下尤为生动的印象。

鉴于此事变与上海市民息息相关，我们应竭尽全力纪念这一周年，以便在全国抗日期间，上海居民能更大程度地协助救亡运动。

一·二八事变在上海市民中引起的反响，为我们执行任务提供了便利。通过广泛的反敌宣传运动，我们将推进民众的组织工作，并通过各种与民生相关的活动，如失业救济和维持就业等，动员民众并将其组织起来。同时，我们将努力说服仍留在上海的华人资本家、政界及国民党官员、社团、协会和同业公会采取一致行动。

从农历十二月二十七日（1938年1月28日）至正月初五（1938年2月4日）的这一周，将是我们就一·二八

Subject Yen Pao Hang(閻寶航), alleged to be an influential member of the Chinese Communist Party and the Various Circles' National Salvation Association.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by C. Crawford D I

With reference to that part of the French Police daily report dated 20.1.38 on one Yen Pao Hang who is alleged to be an influential member of the Chinese Communist Party and reported to have been sent to Shanghai to organise a section of the Party, I have to state that this report lacks confirmation.

Enquiries elicit that Yen Pao Hang is Chief of Second Section of the "National Committee to Support the Mobile Units in War Areas"(全國各戰區游擊隊後援會), undertaking the training of executive elements, which was recently organised at Hankow by Messrs Sung Chuin Sz(沈鈞儒), Doo Zoong Yuen(杜重遠) and other members of the local National Salvation Movement.

It is to be noted that Mr. Doo Zoong Yuen who played a prominent part in the lese majeste was arrested by the Municipal Police in July, 1935, while Sung Chuin Sz, one of the seven leaders in the campaign of national liberation, was released on August 1, 1937.

A constant watch on the activities of the "Various Circles' National Salvation Association" has been maintained by the staff of S.1., but no information has so far been obtained regarding any meeting being held at the Great Eastern Hotel, Kin Wo Ka, off Nanking Road. Enquiries from other channels have also failed to trace the presence of a communist agent named Liu whose activities are connected with the local national salvation movement.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL SPECIAL BRANCH 25 JAN 1938）

January 27, 1938.

Anniversary of the January 28th Incident and the Lunar New
Year Holidays - proposed National Salvation Propaganda Movements

According to information obtained from various sources,
local national salvation elements are planning to conduct a
propaganda campaign between January 28 and February 4 in
connection with the anniversary of the January 28 Incident
(Sino-Japanese Hostilities in 1932) and the lunar New Year
Festival. The programme of the campaign has been ascertained
to consist of the following :-

(1) Hoisting of national flags at half mast on January 28 in
memory of the officers and men killed during the hostilities.
In this connection, members of local national salvation
bodies will approach their relatives and friends as well
as shop owners and householders whenever possible.

(2) All citizens to observe a three minute silence at 11 a.m.
January 28.

(3) Holding of memorial meetings at different places by small
groups.

(4) Publishing of articles bearing on the anniversary in
magazines, dailies and other periodicals.

(5) Comforting and organizing refugees for the purpose of
utilizing them for propaganda activities.

(6) Printing and writing of new year scrolls of a national
salvation character for pasting up on doors of residences
and shops.

(7) Conducting of national salvation propaganda among relatives
and friends during visits for offering new year greetings.
In this connection, members of local national salvation
bodies will be organized into so-called "New Year Visiting
Parties."

1938年1月27日。

一·二八事变周年及农历新年假期——拟议的救亡宣传运动

根据从各方获得的情报，本地救亡分子计划于1月28日至2月4日期间，结合一·二八事变（1932年中日战事）周年及农历新年节日，开展宣传运动。经查实，该运动的方案包括以下内容：

(1) 1月28日降半旗，以悼念在战事中阵亡的官兵。为此，本地救亡团体的成员将在可能的情况下接触其亲友以及店主和住户。

(2) 所有市民于1月28日上午11时默哀三分钟。

(3) 在各处由小组举行追悼会。

(4) 在杂志、日报和其他期刊上发表有关周年纪念的文章。

(5) 慰问并组织难民，以便利用他们进行宣传活动中。

(6) 印刷和书写具有救亡性质的春联，张贴在住宅和商店的门上。

(7) 在拜年走访亲友期间进行救亡宣传。为此，本地救亡团体的成员将被组织成所谓的“新年拜年团”。

Subject Distribution of handbill on Nanking and Peking Roads by a
Chinese boy on January 1.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by C. Crawford

（批：How are obtained or copies before ?）
（印：A. MUNRO / - 4 JAN 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：S.B / O.R. / 571 / G.D. & Sth / C.S / 8/1）

At about 9.30 a.m. January 1, 1938, copies of a handbill
of a national salvation nature couched in the following
terms were distributed to shop assistants on Peking and
Nanking Roads by a Chinese boy of about 14 years of age:-

"Dear brothers:-

With the advent of the New Year of 1938, upon
looking back over the year 1937, when the war of
resistance for the emancipation of the Chinese race
broke out, we can feel proud that never before in our
history can we find such a great war of resistance.

Although we have been unsuccessful from a military
point of view, yet we are convinced that the final
victory must be ours, as we can tell by the revolutionary
history of Russia, when workers, armed with not an
inch of iron overpowered the "Czar." The revolution--
aries of China, in 1911, who were barehanded, succeeded
in overthrowing the Tsing Dynasty. Even in the
Spanish Civil War, the government forces have been
ever victorious.

All events prove to us that right surpasses might,
and indicates that force is not almighty.

Nevertheless, final victory can only be attained
through competition and every one of us should stand
firm by contributing what he possesses to the nation
and the race, and swear never to become slaves.

Should you name the year 1937 as the year of
resistance, then the year 1938 will undoubtedly be
the year of victory.

（批：S.B / O.R. / 571 / G.D. & Sth / C.S / 8/1）

1938年1月1日上午9时30分左右，一名约14岁的中国男孩在北京路和南京路向店员分发了具有救国性质的传单副本，内容如下：-

“亲爱的兄弟们：-

随着1938年新年的到来，回顾爆发中华民族解放抗战的1937年，我们可以自豪地说，在我们历史上从未有过如此伟大的抗战。

虽然从军事角度来看我们尚未成功，但我们坚信最终胜利必将属于我们，正如我们可以从俄国的革命历史中得知，手无寸铁的工人推翻了‘沙皇’。1911年赤手空拳的中国革命者成功推翻了清朝。即使在西班牙内战中，政府军也屡获胜利。

所有事件都向我们证明，正义胜过强权，并表明武力并非万能。

然而，只有通过竞争才能取得最终胜利，我们每个人都应坚定立场，将自己拥有的一切贡献给国家和民族，并宣誓绝不成为奴隶。

如果将1937年称为抗战之年，那么1938年无疑将是胜利之年。

On receipt of information on December 28 that New
Year Greeting cards were being printed for national salvation
elements, C.D.S. 156 discovered when making enquiries through
printing establishments that the Zuan Hwa Company, Lane 127,
House 7 Fokien Road, had a large number on sale.

Acting on the instructions of D.C. (Special Branch),
C.D.S. 156 and the undersigned visited the Zuan Hwa Card-making
Company, Lane 127, 7 Fokien Road, at 2.45 p.m. December 30,
1937, and interviewed Mr. Ling Chien-hang (林建衡), a staff
employee of the company, who in the absence of the owner,
was in charge of the firm. He produced on request all
accounts in respect of sales of greeting cards (known as
Sample No.60), similar to the attached specimen, during the
past two months. Mr. Ling stated that towards the end of
November, salesmen of the firm distributed sample sets of

purchase from the Zuan Hwa Card-making Company. Mr. Ling
stated that there was no account book recording these
transactions as they had all been in the nature of cash sales,
in respect of which the company did not make a practice of
recording the buyers' particulars. The only records kept
by the firm regarding cash sales of the cards in question are

Copies of a handbill entitled "Letter to countrymen on

which is of an anti-Japanese nature, were dropped from the
roof garden of the Sun Sun Company, Nanking Road, on the

1937. A summarized translation of this handbill is given
hereunder :-
"Dear Brothers:
New Year has come. It is the first day of the 27th
year of the Republic of China but we should not forget,
it is also the 142nd day since the war of resistance
was commenced on August 13, 1937.
Against the Japanese large scale aggression, with
the intent to enslave us, and because of the unwillingness
of the Chinese people to surrender, we have bravely
waged this war for the defence of the race, and in which
we are now seeking the true happiness of the New Year.
We fight for that ever rising generation which should
not be slaves. We are ready to sacrifice everything.
Since the withdrawal of Chinese troops on November
12, 1937, Shanghai appears to have fallen into the
hands of the Japanese "robbers" who immediately held
demonstrations on Nanking Road, and arrested persons
without notice to the authorities concerned; all such
action tends to show that they treat us as they would
treat slaves. However, we are confident that none of
our race are willing to become slaves or traitors.
Moreover, they will struggle further and are willing to

pages.en:
TRANSLATION

A joint letter to people in various circles from the
Shanghai Citizens' National Salvation League, various
Shop Employees' National Salvation Association, and
the Various Factory Employees' National Salvation Asso-
ciation in commemoration of the New Year.

"In spite of the special circumstances prevailing
in Shanghai and which followed the withdrawal of the
Chinese troops, we should not become traitors, but
continue to show the spirit of the Chinese race.
Consequently, on the forthcoming New Year's Day, shops
and residences throughout this city ought to hoist
the "Chinese National Flag" and swear not to disgrace
the nation; to extend the national salvation propaganda
movement; not to buy enemy goods; and not to co-operate
with the enemy. We should support our Government and
drive out the Japanese robbers. In commemoration of
the New Year, we should curtail expenses, and contribute
the money thus saved for the relief of wounded soldiers,
refugees and the families of those who have made
sacrifice for the nation. We should shout the following
slogans:-

1) To commemorate the New Year, we should continue the
war of resistance to the bitter end, drive away the
Japanese robbers and annihilate all traitors and
running dogs.

2) To commemorate the New Year, we should co-operate
with Great Britain, U.S.A., France and U.S.S.R.
in dealing with Japan.

3) To commemorate the New Year, we should support
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and other military
commanders and recover the lost territory.

4) To commemorate the New Year, we should determine
not to buy and sell "enemy" goods and should not
support the enemy in any.

5) Down with Japanese Imperialism. Long live the
emancipation of the Republic of China!"

Envelops:
Commemorate the New Year!
Don't forget the national crisis!
pages.zh:
译文

上海市民救国大同盟、各业店员救国协会及各工厂职工救国会纪念新年致各界人士联合信。

“尽管上海局势特殊，且在中国军队撤退之后，我们不应成为汉奸，而应继续展现中华民族的精神。因此，在即将到来的元旦，本市各商店和住户应当悬挂‘中国国旗’，宣誓不辱国格；扩大救国宣传运动；不买敌货；不与敌人合作。我们应支持政府，驱逐日本强盗。为纪念新年，我们应缩减开支，并将节省下来的钱款捐赠给伤兵、难民以及为国牺牲者的家属。我们应高呼以下口号：

1) 纪念新年，我们要坚持抗战到底，赶走日本强盗，消灭所有汉奸和走狗。

2) 纪念新年，我们要联合英国、美国、法国和苏联共同对付日本。

3) 纪念新年，我们要支持蒋介石委员长及其他军事指挥官，收复失地。

4) 纪念新年，我们要决心不买卖‘敌’货，并在任何方面不支持敌人。

5) 打倒日本帝国主义。中华民国解放万岁！”

信封：
纪念新年！
勿忘国难！
